fab_ac_landing.0001.desc.text:
A hundred years ago, the world called my forefather Aenar a fool. Lord Aenar Targaryen, a lesser dragonlord of mighty Valyria, who sold his estates and moved his whole house - wives, children, dragons and all - to a bleak smoking rock at the western edge of the world, on no better counsel than the dreams of his daughter. Twelve years later, the Fourteen Flames tore Valyria apart in a single day and night, and the greatest civilization the world has known drowned in fire and salt water. Daenys the Dreamer had seen truly. Of all the dragonlords of the Freehold, only we endured. We are the last.

For a hundred years since - the century the world remembers as one long letting of blood - the daughters of Valyria have torn at each other over the corpse of their mother. I have had my taste of those wars: when Pentos and Tyrosh sought the aid of the young Lord of Dragonstone against the grasping Volantenes, I flew Balerion east, burned a war fleet to the waterline, and came home. The lords magister feasted me and begged me to stay. I would not. There is nothing in the east but old ashes quarreling over older ashes.

#bold It is the west that has always called to me. It called to Aenar across a hundred years - and now, at last, I understand why.#!

fab_ac_landing.0002.desc.text:
Years ago I commanded the carpenters of Dragonstone to carve me a table. They thought their lord mad by the time it was done - fifty feet long, five-and-twenty wide at its broadest, hewn from a single mighty block and painted, every inch, in the likeness of Westeros. Every river and bay, every mountain range and ruined ringfort, every castle and town and holdfast from Oldtown to the Wall, set down exactly - my painters worked from the charts of a hundred traders and the accounts of a thousand travelers.

One thing, and one thing only, I forbade them to paint: borders. Wander the table's length and you will find no line where the stormlands end and the Reach begins, no seam dividing the kingdoms the Andals carved out of one another. From the raised seat at Dragonstone's place - where I sit now, with the brazier crackling behind me and my sisters at either hand - a man sees the truth those lines were drawn to hide.

#bold It was never seven kingdoms. It is one land. It wants only one king.#!

fab_ac_landing.0003.desc.text:
Harren the Black's monstrous castle by the Gods Eye nears completion at last, and forty years of the riverlands' misery with it. A man who has spent a lifetime building the greatest fortress in the world does not intend to sit quietly in it; all Westeros whispers that Harren looks about for new conquests - and none whisper more anxiously than his neighbor the Storm King.

So Argilac Durrandon, grown old and, for the first time in his proud life, afraid, sent his offer across the water: an alliance against Harren, sealed with the hand of his daughter Argella - and a dowry of lands along the Blackwater to stand as a buffer between stag and kraken. Lands, be it noted, that Harren holds and Argilac does not; the old man offered me another king's ground. I declined the lady with courtesy - the blood of the dragon does not want for wives; I have two, my sisters, wed as Valyria always wed. In her place I offered the hand of Orys Baratheon, my dearest friend and, the whispers say, my brother - and asked lands within Argilac's actual gift as the dowry.

His answer arrived today, in a box. The hands of my envoy, salted like pork. And a message: #italic 'These are the only hands you shall receive.'#!

#bold The Arrogant, they call him. He has earned the name today - and he will learn the price of it.#!

fab_ac_landing.0003.option1.text: Argilac will lose more than hands for this.

fab_ac_landing.0004.desc.text:
The box sits open on the Painted Table. My envoy will live, the maester says. He will never hold a sword again.

I have been patient. For years the kings of Westeros have sent their ravens to Dragonstone - seeking my dragons for their wars, my fleet for their quarrels, my house for their daughters - as though the blood of the dragon were a sellsword company to be hired, flattered, and dismissed. Argilac's insult is only the last and grossest of a hundred. They see a petty lord on a barren rock. They have forgotten what came out of Valyria and what the Doom could not kill.

I am done with the courtesies of petty lords and false kings. Of all the houses of Old Valyria, only mine came through the Doom with its dragons, and no one else under the sun has any. They have taken my patience for weakness - every one of them.

#bold No longer. Westeros will be mine.#!

fab_ac_landing.0004.option1.text: #S We answer with fire and blood. #!

fab_ac_landing.0005.desc.text:
I have called my banners and taken counsel - with my sisters, with Orys, with the lords of the narrow sea. The Velaryons and Celtigars, kin to my house and Valyrian as we are, were mine before I finished speaking; Lord Bar Emmon of Sharp Point and Lord Massey of Stonedance knelt the same hour. Small lords, the kings of Westeros would say. The first lords of a new realm, say I.

Then I sent the ravens - one to every king and great lord in Westeros, each bearing the same words. That from this day there is one king in Westeros. That those who bend the knee to Aegon of House Targaryen shall keep their lands and titles, diminished in nothing but their crowns. And that those who take up arms against him shall be thrown down, humbled, and destroyed.

The maesters will note that I addressed no kingdoms, acknowledged no borders, treated the seven crowns as seven vanities. That was no oversight. I have stood at the Painted Table; I know what Westeros is, even if Westeros does not yet know it itself.

#bold Every hall from Sunspear to Winterfell will read it: the dragon does not ask twice.#!

fab_ac_landing.0005.option1.text: There is only one king in Westeros.

fab_ac_landing.0006.text: The Toad and the Hawk Reply

fab_ac_landing.0006.desc.text:
The ravens return, and two answers among them want remembering.

From Sunspear writes Meria Martell, Princess of Dorne - eighty years old, blind, immense, and cunning as ever her enemies feared: the Yellow Toad offers me alliance against Argilac the Storm King. Alliance. She will fight beside me, share the spoils with me - and yield me nothing. From the Eyrie writes Sharra Arryn, regent of the Vale for her boy Ronnel, with a subtler snare: an alliance sealed with her own hand in marriage - she sends a portrait, and word that she was once called the Flower of the Mountain - provided only that I name her son my heir. She covets the east bank of the Green Fork, and would have my dragons win it from Harren for her.

I have refused them both, the toad and the hawk alike, and in the same words: I did not send my ravens seeking allies. I sent them seeking subjects. There is no place in what is coming for kings and queens who would treat with me as equals - for I have no equals in Westeros.

#bold They may keep their crowns a little longer. I shall come for them in due course - and I will come beneath a banner all the world shall learn.#!

fab_ac_landing.0007.t.text: The Three Heads of the Dragon

fab_ac_landing.0007.desc.text:
The dragonlords of old Valyria kept no banners. The Freehold flew no sigils to war; a dragon overhead was herald enough. But I do not mean to rule Valyria - I mean to rule Westeros, and Westeros reads the world through its banners: direwolf and kraken, lion and stag, falcon and sun-and-spear.

So let them have one to remember. Visenya has overseen the work herself: a field black as Balerion's wings, and upon it a dragon red as flame, #bold three-headed#! - one head for me, one for each of my sister-queens, for it is the three of us together who will do this thing. When the maesters of far-off ages write of how the Seven Kingdoms became one, this is the banner that will fly over every page.

#bold Fire and blood, on black and red. It will be sewn on every sail. #!

fab_ac_landing.0007.a.text: One head for each of us. Raise it over Dragonstone.

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.harren.text:
A raven has crossed the Gods Eye bearing Aegon Targaryen's demand: every king in Westeros is to surrender his crown and name the Lord of Dragonstone his sovereign. He offers peace to those who kneel and fire to those who refuse.

The boy has three dragons, but I have Harrenhal—the greatest fortress ever raised, with walls no army can breach and towers no flame can threaten. Aegon may come and dash himself against the monument I spent forty years building.

#bold Stone does not burn, and Harren the Black does not kneel.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.torrhen.text:
A raven from Dragonstone has reached Winterfell. Aegon Targaryen styles himself king of all Westeros and commands every crowned head to lay down his crown. Those who submit may keep their lands; those who resist are promised fire and blood.

The North has followed Stark kings since the Long Night. No southern conqueror has ever crossed the Neck and ruled us, yet no southern conqueror ever came astride Balerion, with Vhagar and Meraxes at either wing. Soon I must call the banners and decide what an ancient crown is worth in northern lives.

#bold The North remembers its kings. The dragon will learn that.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.meria.text:
Aegon Targaryen's raven has flown as far as Sunspear. The dragonlord commands me to yield my crown, bend my knee, and acknowledge him as king of all Westeros. Submission will bring peace, he says; refusal will bring dragonfire.

The other kings may count their walls and armies. Dorne has survived greater powers by offering neither battle nor surrender, only empty roads, poisoned wells, and sands that swallow invaders whole. Dragons may burn what they can find. We shall give them precious little to find.

#bold Unbowed, Unbent, Unbroken. That is my answer.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.loren.text:
Aegon Targaryen has sent his terms to Casterly Rock. He claims all Westeros as one realm beneath one king and bids me exchange the crown of the Rock for his peace. If I refuse, the raven warns, he will answer with Balerion, Vhagar, and Meraxes.

The Westerlands are rich enough to arm hosts beyond counting, and Mern Gardener commands the greatest strength in the Reach. Together our banners could cover the earth from horizon to horizon. Yet the Targaryens mean to fight from the sky. Gold has purchased every weapon known to men; now it must purchase an answer to dragons.

#bold The lion has not ruled the Rock for six thousand years merely to become a dragon's cat.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.mern.text:
The Lord of Dragonstone has sent a raven to Highgarden declaring himself king of all Westeros. Aegon Targaryen offers mercy if I surrender the green crown and threatens fire if I do not. Three dragons, he believes, outweigh the oldest dynasty and greatest host in the realm.

Every field of the Reach can yield another company of spears. Loren Lannister shares my danger, and the might of Highgarden joined to the gold of Casterly Rock will make an army such as Westeros has never seen. The dragonlord has wings, but he must still take and hold a continent.

#bold House Gardener has flourished since the dawn of kings. I will not be its last bloom.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.argilac.text:
Another message has come from the boy on Dragonstone. After answering my daughter's hand with the offer of his bastard brother, Aegon Targaryen now demands my crown as well. He names himself king of all Westeros and promises fire to every ruler who will not kneel.

I have broken Dornish hosts, slain kings, and defended these stormlands since before Aegon first sat a saddle. His beasts are terrible, but storms have cast down prouder things than dragons, and Storm's End was raised to defy the fury of the gods themselves.

#bold He knows where to find me. The last Storm King still has one war left in him.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.ronnel.text:
A raven has come from the dragonlord. Mother read it twice and then shut herself in council with the lords of the Vale. Aegon Targaryen says all Westeros is one kingdom now, and every king must give him his crown or face his three dragons.

They say no army can pass the Bloody Gate and no castle is safer than the Eyrie. But dragons do not climb roads. Balerion is large enough to swallow a horse, Vhagar is nearly as fierce, and Meraxes has golden eyes. Everyone looks afraid when they think I am not watching.

#bold I am King of Mountain and Vale. Surely even a dragon must ask before taking my crown.#!

fab_ac_landing.0008.desc.text: Ravens now carry Aegon Targaryen's proclamation to every court in Westeros: the Lord of Dragonstone claims the whole continent and names himself its king. Many laugh at the presumption, but wiser rulers remember the doom that dragons once brought to armies and cities. \n \nAegon does not come alone. Visenya rides Vhagar, Rhaenys rides Meraxes, and Balerion the Black Dread answers to Aegon himself. Soon the Seven Kingdoms will learn whether ancient crowns can withstand the last power of Valyria.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option1.text: Our ancient crowns will not yield so easily.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.harren.text: What is dead may never die—and Harrenhal shall never fall.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.torrhen.text: Winter is coming, even for dragons.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.loren.text: The lion will answer with claws.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.mern.text: The Green Hand shall not wither before dragonfire.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.argilac.text: Ours is the Fury. Come, dragon.

fab_ac_landing.0008.option.ronnel.text: As High as Honor—higher even than dragons.

fab_ac_landing.0009.desc.text:
Forty years. Forty years of the rivers' timber and the rivers' gold and the rivers' backs bent to my quarries, and today the masons set the last stone of Harrenhal. Five towers to shame the mountains, walls no engine built by man could trouble, halls that could stable armies. No castle in all the world has ever matched it. None ever will.

And on this same day, a raven from Dragonstone. The Valyrian salt-lordling bids me kneel — me, whose line has worn crowns since before his precious freehold was ash — or be destroyed.

The gods below have a sense of humour after all. He may come and look upon what I have built. Valyria has been dead for a hundred years. I will not kneel to what is left of it, and if he brings it to my gates, he will find them shut.

fab_ac_landing.0009.option1.text: Come, dragon, and learn what stone means.

fab_ac_landing.0010.desc.text:
The dragonlord's envoy stood beneath Durran Godsgrief's roof and delivered his master's answer as though it were some great courtesy. I had offered Aegon Targaryen my daughter's hand and lands that Harren Hoare has no right to hold, enough to make common cause between two kings against a common enemy. The heathen refused Argella for himself. Instead he offered me Orys, his baseborn half-brother, and presumed to name still more lands besides.

There are insults a king may swallow for the good of his realm. This was not one of them.

The envoy leaves Storm's End with Aegon's answer returned to him in a cedar box. His hands are inside it. If Orys Waters desires something of mine badly enough to reach for it, he may begin with those.

Aegon may sit upon his smoking rock with his sister-wives and mistake restraint for weakness if it pleases him. The Storm Kings were fighting ironmen, Dornishmen, and worse before Valyria was ash, and I have not survived this long by fearing every foreign lord with a strange name and a monstrous beast beneath him. If the dragon wants war, by the Seven, he shall learn why my house has kept these lands for a thousand years.

#bold The storm has given its answer. Dragonstone may make what it will of it.#!

fab_ac_landing.0011.desc.text:
Our ships are drawn up where the Blackwater Rush meets the bay, and I chose the place with care: the land is claimed by both Argilac the Arrogant and Harren the Black, which is to say defended by neither. The two of them can quarrel over whose problem I am. Three hills rise north of the river: a high hill, a wooded hill away to the north, and a lower one nearer the water. No one has yet troubled to give them names. That will change.

On the high hill my men are already raising a fort of earth and timber, while my sisters attend to our first task - the lords of the shore. Rhaenys is flying Meraxes to Rosby, and Visenya is taking Vhagar to Stokeworth. Both lords will kneel to their king, or face dragonflame.

#bold A fort of logs today; a city, one day. The maesters may argue over its name. #!

fab_ac_landing.0012.desc.text:
The Targaryen has put ashore at the mouth of the Blackwater and thrown up a ditch and a timber palisade on the high hill. My land, as it happens — though the quarrelsome little lords of that shore forget whose peace they keep whenever it suits them.

He hopes to sting me into rushing down to meet him, no doubt. Why would I? Every day he sits in his mud fort, my walls stand just as high. He can bleed himself on Darklyn and Mooton and the Storm King's pride first.

When he has worn his little host to rags, he may come and break what remains of it against Harrenhal.

fab_ac_landing.0012.option1.text: The shore lords can blunt him first.

fab_ac_landing.0013.desc.text:
Word from the Blackwater: the Targaryen has landed at the river's mouth, on the three hills where the fisherfolk beach their boats. A few thousand men, some ships, and the three beasts of Dragonstone.

The mouth of the Blackwater is Harren's land — let the old squid dig him out, or lose the rivers trying. Both would suit me. Whichever of them bleeds first, the Stormlands watch, and arm, and wait.

Storms have broken on these lands since Durran defied the gods themselves. A lizard with wings does not frighten me.

fab_ac_landing.0013.option1.text: The dragon and the squid can tear at each other.

fab_ac_landing.0014.desc.text:
My sisters return before the week is out, and behind them come the first oaths.

Rhaenys found Rosby's gates open. The old lord watched Meraxes circle his towers once, twice, and had his banners struck before she finished the third pass; he met her in his own yard, knelt on the cobbles, and offered bread, salt, and homage without a single bolt loosed. His seat lies a short ride from our three hills, his lands run with the chalk road toward Duskendale, and his house is old enough to remember when kings were smaller things. He strikes me as a man who means to survive whatever comes next. I can use such men.

Stokeworth cost a little more. Visenya came down over their keep, and their crossbowmen - braver than their lord, or perhaps only worse informed - loosed a volley at her. Vhagar answered with a single breath. The roofs of the keep took flame, and the same crossbowmen spent the evening hauling water while their lord waved a peace banner from the walls. Rich farms, full granaries, and a house that will spend the next hundred years insisting it was faithful from the first. The scorched rafters will only make the tale better.

Two oaths, then, and the whole shore watching: Hayford, Rook's Rest, the Antlers, a dozen petty lords weighing dragons against the old crowns. Only from Duskendale and Maidenpool, where the Darklyns and the Mootons sit, has there come no word at all.

#bold The silence to the north has a sound I know. It is the sound of swords being counted.#!

fab_ac_landing.0014.option1.text: Bread and salt for the faithful.

fab_ac_landing.0015.desc.text:
The fort is finished - or finished enough for a king to sleep in it.

We raised it on the tallest of the three hills, where I first planted the banner: a ring of raw logs and packed earth, a timber hall roofed in thatch and hides, stables, a smithy, a longhouse for the men. There is not a block of dressed stone in the whole of it. Visenya walked the wall once and called it a woodpile waiting for a torch. She is not wrong. It will serve.

From its gate I can see everything I came for: the bay, the river mouth, and the fishing village below swelling day by day into a town of tents and mud lanes - traders, masons, camp followers, septons, every kind of man who can smell a court being born. The smallfolk have already named the hills. This one is Aegon's High Hill now; the wooded one to the north is Rhaenys's, and the one by the water Visenya's. And the town needs no maester to name it. Men simply say they are going to the king's landing.

Balerion suns himself on the slope below the wall, which does more for the fort's defenses than every log in it.

It is well he does. Word comes at dusk that the Darklyns of Duskendale and the Mootons of Maidenpool have called their banners and joined their strength. They mean to come and burn my woodpile.

#bold They are welcome to try. Every king must have a seat, and mine will outgrow the both of theirs.#!

fab_ac_landing.0015.option1.text: This will do. For a start.

fab_ac_landing.0016.desc.text:
My outriders have counted them on the road out of Duskendale: three thousand men, with carts, camp followers and levies strung out behind. They march openly and they march slowly, which tells me they expect a battle at the end of it and not a hunt.

I can put fewer than sixteen hundred in the field, and half of those are narrow sea men who fight better from a deck than a ditch.

Neither lord has ever seen a dragon. Their whole plan rests on that, and they do not know it.

#bold They have until the ditch to think better of this.#!

fab_ac_landing.0016.option1.text: Three thousand men. I have three dragons.

fab_ac_landing.0017.desc.text:
The ditch is dug, the palisade is up, and my sisters do not agree.

Visenya would have us stand behind the timber and make them come to it: men who charge a palisade break on it, she says, and dragons can take them while they are breaking. Rhaenys would rather we rode out and met them on ground I choose, where they will have room to run and nowhere worth running to.

#bold Both counsels end the same way. The difference is only where I stand while it happens.#!

fab_ac_landing.0017.option1.text: We hold the palisade. They can come to us.

fab_ac_landing.0017.option2.text: Ride out. I will choose the ground.

fab_ac_landing.0018.desc.text:
They came on at the palisade in good order, and they were still in good order when the sky opened.

Vhagar and Meraxes came out of the sun on either flank. What had been an army was fire and screaming before a man could finish a prayer, and the ditch we dug caught most of those who ran the wrong way.

Lord Darklyn and Lord Mooton burned with their men. Of the host that marched out of Duskendale, the road will not carry a tenth of it home.

#bold The first army raised against me in Westeros is ash. Every hall between here and the Trident will hear of it within the week.#!

fab_ac_landing.0018.desc.sally.text:
I would not fight my first battle in Westeros from behind a ditch. I rode out and took the ground I wanted, with the road at their backs and nothing at all on their flanks.

Then the sky opened. Vhagar and Meraxes came out of the sun on either side of them, and what had been an army was fire and screaming before a man could finish a prayer. My own line never had to hold longer than a moment.

Lord Darklyn and Lord Mooton burned with their men. Of the host that marched out of Duskendale, the road will not carry a tenth of it home.

#bold The first army raised against me in Westeros is ash, and I stood on the field to watch it burn.#!

fab_ac_landing.0019.desc.text:
They came to the Aegonfort before their dead were buried. Duskendale rode in at first light under a peace banner, Maidenpool followed within the hour, and neither asked for terms.

They knelt in the mud outside a half-built hall, gave up their castles, and asked one thing: their names and their lands. I granted it. Visenya already has men counting what sits in the Duskendale warehouses - it is the busiest port on the narrow sea, and tonight it is mine.

#bold Their fathers would not kneel, so their heirs do. Westeros should see both halves of that.#!

fab_ac_landing.0019.option1.text: Rise. You keep your names and your lands.

fab_ac_landing.0021.desc.text:
Word of our landing ran up the coast faster than our outriders. Lord Darklyn of Duskendale and Lord Mooton of Maidenpool joined their strength - three thousand men, by the count of our scouts - and marched south to drive us back into the sea that brought us. It was the first true test of this conquest, and it lasted less than a morning.

Orys met them with our vanguard and broke their line; Rhaenys came down upon their rear on Meraxes, and what had been a host became a rout. Both lords lie among the slain. Darklyn's son and Mooton's brother knelt to me on the field, amid their own dead, and did homage for their fathers' halls - and they shall keep them. All Westeros will mark it: those who bend the knee will find me open-handed. Those who take up swords against me will find I keep the swords.

For I have ordered the blades of the fallen gathered, every one, and carried up the high hill to the Aegonfort. I have a purpose for them - and it will want many more swords yet before it is done.

#bold The ground about our landing is secure. Westeros has tested us, and been answered.#!

fab_ac_landing.0022.desc.text:
My sisters would wait no longer. A conqueror who names himself king of all Westeros, Visenya said, ought to look the part before the lords he means to rule - and there are lords enough to witness it now, new-sworn and watching to see what manner of man holds their oaths.

So it was done - though no grand affair: a bare handful of lords stood witness in the timber hall, the new-sworn shore lords and my own captains, with the banners of Darklyn and Mooton hung fresh among my own. Before them I knelt to my elder sister, as our forebears knelt in the shadow of the Fourteen Flames. Visenya set upon my brow a circlet of Valyrian steel, studded with great square-cut rubies - no southron bauble of gold and velvet, but steel, dark and keen as the work of Old Valyria. It is the only crown I mean to wear.

Then Rhaenys' voice rang out over the ranks, and the words she gave them shall be the style of every king of my line that follows after:

#bold Aegon, First of His Name, King of All Westeros, and Shield of His People.#!

The little company took up the cry - a few dozen voices where one day there will be thousands - and somewhere above the clouds, the dragons answered louder than any host could.

#bold Seven kingdoms do not yet know they have a king. They will learn.#!

fab_ac_landing.0023.desc.text:
A crown is a weight, and a king who bears every weight alone will break beneath them. The lords about me understood this before I had worn mine a day - suddenly there was no shortage of counsel at the Aegonfort, nor of counsellors hungry to be seen giving it.

There was never a question of whom I would raise first. Orys has been at my side since we were boys in the yard at Dragonstone, matching blunted swords before either of us could grow a beard. The court whispers that he is my brother, base-born of my father's blood; I have never dignified the whisper with an answer, and never once denied it. It was Orys who broke the lords Darklyn and Mooton on the field that won us our landing. Where the fighting is thickest, there he is; where I am weakest, there he is also.

So before the assembled court I bade him kneel, and named him the first Hand of the King - and the realm would do well to mark the words I gave him, for I meant every one:

#bold My shield, my stalwart, my strong right hand.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0001.desc.text:
A crown settles nothing; it only promises. Mine promises all of Westeros, and Westeros is held by kings who mean to keep it. In the hall of the Aegonfort my council bends over the maps, and every finger points a different way.

North sits [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstNameNicknamed], King of the Isles and the Rivers, behind the walls of Harrenhal - the monstrous castle his ironmen wrung out of forty years of riverland blood and toil, finished, the singers say, on the very day I stepped ashore. Five towers like the fingers of a grasping hand, walls too high and thick for any siege ladder ever made. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] thinks [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] stone will keep [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim]. The rivermen who built it groan beneath his yoke, and I am told some of their lords would rise for me - if someone gave them cause.

South waits Argilac the Arrogant, the old Storm King, who cut the hands from my envoy and sent them to me in a box. His pride began this war. He is old, but the strength is not gone from him, and unlike [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] he will not cower behind walls - the Durrandon will come out to meet me in the open field, storm and all. There would be a certain justice in answering him first.

#bold Two kings, two roads. Either way, the wars for Westeros begin in earnest.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0001.option1.text: Set the host upon the road to Harrenhal.

fab_ac_riverlands.0002.desc.text:
The war will not wait on carpenters, so this morning I put the host on its roads.

Mine runs northwest, up the Blackwater to the Gods Eye, with Balerion above it. Visenya sails north with Daemon Velaryon and the fleet, to learn what the Vale will pay to keep its peace. Orys holds the rest under arms on the southern marches, with Rhaenys and Meraxes over him. Argilac would not have him for a good-son; he can have him for an enemy.

#bold Three roads and three dragons. Mine ends at Harrenhal.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0003.desc.text:
They were waiting where the reeds grow tall on the southern shore of the Gods Eye, and they chose their moment well. My column was strung out along the water and the ground gave way under armoured men.

What they had not reckoned on was Balerion already aloft. He came in low over the water, the reeds went up from end to end, and after that it was less a battle than a reckoning.

We hold the field. We also have fewer men than we had this morning, and the maesters will be working until dawn.

#bold This country will cost me blood even where I win. Better to learn it here than at the walls.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0003.option1.text: The field is ours. Press on.

fab_ac_riverlands.0004.desc.text: They crossed the Gods Eye in the dark with cloth wrapped round their oars, and they know that water better than my scouts know the shore. The first we knew of them was the willows moving where there was no wind.\n\nThey struck the rear, among the wounded and the baggage, and were gone again before the horns stopped sounding. Smashed carts, burning tents, and more of my men dead than the reeds cost me.

fab_ac_riverlands.0004.desc.sons.text: \n\nThe prisoners name the two who led them across: [fab_ac_hoare_son_a.GetFirstName] and [fab_ac_hoare_son_b.GetFirstName] Hoare.

fab_ac_riverlands.0004.desc.son.text: \n\nThe prisoners name the man who led them across: [fab_ac_hoare_son_a.GetFirstName] Hoare.

fab_ac_riverlands.0004.desc.close.text: \n\n#bold They fought like ironborn, and they fought well. I shall remember the willows.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0004.option1.text: Count the dead. Then find me those boats.

fab_ac_riverlands.0005.desc.text: Whatever the ironborn know about water, the Gods Eye is a lake, and a lake offers a longship nowhere to hide. They were still out on it at first light, rowing low and heavy with everything they had carried off.\n\nBalerion took them in open water. The boats burned to the waterline, and men in mail do not swim.

fab_ac_riverlands.0005.desc.sons.text: \n\n[fab_ac_hoare_son_a.GetFirstName] and [fab_ac_hoare_son_b.GetFirstName] Hoare went out onto that lake last night. Neither came back.

fab_ac_riverlands.0005.desc.son.text: \n\n[fab_ac_hoare_son_a.GetFirstName] Hoare went out onto that lake last night. He did not come back.

fab_ac_riverlands.0005.desc.close.text: \n\n#bold The willows are paid for. Now Harrenhal.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0005.option1.text: Word will reach Harrenhal before I do.

fab_ac_riverlands.0006.desc.text:
The ravens went out from Harrenhal at first light. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] has called every river lord to arms and named the muster beneath the castle walls.

My outriders have watched the fords and the river road for three days. No columns, no banners out of Stone Hedge or Fairmarket, no boats coming down the Trident. The summons has gone out, and the rivers have gone quiet.

#bold Every lord who ignores that summons has already half-answered mine.#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0006.option1.text: Mark who comes. Mark who does not.

fab_ac_riverlands.0009.desc.text:
Three generations of my house have carried stone for the Hoare kings' monument. Three generations of river blood and river silver, swallowed by that black pile on the Gods Eye, while ironborn reeves count our harvests and ironborn axes answer our complaints.

Now a dragonlord camps at the Blackwater's mouth and makes war on our master, and every riverlord from the Cape of Eagles to Maidenpool is asking the same question behind barred doors: is the dragon a deliverer, or just the next master with a hotter brand?

House Tully has an older answer to that question. We were kings here once, before the storm kings, before the squids. Whoever humbles [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] will need river men to hold the rivers — and the lord who rises FIRST will be remembered above all the lords who merely followed.

fab_ac_riverlands.0009.option1.text: Family, Duty, Honour. Riverrun rises for the dragon.

fab_ac_riverlands.0009.option2.text: We wait, and kneel to whoever is left standing.

fab_ac_riverlands.0010.desc.text: [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstNamePossessive] tyranny has broken the Riverlands for the last time. Riverrun and its banners now stand with the Dragon.\n\nCommand us as you will, and the Trident shall be yours.

fab_ac_riverlands.0010.desc.child.text: Ironborn tyranny has broken the Riverlands for the last time. Riverrun and its banners now stand with the Dragon.\n\nCommand us as you will, and the Trident shall be yours.

fab_ac_riverlands.0011.desc.text:
The word runs down the rivers faster than any raven: Lord Edmyn Tully has thrown open Riverrun to the dragon king and called on every riverlord to rise against [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName].

Three generations we have bled for the squid's monument. Now the Blackwoods are moving, and the Brackens — on the same side, for once in a century, which alone should tell a man which way the gods are leaning. The dragonlord is said to be a lenient overlord, careful of gods and customs, which is more than was ever said of [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName].

If the rivers rise together, we are not rebels; we are a kingdom throwing off a foreign yoke. If we hang back and the dragon wins anyway, our sons will ask us where we were.

fab_ac_riverlands.0011.option1.text: The rivers rise. No more ironborn masters.

fab_ac_riverlands.0011.option2.text: We wait, and kneel to whoever is left standing.

fab_ac_riverlands.0013.desc.text:
Harrenhal devours the horizon long before my host reaches the lakeshore. Five monstrous towers rise above walls broad enough for men to ride six abreast, every stone dark with rain and river mist. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstNameNicknamed] spent forty years raising this place, and forty years bleeding the riverlands to pay for it. The last stone was set scarcely before my landing. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] has built [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim]self a tomb and mistaken it for a kingdom.

My captains measure the walls and return grim-faced. Ladders would break beneath their own weight before reaching the battlements. Rams must cross killing grounds overlooked by a hundred murder holes, while the lake guards one flank and [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName]'s ironborn hold the gates. We may starve [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim] out, perhaps, but the stores within could outlast more than one harvest, and every moon spent here is a moon granted freely to the other kings of Westeros.

Then Balerion's shadow passes over the tents, and the answer seems plain. Stone may keep out men. It has never yet kept out the sky.

Still, fire need not be the first word spoken. I can summon [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] beneath a peace banner and offer [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim] one chance to exchange [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] crown for [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] life—or I can spare those within the castle from dragonflame and trust time, steel, and hunger to open what pride has shut.

fab_ac_riverlands.0013.desc.heir.text:

Forty years of riverland blood and toil went into this place, and the last stone was set scarcely before my landing. The king who raised it is dead, and [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] holds it now.

My captains measure the walls and return grim-faced. Ladders would break beneath their own weight before reaching the battlements. fab_ac_riverlands.0013.desc.child.text:

The king who raised it is dead, and [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] holds it now: a child too young to lift a sword, with ironborn captains commanding the walls in [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] name.

My captains measure the walls and return grim-faced. Ladders would break beneath their own weight before reaching the battlements. Rams must cross killing grounds overlooked by a hundred murder holes, while the lake guards one flank and the ironborn hold the gates. We may starve them out, perhaps, but the stores within could outlast more than one harvest, and every moon spent here is a moon granted freely to the other kings of Westeros.

Then Balerion's shadow passes over the tents, and the answer seems plain. Stone may keep out men. It has never yet kept out the sky.

There will be no parley. I do not bargain with children, nor with the grey captains who hide behind them, and there is no one within those walls whose word could bind the ironborn to a peace. They have had every chance to open their gates. At sunset, they will learn what their walls are worth.

fab_ac_riverlands.0013.option1.text: Send for [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName]. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] shall have one chance to kneel.

fab_ac_riverlands.0013.option1.child.text: No parley with a child. Harrenhal burns at sunset.

fab_ac_riverlands.0013.option2.text: No. Stone will answer stone, and hunger will open the gates.

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.desc.text:
[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] has agreed to words before war. We met on open ground beneath his monstrous castle, under a banner of peace: I came with a handful of knights, and [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] rode out from his gates attended by his sons. The old king is grey and grim, hard as the stone he loves so well, and there was no fear in his eyes as he looked on me - only a black amusement, as a man might look upon a beggar come to demand his hall.

Behind him rose the five towers, and I will grant the old spider this much: no castle ever raised by men has walls the like of them. Forty years of the riverlands' blood and toil stand in those walls. Had I no dragons, I might grow old and die beneath them.

But I have dragons. So let us begin with terms - generous ones, offered once.

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.desc.heir.text:
[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] has agreed to words before war. We met on open ground beneath Harrenhal, under a banner of peace: I came with a handful of knights, and [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] rode out from the gates with ironborn captains at [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] back. There was no fear in [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] eyes as [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe] looked on me, only contempt, as if I were a beggar come to demand [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] hall.

Behind [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim] rose the five towers, and this much I will grant: no castle ever raised by men has walls the like of them. Forty years of the riverlands' blood and toil stand in those walls. Had I no dragons, I might grow old and die beneath them.

But I have dragons. So let us begin with terms - generous ones, offered once.

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.option1.text: #bold Yield now, and you may remain as Lord of the Iron Islands. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.option2.text: #bold Yield now, and your sons will live to rule after you. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.option2.heir.text: #bold Yield now, and your blood will rule the Isles after you. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0014.option3.text: #bold I have eight thousand men outside your walls. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0015.desc.text:
The old king heard my terms out in silence. His sons watched him; one of them, I think, would have taken the offer, had it been his to take. It was not. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] leaned from the saddle and spat, and gave me his answer:

#bold "What is outside my walls is of no concern to me. Those walls are strong and thick."#!

Strong and thick. Every stone of them paid for with riverland blood, every tower cursed by the widows of the men who died raising them. He wrung this castle out of a conquered people for forty years, and now he means to hide inside it while my host breaks against the gates.

He is still thinking of walls. He has not yet understood what has landed on his shores.

fab_ac_riverlands.0015.desc.heir.text:
[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] heard my terms out in silence. The captains at [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] back watched [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim], and more than one of them, I think, would have taken the offer, had it been theirs to take. It was not. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] leaned from the saddle and spat, and gave me [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] answer:

#bold "What is outside my walls is of no concern to me. Those walls are strong and thick."#!

Strong and thick. Every stone of them paid for with riverland blood, every tower cursed by the widows of the men who died raising them. Now [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe] means to hide behind them while my host breaks against the gates.

[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] is still thinking of walls. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] has not yet understood what has landed on [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] shores.

fab_ac_riverlands.0015.option1.text: #bold But not so high as to keep out dragons. Dragons fly. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0016.desc.text:
For the first time, something moved behind the old king's eyes - not fear, not yet, but the shadow where fear begins. He mastered it quick enough, and his answer came flat as a falling portcullis:

#bold "I built in stone. Stone does not burn."#!

And there it is - the whole of [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName]'s faith, laid bare beneath a peace banner. He believes it. He has come to believe that so much cruelty piled so high must be proof against anything: gods, time, and dragons alike.

The sun hangs low and red in the west behind his towers. Words are done. There is only one thing left to say to him, and then a wheeling of horses, and the long ride back to my host - and I shall not look behind me.

fab_ac_riverlands.0016.desc.heir.text:

#bold "Harrenhal is built in stone. Stone does not burn."#!

And there it is - the whole of [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName]'s faith, laid bare beneath a peace banner. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] believes it. [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetSheHe|U] has come to believe that so much cruelty piled so high must be proof against anything: gods, time, and dragons alike.

The sun hangs low and red in the west behind the towers. Words are done. There is only one thing left to say to [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHim], and then a wheeling of horses, and the long ride back to my host - and I shall not look behind me.

fab_ac_riverlands.0016.option1.text: #bold When the sun sets, your line shall end. #!

fab_ac_riverlands.0017.desc.text:
The dragonlord came to my gates under a peace banner, and I rode out to hear him. He is younger than I thought, and quieter — he wastes no words, I will grant him that.

He offered me the Iron Islands for my line if I yield, and pointed to the thousands he has camped outside my walls. I told him plainly: what is outside my walls is no concern of mine. Walls like these have never been built before.

#bold 'But not so high as to keep out dragons,'#! he said. #bold 'Dragons fly.'#!

I built in stone, I told him. Stone does not burn.

He looked at me the way a man looks at a grave already dug, and gave me until sunset. My sons watch from the towers. The choice is mine to make.

fab_ac_riverlands.0017.desc.heir.text:
The dragonlord came to my gates under a peace banner, and I rode out to hear him. He is younger than I thought, and quieter — he wastes no words, I will grant him that.

He offered me the Iron Islands for my line if I yield, and pointed to the thousands he has camped outside my walls. I told him plainly: what is outside my walls is no concern of mine. Walls like these have never been built before.

#bold 'But not so high as to keep out dragons,'#! he said. #bold 'Dragons fly.'#!

Harrenhal is built in stone, I told him. Stone does not burn.

He looked at me the way a man looks at a grave already dug, and gave me until sunset. My kin watch from the towers. The choice is mine to make.

fab_ac_riverlands.0017.option1.text: Stone does not burn. He may do his worst.

fab_ac_riverlands.0017.option2.text: Bend the knee, and keep the Isles.

fab_ac_riverlands.0018.desc.text:
[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] had given me [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] answer, and it was no answer at all. So be it.

When the sun went down I took Balerion up, higher and higher into the dark, through the cold and the clouds, until the greatest castle ever raised in Westeros was but a scattering of embers far below and the dragon himself no larger than a moth against the moon. There we turned. There we fell.

On wings black as pitch Balerion plunged through the night, and when the five towers of Harrenhal rose up to meet us, the dragon opened his jaws and bathed them in black fire shot through with swords of red.

Stone does not burn, [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] had boasted to me. But no castle is made of stone alone. The wood and the wool, the hemp and the straw, the bread and the salt beef and the grain in the storerooms — all of it took fire. Nor were [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] ironmen made of stone. Smoking, screaming, wrapped in flame, they fled across the yards and fell from the wallwalks to break upon the ground below. And stone itself will crack and run if the fire is hot enough. The towers glowed red against the night like five great candles, and like candles they began to slump and twist, molten rock streaming down their sides.

[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstNameNicknamed] and the last of [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] line perished in the inferno that swallowed that monstrous seat. The Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers died with them, and the Riverlands were mine.

fab_ac_riverlands.0018.desc.child.text:
There was no answer to be had from a child, and I sought none.

When the sun went down I took Balerion up, higher and higher into the dark, through the cold and the clouds, until the greatest castle ever raised in Westeros was but a scattering of embers far below and the dragon himself no larger than a moth against the moon. There we turned. There we fell.

On wings black as pitch Balerion plunged through the night, and when the five towers of Harrenhal rose up to meet us, the dragon opened his jaws and bathed them in black fire shot through with swords of red.

Stone does not burn, the ironborn boasted. But no castle is made of stone alone. The wood and the wool, the hemp and the straw, the bread and the salt beef and the grain in the storerooms — all of it took fire. Nor were the ironmen made of stone. Smoking, screaming, wrapped in flame, they fled across the yards and fell from the wallwalks to break upon the ground below. And stone itself will crack and run if the fire is hot enough. The towers glowed red against the night like five great candles, and like candles they began to slump and twist, molten rock streaming down their sides.

[fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetFirstName] and the last of [fab_ac_harrenhal_lord.GetHerHis] line perished in the inferno that swallowed that monstrous seat. The Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers died with them, and the Riverlands were mine.

fab_ac_riverlands.0019.desc.text:
The ironborn yoke is lifted from the Trident. Three generations the riverlands groaned beneath House Hoare, bled for its wars and its walls - and it was the rivermen themselves, as much as my dragons, who threw the yoke off. I mean them to remember that. But a land without a lord is a land at war with itself, and the Trident must have a Lord Paramount to hold it in my name. Two names weigh heaviest in my councils.

Edmyn Tully of Riverrun was the first of the river lords to rise for me. He called his banners while the ironborn still held the Trident and the outcome was anything but sure, and where Riverrun led, the rest of the Trident followed. The riverlords know him; they trust him; he is one of their own. A loyal man raised high by a grateful king - that is a lesson I would have all Westeros learn, and learn early.

And yet there is Quenton Qoherys, my old master-at-arms at Dragonstone, who taught me the sword and then carried one at my side. The blood of Old Valyria runs in his veins as it does in mine - a brother-in-arms, proven long before this conquest began. Give him the Trident and its heart is held by a man bound to me by more than gratitude.

Some at court speak also for the Mallisters of Seagard - an ancient and honorable line, with war-ships to watch the ironmen's return.

#bold Who deserves the Trident?#!

fab_ac_riverlands.0019.option1.text: Lord Tully rose first. He shall rise highest.

fab_ac_riverlands.0019.option2.text: The blood of Old Valyria shall rule the Trident.

fab_ac_riverlands.0020.desc.text:
The ironborn king is ash, his line is ended, and the king the rivers rose for has kept faith with the men who rose first.

Before the assembled riverlords, King Aegon has named House Tully Lords Paramount of the Trident — the fealty of every lord from the Cape of Eagles to Maidenpool, sworn not to a conqueror's garrison but to Riverrun. The rivers ruled by river men, for the first time in three hundred years.

I wagered my house on a stranger with three dragons when the wise counsel was to wait. Every lord who waited can reflect on the difference between rising and following.

fab_ac_riverlands.0020.option1.text: The Trident acclaims Aegon the Dragon.

fab_ac_riverlands.0021.desc.text:
Harrenhal stands. That is the most that can be said of it - the towers raised to outlast the ages are melted and blackened, twisted like the candles of some giant's feast, and the halls below still reek of smoke. Yet even ruined, those walls command the heart of the riverlands, and the greatest castle ever raised by men cannot sit lordless.

Quenton Qoherys served me long years as master-at-arms of Dragonstone; it was he who first put a proper sword in my hand. His blood is the blood of Old Valyria, and he has fought at my side since we came ashore. To seat House Qoherys at Harrenhal is to put a man I trust at the center of my new realm - and to show all Westeros that those who follow the dragon rise with him.

With House Hoare no longer an obstacle, the seat is mine to give. Though perhaps a castle so great should not be given at all - the dragon might keep Harrenhal for House Targaryen, for now.

fab_ac_riverlands.0021.option1.text: Harrenhal shall pass to the newly raised House Qoherys.

fab_ac_riverlands.0021.option2.text: Valyrian blood shall guard the heart of the Trident.

fab_ac_riverlands.0021.option3.text: The castle may serve another purpose.

fab_ac_riverlands.0021.desc.whole.text:
Harrenhal stands whole. Those five monstrous towers were raised to outlast the ages, and outlast their builder they have - black and enormous above the waters of the Gods Eye, behind walls no host in Westeros could hope to storm. It never came to fire; the greatest castle ever raised by men passes to me with not a stone out of place, and the halls that were built to humble kings now wait upon mine. So vast a seat cannot sit lordless.

Quenton Qoherys served me long years as master-at-arms of Dragonstone; it was he who first put a proper sword in my hand. His blood is the blood of Old Valyria, and he has fought at my side since we came ashore. To seat House Qoherys at Harrenhal is to put a man I trust at the center of my new realm - and to show all Westeros that those who follow the dragon rise with him.

With House Hoare no longer an obstacle, the seat is mine to give. Though perhaps a castle so great should not be given at all - the dragon might keep Harrenhal for House Targaryen, for now.

fab_ac_riverlands.0022.text: The Keys to the Great Folly

fab_ac_riverlands.0022.desc.text:
My house followed the Targaryens out of Valyria before the Doom, when leaving was madness and staying was death, and we have served on Dragonstone ever since — I taught the king himself his swordwork, in the yard below the Stone Drum.

I expected a modest reward when the wars were done. A keep, some land. Instead the king has given me Harrenhal — the greatest castle ever raised by men, with the burnt bones of its last king barely cold in the tower they now call Kingspyre.

The river lords look sideways at a Valyrian master-at-arms raised over them, and the smallfolk mutter that the place is cursed. Perhaps. But a house must begin somewhere, and House Qoherys begins in the largest hall in Westeros.

fab_ac_riverlands.0022.option1.text: We serve the Dragon, as we always have.

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.desc.text: The King of the Isles and the Rivers is ended - his line, his kingdom, and his boast, all in a single night. The Trident is mine, and the rivermen who bled to raise his walls now kneel to the house that brought them down.\n\n

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.option1.text: We shall crush Argilac, to Storm's End!

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.desc.whole.text: The King of the Isles and the Rivers is finished - his kingdom taken from him, his boast undone, the ironborn grip on the Trident broken for good and all. His towers still stand above the Gods Eye, but no Hoare will look on them again as a king. The rivermen who bled to build his walls now kneel to the house that freed them of him.\n\n

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.desc.south.text: Now all eyes turn south. Argilac the Arrogant still names himself the Storm King, and it was his insolence - my envoy's hands, returned to me in a box - that began this war. He will not make the ironborn king's error; the old warrior has no love of walls. He will come out to meet us, sword in hand, as Durrandon kings have done for a thousand years.\n\nThere is talk already of what follows him. Argilac has no son, only his daughter Argella, and no other Durrandon survives; some at my councils would see a Stormlander loyal to our house raised over the stormlands when he falls. Decisions for another day. First, the Storm King must have his storm.

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.desc.south_fallen.text: The south has not waited for me. Argilac the Arrogant is dead, and the war his insolence began is nearly finished without him. His daughter still holds Storm's End, but the stormlords are already choosing between her and the dragon, and that choice will not take long.

fab_ac_riverlands.0023.option_storm_marc.text: The Trident is mine. Storm's End will follow.

fab_ac_riverlands.0025.desc.text:
The Targaryen is finished — dead or skulking back on his rock, no two tales agree. His grand conquest is done, and it never so much as reached my walls.

A salt-lordling with three beasts thought to make himself king of all Westeros by writing letters. The kings of the Isles and the Rivers have outlasted a hundred such dreamers.

Harrenhal stands. That is the only answer the world ever needed to give him.

fab_ac_riverlands.0025.option1.text: The last ember of Valyria, gone out.

fab_ac_riverlands.0026.desc.text:
The dragon has broken off. His host is scattered from the Gods Eye to the Trident, his lords are riding south with their tails tucked, and half my camp swears he is dead. I will believe that when a man sets the head on my table.

He crossed my rivers. He burned my fields. And then he came to the foot of my walls and learned what forty years of stone means. Every dreamer who thought dragons had made walls worthless may now think again.

The Kingdom of the Isles and the Rivers stands. Harrenhal stands. He may come again when he has the stomach for it.

fab_ac_riverlands.0026.option1.text: He is welcome to come again.

fab_ac_stormlands.0001.desc.text:
The host turns south - but I shall not lead it. This war began with an insult to Orys as much as to me: it was his hand Argilac scorned to take, offering my brother-in-arms a lesser match as one throws scraps to a dog. So it is Orys, my Hand, who leads the flower of my strength down the coast toward Storm's End - and above his columns flies Queen Rhaenys upon Meraxes, silver and gold against the darkening sky.

Our scouts tell us Argilac has stripped his garrisons and gathers his whole power in the open field. The old warrior knows how Harren died; he will not rot behind stone waiting for dragonfire. He means to meet Orys blade to blade, with the storm at his back, and end this war the old way - or end himself in the trying.

He shall have his battle. The clouds are already piling black above the stormlands, as if the Storm God himself means to attend.

#bold The singers will want a name for what is coming. Something tells me they shall call it the Last Storm.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0001.desc.first.text:
The host turns south - but I shall not lead it. This war began with an insult to Orys as much as to me: it was his hand Argilac scorned to take, offering my brother-in-arms a lesser match as one throws scraps to a dog. So it is Orys, my Hand, who leads the flower of my strength down the coast toward Storm's End - and above his columns flies Queen Rhaenys upon Meraxes, silver and gold against the darkening sky.

Our scouts tell us Argilac has stripped his garrisons and gathers his whole power in the open field. The old warrior has no love of walls, and no intention of rotting behind them while dragons circle his sky. He means to meet Orys blade to blade, with the storm at his back, and end this war the old way - or end himself in the trying.

He shall have his battle. The clouds are already piling black above the stormlands, as if the Storm God himself means to attend.

#bold The singers will want a name for what is coming. Something tells me they shall call it the Last Storm.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0002.desc.text:
For two days the sky above the stormlands has been black as a bruise, and on the second day Argilac came out to meet us. His counsellors begged him to keep behind his walls - Storm's End has never fallen, and no dragon has yet tried its stones. The old king would not hear it. He had no wish to learn what dragonfire makes of a castle that cannot answer it; he would not die roasting in his own keep. Better to trust to sword and storm, and meet his foe in the open field.

So he came down upon our host with the gale at his back, rain falling in sheets, the ground churned to mire - and I will say this of him: it was well and cunningly done. His heavy horse smashed into our line while the wet kept our archers' strings slack, and the same storm he trusted in kept Meraxes out of the sky: no dragon could take wing in that howling murk. For a black hour the day hung in the balance.

Then our center bent, and broke - and the storm knights poured through the gap at the gallop, thinking the day already won.

#bold They could not know what my sister had set waiting for them at the heart of our host.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0003.desc.text:
The gods sent a storm worthy of the name, and I chose it for my battlefield — rain to drown their bowstrings, mud to swallow their advance, and their she-dragon's wings pinned to the earth by the gale.

Twice my horse charged their flank; twice the mud and the dragonfire threw us back, and in the third press my own mount went down and I fought on foot, ringed by dead men of both colours. That was when the bastard came down the hill to find me.

He called on me to yield. Yield! I gave him my answer with steel. Now we fight, he and I, in the rain and the ruin of my army — the old king of the storm against the dragon's strong right hand. The singers had best watch closely. Whatever they sing, they will not sing that Argilac knelt.

fab_ac_stormlands.0004.desc.text:
Any other day, Meraxes would have ruled the sky above that field. Not this day - the rain fell too hard and the wind blew too wild for any dragon to fly. So Rhaenys did not fly. She sat Meraxes at the very center of our host, on the ground, wings folded tight against the storm, still as a rock in a river while the battle broke around her. Waiting.

The storm knights burst through our shattered center at the full gallop - and found her. Horses that had carried their riders through arrow-hail and shield-wall took one look at what stood before them and went mad. And Meraxes, they will learn, needs no sky. She met the charge the way a cliff meets a wave: dragonflame at ten paces cares nothing for wet ground, and what the fire did not take, her jaws did - horse and rider together, whole.

The breach that was to win Argilac his battle became his ruin. The charge died where it stood, and what was left of the storm lords' van reeled back into the rain, whipped on by the gale, past their king.

#bold Argilac's great gamble broke on the one thing no storm can drown.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0004.option1.text: Bring me word of how it ends.

fab_ac_stormlands.0005.desc.text:
Twice Argilac was unhorsed, and twice he found his feet and killed the men who came to take him. Now he stands ringed by dismounted knights in the pouring rain, his guard dead about him, his host fled or dying - and thrice offered quarter, thrice he has answered with steel. He did not come out from behind his walls to be taken.

Word was carried to Orys, and my Hand - gods love him - did as I myself would have done. He bade the ring of spears open. He climbed down from his horse and drew his longsword, and called on the old king to finish this in the old way, blade to blade.

An old storm of a man, last of a line of kings that runs back to the dawn of days, and the finest sword of my host, alone in the mud between two armies. Argilac the Arrogant shall have the death he came seeking - a blade in his hand and a worthy foe before him.

#bold It remains only to see whose blood the rain washes away.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0005.option1.text: Orys fights with my blessing. (Guide his blade)

fab_ac_stormlands.0005.option2.text: This is Orys' fight, not mine. (The Gods shall decide it)

fab_ac_stormlands.0007.desc.text:
It was nearly a song - the wrong song. Argilac fought as though the Warrior himself had slipped into his old bones: he turned every cut, gave back two for one, and beat my Hand down to one knee in the mud. The men who watched say the old king was laughing when he raised his sword for the killing stroke.

Then the storm itself came down upon him.

Rhaenys had watched the whole of it from Meraxes' back, grounded at the center of the field where the charge had broken, near enough to see every stroke through the rain. She did not wait to see this one fall. Grounded or no, a dragon crosses a hundred yards of mud faster than any horse ever foaled - Meraxes came on like the tide coming in, and the last of the Storm Kings ended in dragonflame, cheated at the very last of the death he had come out to find. The singers can quarrel over whether that was mercy.

#bold Orys lives - bruised in body, and wounded far worse in his pride. He owes my sister a debt no Hand will find easy to carry.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0007.option1.text: The debt is owed to Rhaenys.

fab_ac_stormlands.0008.text: The Last of the Storm Kings

fab_ac_stormlands.0008.desc.text:
They fought in the mud between the two hosts, my Hand and the old king, while thousands stood in the rain and watched. Argilac was strong yet, and full of an old man's cunning - he marked Orys more than once, and there was a moment, the watchers say, when the day might have gone either way. But Orys was younger, and colder, and the better blade. It ended as such things end: quickly, at the last, and in silence but for the rain.

Argilac Durrandon died as he wished to die - sword in hand, storm at his back, the last Storm King of a line that had held Storm's End since the dawn of days. And Orys, gallant even in victory, knelt beside him in the mud and closed his eyes with his own hand. Men on both sides will remember that.

#bold Storm's End yet stands - and within it Argilac's daughter Argella, who has barred her gates, they say, and named herself the Storm Queen. The storm is broken. What remains is only rain.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0008.option1.text: He died the old way. Honor him for it.

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.text: The Fate of the Storm King

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.desc.duel.text:
So ends Argilac, called the Arrogant - the last Storm King, felled blade to blade by my Hand in the mud and the rain, with two armies for witnesses. The singers are already at work on it; they call the battle the Last Storm, and for once the singers have it right. There will be no other. A line of kings that ran unbroken from Durran Godsgrief - through storm and siege and the Andals and a thousand years of pride - has ended on a sword's point, in the old way, exactly as the old man wished.

His host is dead, fled, or kneeling. His kingdom is a body without a head.

But not quite without a crown. Word comes from the south that Argilac's daughter Argella has barred the gates of Storm's End and named herself the Storm Queen - one castle, one garrison, and one young woman's defiance against everything that broke her father.

#bold Durran's ancient seat has never once fallen to storm or siege. We shall see what it makes of dragons.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.desc.meraxes.text:
So ends Argilac, called the Arrogant - the last Storm King, and it must be said plainly: no man killed him. He beat the finest sword of my host to one knee, and it took Meraxes herself to end him. The storm lords will grieve, but they will not be ashamed; their king died with his blade in his hand, undefeated by any man living, and the singers will make much of it. They call the battle the Last Storm, and for once the singers have it right. A line of kings that ran unbroken from Durran Godsgrief has ended - in dragonflame, as this whole conquest may yet be written.

His host is dead, fled, or kneeling. His kingdom is a body without a head.

But not quite without a crown. Word comes from the south that Argilac's daughter Argella has barred the gates of Storm's End and named herself the Storm Queen - one castle, one garrison, and one young woman's defiance against everything that broke her father.

#bold Durran's ancient seat has never once fallen to storm or siege. We shall see what it makes of dragons.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.desc.fallen.text:
So ends Argilac, called the Arrogant - the last Storm King. He did not get the ending the singers would have written for him, steel against steel before two watching hosts; war is not a song, and it takes kings as carelessly as it takes lesser men. However it found him, it found him with a sword in his hand - no one who knew the man doubts that much - and a line of kings that ran unbroken from Durran Godsgrief has ended with him.

His host is dead, fled, or kneeling. His kingdom is a body without a head.

But not quite without a crown. Word comes from the south that Argilac's daughter Argella has barred the gates of Storm's End and named herself the Storm Queen - one castle, one garrison, and one young woman's defiance against everything that broke her father.

#bold Durran's ancient seat has never once fallen to storm or siege. We shall see what it makes of dragons.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.desc.deposed.text:
So ends the reign of Argilac, called the Arrogant - though not, as it happens, the man himself. The last Storm King did not get the ending the singers would have written for him: no duel before two watching hosts, no blaze of glory. His strength failed him by inches instead - castle by castle, banner by banner - until nothing remained but to accept my terms and live. There are those who say the old warrior would sooner have died sword in hand. Perhaps. But a king who has spent his whole life fighting knows better than most when a fight is finished.

He is the last of his line to have worn a crown, whatever becomes of his blood hereafter. A line of kings that ran unbroken from Durran Godsgrief ends not in fire or steel, but in a signature.

His host is broken, his lords are kneeling - and his kingdom must now be given into stronger hands.

#bold The storm is spent. What remains is to settle who shall hold the stormlands in my name.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0010.option1.text: Argilac's reign ends upon this field.

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.desc.text:
Storm's End's defiance lasted less than a fortnight - and it was not broken by us. Argella's own garrison looked out from those unfallen walls at my host and my dragons, and understood what no one needed to tell them: walls that have never fallen have also never been asked to stop dragonfire. Rather than burn for a one-day queen they rose against her in the night, and delivered her to Orys' camp as a peace offering: gagged, chained, and naked as her name day.

Orys shamed every man of them. He struck off her chains with his own hands, wrapped his cloak about her shoulders, and gave her food and wine beside his fire - and told her, gently, of her father's courage at the end. She has not yet spoken a word, they say; she watches him the way a caged bird watches a cat. Fear like hers is not mended in a day. But if any man alive can mend it, it is my brother.

I have granted Orys the stormlands as Lord Paramount, and to bind the storm lords to him he shall wed Argella - and take for his new-founded House Baratheon the crowned stag of Durrandon and their words with it. Her father's seat, her father's banner, her father's words: nothing is taken from her line but the crown. Thus the blood of Durran Godsgrief is not ended, but joined to my own.

#bold Once an heir is born to them, the stormlands will be held forever by my brother's line - and the fury of the storm will answer to the dragon.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.desc.noargella.text:
Storm's End's defiance is ended, and the stormlands must now be held - and there was never any question of whose hand should hold them. I have granted Orys the stormlands as Lord Paramount: my brother in all but name, my Hand, and the man whose sword did more than any other to win this coast. He takes for his new-founded House Baratheon the crowned stag of Durrandon and their words with it - the arms of the kings he broke, kept alive in the house that broke them. It is how such things should be done: the old glories folded into the new, not burned with them.

The marriage that might have sealed it - Orys and Argilac's daughter Argella - was not to be; fate disposed of that match before we could make it. A pity. It would have been neater. But the stormlords will learn to love the stag on its own account, or they will learn to fear it; my brother has a gift for teaching both.

#bold The stormlands are settled, and settled on my own blood. The fury of the storm will answer to the dragon.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.option1.text: Long may the stag stand beside the dragon.

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.option2.text: Ours is the Fury. (Play as Orys Baratheon)

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.option3.text: No dead king's words, no dead king's daughter. His own house, under the hand.

fab_ac_stormlands.0011.option4.text: The Right Hand takes his own path. (Play as Orys Baratheon)

fab_ac_stormlands.0012.text: A Second House of the Dragon

fab_ac_stormlands.0012.desc.text:
The crowned stag does not fly above Storm's End. Orys would take neither the dead king's daughter nor the dead king's glory for his own. He has kept the banner beneath which he won the stormlands: a black hand upon red, the sign of the brother who has ever been my strong right hand.

The stormlords may mutter of a bastard raised too high. I know the blood in Orys' veins. He is my father's son, my half-brother, and no less a scion of old Valyria for the accident of his birth. If his new house is to stand upon that inheritance, I may give it a greater inheritance still.

At my command, three heavy caskets have been brought from Dragonstone. Within them lie three dragon eggs, dark and hard as polished stone, yet warm beneath the hand. Given to Orys, they might one day make the Baratheons a second family of dragonlords—bound to House Targaryen by blood, loyalty, and fire. Or they might place dragons in hands beyond my own line for the first time.

#bold House Baratheon may fly beside us. Yet a dragon flying beside you may one day choose another course.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0012.option1.text: He is blood of old Valyria, as we are. The Baratheons shall fly beside us.

fab_ac_stormlands.0012.option2.text: Alas, there can be only one Dragonlord family in Westeros.

fab_ac_stormlands.0012.eggs_tt.text: Three dragon eggs from Dragonstone will be given to Lord Orys

fab_ac_stormlands.0013.desc.text:
The crowned stag does not fly above my new-won walls. I took neither Argella Durrandon's hand nor her father's glory. Above Storm's End flies the banner I carried into the Last Storm: a black hand upon red, the sign of the service I have given freely and the victories I may claim as my own.

The stormlords call me bastard when they believe I cannot hear them. They are right, but it is not the whole truth. The same father sired Aegon and me. The blood of old Valyria runs in my veins, however the maesters choose to write my name.

My brother receives me alone. Before him stand three heavy caskets brought from Dragonstone, and within them lie three dragon eggs, dark and hard as polished stone, yet warm beneath my hand. He offers them not to his Hand or his Lord Paramount, but to his brother. With them, my children might take to the skies beside his own, and House Baratheon might become a dragonriding family in truth. Yet accepting them would end House Targaryen's mastery of dragonflame—and bind our descendants to the wisdom, or folly, of ours.

#bold I have claimed my own name and banner. Now I must decide what bloodright will pass with them.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0013.option1.text: I am blood of old Valyria, as he is. The Baratheons shall fly beside him.

fab_ac_stormlands.0013.option2.text: Alas, there can be only one Dragonlord family in Westeros.

fab_ac_stormlands.0015.desc.text:
The storm is broken. Argilac the Arrogant is finished - his host scattered, his line's thousand-year reign ended - and the stormlands answer to the dragon now. The kingdoms that watched him defy me have gone very quiet.

So all eyes turn north, to the last king standing between me and the mastery of the east: Harren the Black, squatting behind the walls of the greatest castle men have ever raised. He believes those walls make him a different matter from Argilac. They make him slower, nothing more.

And Harren carries a weakness no wall can mend: the riverlands hate him. Forty years of the lash and the quarry built Harrenhal, and the men who paid for it in blood and sons remember every stone of the price. I am told there are riverlords who would rise for any banner that promised an end of ironborn rule. Good. They can rise for mine.

There is talk already of what comes after - whether Harren's sons might keep the Iron Islands if they bend the knee, and who shall hold the Trident, for the riverlands will never again answer to Pyke whatever else befalls. Decisions for another day. First, we must conquer.

#bold Harren trusts in stone. We shall see what stone is worth.#!

fab_ac_stormlands.0015.option1.text: The Black will kneel - or Harrenhal will be his pyre.

fab_ac_stormlands.0015.option_rivers_mar.text: The storm is broken. Harrenhal is next.

fab_ac_stormlands.0016.desc.text:
The would-be conqueror is finished — dead, or fled back to his rock, the tales cannot agree, and I find I do not care which. His host is scattered and his great crowning of himself is a jape the singers will tell over wine for a hundred years.

King of all Westeros. Seven kingdoms have stood since before the Andals crossed the sea, and one boy with three beasts thought to swallow them whole.

The storm endures. It always has.

fab_ac_west.0001.desc.text:
With Harren dead in his melted towers and the Storm King broken, one stubborn corner of my new realm remained unspoken for: Crackclaw Point, that tangle of bogs and pine barrens and cracked grey cliffs between the bay and the narrow sea. Petty lords in half-ruined towers, the Brunes and Boggses and Crabbs and Hardys, who never truly bent to Harren nor to the Storm Kings before him - a people who have made proud poverty and stubbornness into something near a religion.

Visenya went herself, alone on Vhagar, to demand their submission. She has always understood such folk better than I do, and they proved her right. The Crackclaw lords are poor, but they are not blind: they had heard of Harrenhal, and they knew they had no chance against a dragon. One by one they came out of their bogs and towers and laid their swords at my sister's feet - without a qualm, she tells me, and near enough with pride, for kneeling to a Valyrian queen on dragonback stings less than kneeling to a neighbor.

And Visenya, in her wisdom, gave them the one reward such men treasure: she took them as her own. No riverlord shall be set over them, no Crownland liege, no middleman of any stripe. The lords of Crackclaw Point shall owe fealty to no one - no one but the Iron Throne itself.

#bold A wilderness of proud beggars, sworn direct to the crown. Visenya may have bought more loyalty with that promise than I have bought with three kingdoms' worth of pardons.#!

fab_ac_west.0001.option1.text: They kneel to the dragon alone. Next, we move west.

fab_ac_west.0001.option_west_won.text: They kneel to the dragon alone, as the West already does.

fab_ac_west.0001.option_west_marching.text: They kneel to the dragon alone. The host is already west.

fab_ac_west.0001.desc.alt.text:
With the Trident won and the last of Harren's banners struck, one stubborn corner of my new realm remained unspoken for: Crackclaw Point, that tangle of bogs and pine barrens and cracked grey cliffs between the bay and the narrow sea. Petty lords in half-ruined towers, the Brunes and Boggses and Crabbs and Hardys, who never truly bent to Harren nor to the Storm Kings before him - a people who have made proud poverty and stubbornness into something near a religion.

Visenya went herself, alone on Vhagar, to demand their submission. She has always understood such folk better than I do, and they proved her right. The Crackclaw lords are poor, but they are not blind: they had heard what became of Harren's kingdom, and they knew they had no chance against a dragon.
