One by one they came out of their bogs and towers and laid their swords at my sister's feet - without a qualm, she tells me, and near enough with pride, for kneeling to a Valyrian queen on dragonback stings less than kneeling to a neighbor.

And Visenya, in her wisdom, gave them the one reward such men treasure: she took them as her own. No riverlord shall be set over them, no Crownland liege, no middleman of any stripe. The lords of Crackclaw Point shall owe fealty to no one - no one but the Iron Throne itself.

#bold A wilderness of proud beggars, sworn direct to the crown. Visenya may have bought more loyalty with that promise than I have bought with three kingdoms' worth of pardons.#!

fab_ac_west.0002.text: The Lion and the Green Hand

fab_ac_west.0002.desc.text:
The two great kings of the west have made common cause against me at last.

From Highgarden marches Mern, the Ninth of His Name of House Gardener, King of the Reach, with the whole strength of the most fertile kingdom in Westeros at his back. Beneath the walls of Goldengrove he was met by Loren Lannister, King of the Rock, come down out of the westerlands with all the gold-bought steel of Casterly Rock behind him. Together, my outriders swear, they command the mightiest host ever seen in Westeros: five-and-fifty thousand strong, six hundred lords great and small beneath their banners, and above five thousand knights in armor. Neither king has any love for the other - the Rock and the Reach have warred over the marches for a thousand years - but fear of the dragon has made brothers of old enemies.

And they are not waiting for me to come to them. A host that size eats the land bare wherever it stands; already they have struck their camps at Goldengrove and turned north, through the tall grass and the golden wheat, looking for my host and a battle to end this war at a stroke.

#bold Two crowned kings, marching together, with five men for every one of mine.#!

fab_ac_west.0003.desc.text:
The latest ravens lie open across my council table, each bearing the same impossible news. Harren the Black is dead within the walls he called unbreakable. Argilac Durrandon has fallen with his sword in hand. Two ancient crowns have vanished in the time it takes a merchant to ride from Lannisport to the Rock.

One letter bears the green hand of House Gardener. King Mern proposes that Reach and Rock meet Aegon together: his endless fields of spears joined to my armored horse and golden treasury. Our kingdoms have contested the marches for generations, but neither of us will have a frontier left to quarrel over if the dragon takes both crowns.

Pride counsels me to stand alone. Arithmetic gives wiser counsel. United, we will raise the greatest host Westeros has ever seen—and make Aegon learn that three beasts cannot hold a continent.

fab_ac_west.0003.option1.text: Send my answer to Highgarden: the lion stands with the hand.

fab_ac_west.0004.desc.text:
Each raven from the east bears the death of something ancient. Harren's towers could not shelter him from dragonfire. Argilac's courage could not save his crown. The riverlands and stormlands now answer to a lord whose army would scarcely fill one wing of my own host.

That is the danger. Aegon has proved that walls and valor, offered separately, are not enough. If I wait behind the Mander while he destroys each kingdom in turn, the greatest strength in Westeros will be spent fighting alone. So I have summoned my council beneath the green banners of Highgarden and written the letter pride once forbade me to write.

Loren Lannister commands the gold and heavy horse of the Rock. I command the harvest, chivalry, and numberless spears of the Reach. Our fathers quarreled over borders; our sons will have no kingdoms to inherit unless lion and green hand stand together now.

fab_ac_west.0004.option1.text: By Our Hand, the Reach shall answer—and the lion with us.

fab_ac_west.0005.desc.text:
The Two Kings may have their numbers. I have something better.

My host - a fifth of theirs, and much of it river-lord steel sworn to me barely half a year - I have given over to [fab_host_lord.GetTitledFirstName] of Maidenpool. That house was among the first to take the field against me after the landing, and left its old lord among the slain for it; the oath sworn to me amid that wreckage has been kept better than most given freely, and its lord is a steadier hand in the field than lords twice its rank can boast. [fab_host_lord.GetSheHe] knows what I need: not to win the battle, but to hold the line while the sky does the winning. Smaller than theirs my host may be, but it moves twice as fast - and I mean to choose the ground, not have it chosen for me.

For the rest, this battle will be fought by three. Through every war of this conquest my sisters and I have struck separately - Visenya to Crackclaw Point, Rhaenys to the Last Storm, each dragon a war unto itself. Not this time. Against five-and-fifty thousand there will be no dividing of our strength: Balerion, Vhagar and Meraxes will take the sky together, over one field, for the first time since we left Dragonstone.

#bold The Two Kings believe they are marching to fight an army. They are marching to learn what three dragons are.#!

fab_ac_west.0005.option1.text: Send word to Queen Visenya and Queen Rhaenys, at once.

fab_ac_west.0005.desc.early.text:
The Two Kings may have their numbers. I have something better.

My host - a fifth of theirs, and much of it sworn to me only since I came ashore - I have given over to [fab_host_lord.GetTitledFirstName] of Maidenpool. That house was among the first to take the field against me after the landing, and left its old lord among the slain for it; the oath sworn to me amid that wreckage has been kept better than most given freely, and its lord is a steadier hand in the field than lords twice its rank can boast. [fab_host_lord.GetSheHe] knows what I need: not to win the battle, but to hold the line while the sky does the winning. Smaller than theirs my host may be, but it moves twice as fast - and I mean to choose the ground, not have it chosen for me.

For the rest, this battle will be fought by three. Since the landing my sisters and I have flown apart more often than together, each dragon a war unto itself. Not this time. Against five-and-fifty thousand there will be no dividing of our strength: Balerion, Vhagar and Meraxes will take the sky together, over one field, for the first time since we left Dragonstone.

#bold The Two Kings believe they are marching to fight an army. They are marching to learn what three dragons are.#!

fab_ac_west.0006.desc.text:
The passes behind us are choked with men, horses, wagons, and streaming crimson banners. Every lord of the westerlands has answered me. Ahead, across the Reach, Mern Gardener marches beneath a still greater forest of green. Where our hosts join, fifty-five thousand soldiers will stand together—the largest army ever gathered on this continent.

Aegon's force is scarcely a fifth of ours. His men have campaigned without rest, far from Dragonstone and with hostile kingdoms on every side. Even dragons must land, eat, and tire. If we spread wide enough, press hard enough, and give him nowhere to escape, flesh and blood must tell.

My captains speak confidently around the fires. I have made my own calculations twice. The numbers remain overwhelmingly in our favor.

fab_ac_west.0006.option1.text: Sound the march. Aegon can count our banners.

fab_ac_west.0007.text: The Dragon Marches on the Reach

fab_ac_west.0007.desc.text:
The outriders reached camp before dawn: Aegon has crossed the Blackwater and turned southwest into the Reach. His main host advances along the river roads while his fleet keeps pace upon the coast. Balerion flies above the center; Vhagar and Meraxes range ahead, burning watchtowers and scattering every company sent to delay him. For the first time in the war, all three Targaryens and all three dragons march together.

His purpose is plain. Aegon means to force battle before Loren can unite the western host with mine, then destroy our kingdoms separately as he destroyed Harren and Argilac. I have ordered the Reach banners to concentrate at Goldengrove, where the roads from Highgarden and Casterly Rock meet. Loren is already east of the Golden Tooth with every mounted man the westerlands can furnish.

When our armies join, fifty-five thousand soldiers will stand beneath green hand and golden lion: near five men for every one Aegon commands, thousands of armored knights, and enough archers to darken the sky. We cannot hide from dragons behind stone. We will spread across open ground, deny them a single target, and close upon Aegon's smaller host from every side.

fab_ac_west.0007.option1.text: Call every banner to Goldengrove. We meet the dragon together.

fab_ac_west.0009.desc.text:
My queens have come, Rhaenys up from Storm's End and Visenya from Crackclaw Point, and together we have raced the Two Kings to ground of my choosing: the wide, open plain south of the Blackwater, where the goldroad will run one day. No high ground, as Orys had at the Last Storm. No walls, no rivers, nothing to anchor my line - Mern means to sweep around both my flanks and drive his iron fist through my center, and on this ground he may well do it.

But mark the land, as I have marked it: grass and wheat from horizon to horizon, tall and ripe for harvest. There has been no rain for a fortnight. The day is cloudless - and windy.

#bold They have the numbers. We have the sky - and the field itself is a weapon lying in wait.#!

fab_ac_west.0009.option1.text: Draw the host into a crescent. And wait.

fab_ac_west.0010.desc.text:
Our charge broke their first rank. I saw Aegon's spears bend beneath the weight of the Reach, heard thousands shouting beneath the green hand, and knew the count had been right. His host was too small. His conquest would end here.

Then Balerion descended through the arrows. Vhagar came from the east and Meraxes from the west, not burning men but the dry fields around them. Summer wheat became a wall of flame. Wind drove it through our rear while dragonfire swept the front, trapping horse and foot beneath a sky turned black. Armor glowed red upon living men. The banners caught. The earth itself burned beneath us.

My sons are gone. My brothers are gone. Everywhere I turn, another green hand falls into the fire. Ten thousand years of Gardener blood end here, in one harvest of ash.

fab_ac_west.0011.desc.text:
They came on at the sound of their trumpets, beneath a sea of banners, and I will not pretend it was anything less than magnificent. King Mern himself led the charge against my center on his golden stallion, his son Gawen at his side bearing the great green hand upon its field of white. Roaring and screaming, urged on by horns and drums, the knights of the Reach and the Rock swept down upon my host through a storm of arrows - and my line could not hold them. The spearmen of my crescent were swept aside like chaff; my center was shattered; the iron fist punched through, and fifty-five thousand throats howled victory.

My men had only to bend, not break - Jon Mooton holds what is left of the line, and his archers are already falling back upwind, exactly as they were told.

For by then, my sisters and I were in the air.

#bold I took Balerion up through a storm of spears and stones and arrows, Vhagar and Meraxes rising on either wing - and beneath us the whole proud host of the Two Kings, spread across a tinder-dry field of wheat.#!

fab_ac_west.0012.desc.text:
I swept the length of their ranks upon Balerion, low enough to feel their arrows rattle from his scales, bathing the iron fist in flame again and again. But it was my queens who won the day: Rhaenys and Visenya set their fires upwind of the enemy and behind them, and the dry grass and the standing wheat went up all at once, faster than a man can run.

The wind did the rest. It fanned the flames into walls and drove the smoke into the faces of the advancing ranks. The scent of fire sent their mounts mad; as the smoke thickened, horse and rider alike were blinded, and the charge that was to crush me came apart into ten thousand men groping through a burning fog. Walls of fire rose on every side of them. Their proud sea of banners became a sea of flame.

And upwind, safe from the conflagration, Lord Mooton's men waited with their bows and spears, and made short work of the burned and burning men who came staggering out of the inferno.

#bold Fifty-five thousand men, and the Two Kings never brought me to battle at all. They brought me kindling.#!

fab_ac_west.0013.desc.text:
The Field of Fire, men are already calling it. There will never be another like it.

More than four thousand men died in the flames; another thousand fell to sword and spear and arrow; tens of thousands carry burns, some so cruel they will bear the scars to their graves. King Mern the Ninth lies among the dead, and with him his sons, his grandsons, his brothers, his cousins - the green hand burned root and branch. One nephew was pulled from the ashes alive; the maesters give him days, no more, and when he goes, House Gardener - the line of Garth Greenhand, the oldest royal house in Westeros - dies with him.

Loren Lannister lives. When he saw the day lost, the King of the Rock turned and rode straight through a wall of flame and smoke, and out the other side - the boldest thing any man did on that field, my own charge included. My outriders hunt him now.

Of my own host, we lost fewer than a hundred men. Visenya took an arrow in the shoulder; she pulled it out herself and called it a scratch. The dragons gorge themselves upon the dead.

#bold I have commanded that the swords of the slain be gathered, every one, and sent downriver to the Aegonfort. The pile grows.#!

fab_ac_west.0013.option1.text: Gather the swords of the slain.

fab_ac_west.0014.desc.text:
By every measure known to war, we had won. Our van shattered Aegon's lines, our horse rolled around his flanks, and tens of thousands pressed forward beneath lion and green hand. Then Balerion climbed into the sun, Vhagar and Meraxes beside him, and every measure ceased to matter.

The dragons did not burn our soldiers one rank at a time. They fired the dry grass behind us and turned the wind itself into a weapon. Flame ran faster than horses. Men threw down swords to claw at burning armor. King Mern is dead, his sons and brothers with him, and the ancient House Gardener has perished in a single afternoon.

I escaped through smoke thick enough to hide a king. Aegon's riders will find me soon. I may yield my crown and preserve my house, or flee to Casterly Rock and trust its mountain walls against the fire that destroyed Harrenhal.

fab_ac_west.0014.option1.text: A living lion may roar again. I will yield the crown.

fab_ac_west.0014.option2.text: Casterly Rock has never fallen. I will test his fire against stone.

fab_ac_west.0020.desc.text:
The war is lost, though the green fields did not become a pyre. Our companies are scattered, our roads lie open, and every raven brings another lord asking whether one more battle would save the Reach or merely feed more sons to the dragons. I know the answer, however bitterly.

Before Aegon's camp I remove the crown descended from Garth Greenhand and set it at his feet. He takes my crown but leaves me Highgarden, my line, and lordship over the Reach beneath his new throne. Thus ten thousand years of Gardener kingship ends not in extinction, but in submission.

A crown may be surrendered so that a people survive. The fields will be sown again. The Mander will still run, and the green hand will endure without a crown upon it.

fab_ac_west.0020.desc.submit.text: I have chosen the living Reach over a king's pride. Before dragonfire can turn our fields to ash, I remove the crown descended from Garth Greenhand and set it at Aegon Targaryen's feet. He takes my crown but leaves me Highgarden, my line, and lordship over the Reach beneath his new throne.\n\nTen thousand years of Gardener kingship end by my own hand, but the fields will be sown again. The Mander will still run, and the green hand will endure without a crown upon it.

fab_ac_west.0020.option1.text: By Our Hand, the Reach endures.

fab_ac_west.0021.text: The Last King of the Rock

fab_ac_west.0021.desc.text:
The heat still rises from the earth when I am led before Aegon Targaryen. Balerion waits behind him, black wings folded, while ash drifts across the ruin of the greatest army Westeros ever raised. No threat is spoken. None is needed.

I lay down my sword, remove the golden crown of the Rock, and place both at the conqueror's feet. Aegon accepts my submission, then returns my sword and raises me as Lord of Casterly Rock and Warden of the West. My crown is gone, but my lands, my children, and the rule of House Lannister remain mine.

The Gardeners wagered everything and left no heir to mourn them. I have purchased the future of my house with a crown. A Lannister pays his debts—and I will remember both the mercy granted today and the price demanded for it.

fab_ac_west.0021.desc.submit.text: Casterly Rock has never fallen, and I will not spend the lives of the west merely to prove its walls against dragonfire. I lay down my sword, remove the golden crown of the Rock, and place both at Aegon Targaryen's feet by my own decision.\n\nHe returns my sword and raises me as Lord of Casterly Rock and Warden of the West. My crown is gone, but my lands, my children, and the rule of House Lannister remain. I have purchased the future of my house with a crown, and a Lannister always pays his debts.

fab_ac_west.0021.option1.text: The crown is lost. The Rock and its lions endure.

fab_ac_west.0022.desc.text:
The king is dead. His sons are dead, his brothers, his cousins — every man of the green hand who rode to that cursed field is dead, and House Gardener has gone out of the world in a single afternoon of fire.

And I, who have kept this castle's accounts and stores and keys as my fathers kept them for the kings of old, now hold Highgarden with no king to hold it for. The conqueror's host is on the Roseroad. There is no army left in the Reach to slow it, let alone stop it.

I can open the gates and hand the dragon a jewel unburnt — or bar them, and make Highgarden a pyre for a dynasty already dead.

fab_ac_west.0022.option1.text: Open the gates. Highgarden must live.

fab_ac_west.0022.option2.text: Bar the gates, for the memory of King Mern!

fab_ac_west.0023.desc.text:
I gave the conqueror Highgarden whole — its gates open, its granaries full, its people unbloodied — and he has given it back to me.

Lord of Highgarden. Lord Paramount of the Mander. Warden of the South. Titles that were never meant for a steward's line, and half the old houses of the Reach will choke on every one of them. They rode to the Field of Fire, and my house kept the castle standing and the harvest coming in, which is what the Reach has ever actually needed of its masters.

House Tyrell owes the dragon everything. He will not find us forgetful.

fab_ac_west.0024.text: A New Lord of the Reach

fab_ac_west.0024.desc.text:
When my host came within sight of Highgarden, we found its gates already open and its walls unmanned. Harlan Tyrell, hereditary high steward of the Reach, came out to meet us on foot - and surrendered the greatest castle of the south without a sword drawn, its keys, its garrison, and its treasury entire. The green hand burned on the Field of Fire; its steward saw no profit in burning with it.

Now the greatest seat of the south is mine to bestow, and three names weigh in my councils. Harlan Tyrell, whose house has administered the Reach for generations while the Gardeners wore the crown - every lord of the Mander knows his seal and his fairness, and a steward raised high by the king's own hand breeds no pretenders. Lord Peake of Starpike, proud and hard, whose line boasts Gardener blood by old marriages and holds the marches that watch Dorne - those of my counsellors who mistrust upjumped household men speak his name loudest. And there is a third I did not look to find alive: a nephew of King Mern, the last living drop of Garth Greenhand's line, carried from the Field of Fire so burned that the maesters marvel he still draws breath. Give the boy the garden and the green hand grows again - if he lives, and if a realm won by fire will kneel to what fire so nearly unmade.

One power of the Reach still stands apart: Oldtown. The Hightowers sit behind the walls of the richest city in Westeros and have sent neither defiance nor homage - only silence, and watchers on their towers. The Old Man of Oldtown waits to see what the gods intend. He can wait a little longer.

#bold The garden must have a keeper. It falls to the dragon to choose him.#!

fab_ac_west.0024.option1.text: The rose shall tend the Reach.

fab_ac_west.0024.option2.text: Starpike has kept my peace in the marches. Peake shall keep the Reach.

fab_ac_west.0024.option3.text: The green hand shall grow again. Raise the last Gardener.

fab_ac_west.0025.desc.text:
It was done in the great hall of Highgarden, beneath banners still smelling faintly of smoke. Harlan Tyrell knelt as a steward, and I raised him with my own hands as Lord of Highgarden, Lord Paramount of the Mander and Warden of the South, to hold the whole of the Reach in my name.

He wept, I am told, though not before me. His house has kept this garden for other men's crowns since the days of the green kings; now the garden is theirs to keep for mine. The lords of the Mander came up one by one to do him homage - some gladly, for they know his fairness; some with their eyes on the burned fields and their thoughts kept prudently behind their teeth. The Florents of Brightwater knelt last and lowest, and I do not think they will forget the order of that kneeling. Neither will I.

One matter I settled quietly, after: the burned boy, Mern's nephew, I commended to the maesters' care with every kindness my camp could offer. What the fire began is beyond any man's mending. The green hand ends in a sickbed at Highgarden, tended by the servants of the house that inherits its garden.

#bold The rose shall tend what the green hand planted. And it will remember, always, whose gift the garden was.#!

fab_ac_west.0026.desc.text:
It was done in the great hall of Highgarden, beneath banners not its own. Lord Peake of Starpike knelt a marcher lord and rose Lord of Highgarden, Lord Paramount of the Mander and Warden of the South, to hold the whole of the Reach in my name.

My counsellors had their reasons, and they were sound ones: old blood, Gardener blood by marriage twice over, a strong seat in the marches that has watched Dorne for centuries, and a hardness the soft green heart of the Reach may need in the years I have planned for it. The Reach lords did homage in their turn - though I marked how many eyes went to Harlan Tyrell, standing quiet among them, the steward who opened the gates and was handed back only his stewardship. Peake will need to watch the rose as closely as he watches the sands.

One matter I settled quietly, after: the burned boy, Mern's nephew, I commended to the maesters' care with every kindness my camp could offer. What the fire began is beyond any man's mending. The green hand ends in a sickbed at Highgarden, in a castle that answers to Starpike now.

#bold Proud, hard, and mine by gratitude. The marches have come to the garden.#!

fab_ac_west.0027.desc.text:
It was done in the great hall of Highgarden, and half the court wept to see it. [fab_gardener_nephew.GetFirstName], nephew to King Mern, the last living drop of Garth Greenhand's line, was carried to the dais in a litter - he cannot yet stand unaided - and knelt by lowering his head alone. I raised him Lord of Highgarden, Lord Paramount of the Mander and Warden of the South, to hold in my name the garden his fathers planted.

The maesters tell me plainly he may not see the year's end; the fire that took his king and kin did not spare him so much as agree to wait. But he took the oath in a voice that did not shake, and when it was done the lords of the Reach knelt to a Gardener again - and meant it, every man of them, in a way no conqueror's grant could have made them mean it. If the Seven grant him years, the green hand grows again under the dragon's peace. If they do not, no man will say Aegon Targaryen let the line of the green kings end in a sickbed while its garden was given away above his head.

Harlan Tyrell keeps his stewardship, and serves the boy as his house has served Gardeners for three hundred years. Some things, it seems, survive even dragonfire.

#bold The green hand, grown from ash. The singers will make much of that.#!

fab_ac_west.0029.text: The West Must Have a Lord

fab_ac_west.0029.desc.text:
They took the King of the Rock on the morrow of the battle, and he has asked to kneel. Before I raise him, my counsellors would have me weigh what I am raising.

Loren Lannister rode against me beside Mern Gardener with all the gold-bought steel of the west at his back - and unlike Mern, he lives, because he had the wit to ride THROUGH my fire rather than stand in it. A proud man, a capable one, and the lords of the westerlands are long used to obeying the Rock. Confirm him, and the west changes masters in an afternoon and gives me no more trouble.

But there are other voices. The Reynes of Castamere are the second power of the west, red lions to Casterly's gold, rich from their mines and prouder than princes - and they were quick, very quick, to whisper that a king who fought the dragon might be better replaced by a house that would owe the dragon everything. There is wisdom in a lord paramount built entirely of gratitude. There is also the certainty that the Rock never forgets an insult.

#bold The gold lion or the red. The west will kneel either way - the question is to whom it kneels first.#!

fab_ac_west.0029.option1.text: Loren knelt while breath remained in him to choose. Confirm the Rock.

fab_ac_west.0029.option2.text: A red lion who owes me everything. Raise House Reyne.

fab_ac_west.0030.desc.text:
They took the King of the Rock on the morrow of the battle, not a day's ride from the field. He did not resist. He had ridden through fire to keep his freedom for one more night, and I think he spent it deciding what kind of man would kneel to me come morning.

A proud one, as it happens. Loren Lannister came before me with his back straight and soot still on his cloak, laid his sword and his crown together at my feet, bent the knee, and did me homage as King of All Westeros - the first of the great kings to do so while breath remained in him to choose. And I, true to the promise I have made all Westeros, raised my beaten foe back to his feet with my own hands. He keeps his lands and his lordship: Lord of Casterly Rock now, no longer a king, and Warden of the West besides, holding the westerlands in my name. His bannermen followed him to the knee, and after them a stream of Reach lords who survived the dragonfire, each gladder than the last that I make the kneeling easy.

The crown goes to my treasury. The sword goes downriver with all the others.

#bold The singers have found him a name already: Loren the Last. He wears it, they say, without complaint. He is alive to hear it - the wisdom of that name wants no explaining.#!

fab_ac_west.0031.desc.text:
It was done in the shadow of the Rock it humbled. The Lord of Castamere knelt a bannerman and rose Lord Paramount of the Westerlands and Warden of the West, to hold the west in my name - the first Reyne ever to outrank a Lannister, and well does he know it.

Loren the Last knelt in his turn and did homage to the man who was his vassal a fortnight past. He performed it correctly, word for word and gesture for gesture, with a face that might have been carved from the Rock itself. He keeps Casterly Rock and its gold, and his pride keeps whatever his pride can carry. I have raised a lord paramount who owes me everything and unmade a king who will owe me a grudge to his grave - my counsellors call it a fair trade, and from the Reyne's side of the scale it surely is.

The red lion banners already fly from Castamere to the sea. The gold lion flies over one castle now, and the west will spend a generation learning the new order of things - or testing it.

#bold Gold and red. So long as both kneel, the dragon need not care which lion roars louder.#!

fab_ac_west.0031.option1.text: In a coat of gold or a coat of red, a lion still has claws.

fab_ac_west.0032.text: The Green Hand Breaks the Dragon

fab_ac_west.0032.desc.text:
Aegon's host is in retreat beyond the borders of the Reach. The roads that carried his conquerors south now carry burned wagons, wounded men, and torn dragon banners back toward the Blackwater. Three dragons entered my kingdom. Not one of them won it.

We denied Aegon the battle he wanted, divided his smaller host, and struck wherever his beasts could not be everywhere at once. Every burned village raised another company against him; every fallen knight was replaced by ten spearmen from the next field. At last even dragons could not hold ground beneath an army that would not cease growing.

Highgarden's bells sound across the Mander. The crown of Garth Greenhand remains mine, and all Westeros now knows that the Targaryen is not destiny made flesh. The dragon can bleed. The dragon can fail.

fab_ac_west.0033.text: The Lion Prevails Over the Dragon

fab_ac_west.0033.desc.text:
The last of Aegon's banners has vanished beyond the Golden Tooth. The dragonlord who crossed Westeros as though kingdoms were lines upon his Painted Table has been driven from the westerlands, his host broken against the strength of the Rock.

Balerion darkened our skies and dragonfire scarred our fields, but Casterly Rock did not open its gates. Westermen who fled the Field of Fire returned to fight beneath the lion banner, and every victory drew more men from mine, hill, and harbor. Aegon has learned what Harren and Mern never lived to understand: dragons inspire terror, but terror alone cannot hold a kingdom determined to resist.

The crown remains upon my head. From Lannisport to the Golden Tooth, bells answer one another across the hills, and a single cry rises from the west—louder than the beat of dragon wings.

fab_ac_north.0001.desc.text:
Word comes north of the Neck at last, carried by traders and a merchant captain out of White Harbor: at Winterfell, King Torrhen Stark has called his banners.

They say he stood in the great hall of his forefathers, beneath eight thousand years of Stark kings, and raised Ice above his head - the greatsword of his house, Valyrian steel, older than any grudge in the North - and that the lords of winter roared until the rafters shook. Dustin and Bolton, Umber and Karstark, Manderly and Mormont and Flint: hard men from a hard country, none of whom has ever knelt to a power south of the Neck.

But the North is vast - larger than the other kingdoms of Westeros put together, and most of it empty. A muster of the North is not a thing of weeks; from the Last Hearth to the shores of the Sunset Sea, his lords must gather men across distances my southern foes cannot imagine. It will be many moons before the wolf can march.

#bold Whenever he comes, and however many he brings, the answer waiting for him will be the same.#!

fab_ac_north.0002.desc.text:
The south is falling. Not slowly, the way kingdoms fall in the old tales, but in months — the Storm King dead, Harren burned in his stones, the Reach turned to ash and the Rock on its knees. Every raven out of the Neck carries a worse tale than the last.

The North did not kneel to the Andals when all the south did. It has never knelt to anyone. Thirty thousand men are mustered at Moat Cailin, and I will lead them down the causeway myself.

I do not love this war. But a King in the North who lets the south be devoured piecemeal, and waits his turn behind the Neck, is no king at all.

fab_ac_north.0003.desc.text:
The word reached me at Highgarden, still smelling of the Field of Fire's ashes: Torrhen Stark has come down through the Neck at the head of thirty thousand northmen and entered the riverlands. The King in the North has managed his muster faster than I judged possible, and he marches hard for the Trident.

Every plan I had made for the south - Oldtown, the marches, Dorne - is set aside as of this hour. My host turns north with all the speed it can make, and I do not ride with it: I fly, ahead of them all, on Balerion's wings. The ravens go out before me - to Rhaenys, to Visenya, and to every lord who bent the knee after Harrenhal and the Field of Fire. Riverlord and stormlander, reachman and westerman, all of them owe their new king a war, and I mean to collect at the Trident.

#bold Torrhen brings thirty thousand. Let us show him what has become of everyone else who counted men against dragons.#!

fab_ac_north.0004.desc.text:
The Aegonfort is a poor seat for a king - timber walls and a mud yard above the three hills - but it is mine, and from its ramparts I have decided the last great matter of the Conquest. The North will kneel, as the rest have knelt.

My ravens went north days ago, and the North has answered in the only tongue the Starks have ever spoken to would-be conquerors. Torrhen Stark has come down through the Neck at the head of thirty thousand northmen and crossed into the riverlands, marching hard for the Trident. The King in the North has mustered faster than I judged possible - but muster he did, and now the matter will be settled in the field, or beneath a dragon's shadow.

I do not ride with the host. I fly, ahead of them all, on Balerion's wings, and the ravens go out before me - to Rhaenys, to Visenya, and to every lord who has bent the knee. Riverlord and stormlander, reachman and westerman, all of them owe their king a war, and I mean to collect at the Trident.

#bold Torrhen brings thirty thousand. Let us show him what became of everyone else who counted men against dragons.#!

fab_ac_north.0005.desc.text:
The wolf has reached the Trident and found the dragon waiting.

Torrhen Stark's thirty thousand stand upon the northern bank. Across the water I have five-and-forty thousand: riverlords who remember Harrenhal, stormlanders beneath my Hand's crowned stag, and men of the Reach and westerlands who watched two kings burn upon the Field of Fire. Balerion, Vhagar, and Meraxes wheel above us where every northman may count them.

Between the hosts stands a weathered inn. All night greybeards and maesters pass through its doors bearing words from the northern camp. Some of Torrhen's lords urge him to yield his crown and save his people. Others bid him fall back behind Moat Cailin, and Brandon Snow whispers of a weirwood bow, a boat, and sleeping dragons.

Dawn comes cold upon the river. The door of the inn opens, and the King in the North steps forth with his answer.

fab_ac_north.0005.option1.text: Torrhen lays Ice at my feet. The North kneels.

fab_ac_north.0005.option2.text: Winter is coming, he says. Then war will decide.

fab_ac_north.0005.option2.tt.text: The conquest war continues. Brandon Snow will attempt to slay one of the three dragons, with a #V 10%#! chance of success.

fab_ac_north.0006.desc.text:
The nearer we march, the worse the truth of it. I had heard the tales and trimmed them by half, as a sensible man does — and the truth is worse than the tales. A host five times the dragon's number burned in an afternoon. The riverlords who were to rise with us kneel to him instead, and his army across the Trident is larger than mine, with three dragons above it.

My bannermen thunder about honour and the blood of the First Men. And my bastard brother Brandon offers something else: he swears that with a weirwood bow and a night's darkness he can cross the river and put a shaft through a sleeping dragon's eye.

Sons, brothers, the whole strength of the North — I can spend it all on one cast of the dice, or I can treat with the dragon while I still have a host to treat with.

fab_ac_north.0006.option1.text: We treat. I will not burn the North for my pride.

fab_ac_north.0006.option2.text: The North stands. Brandon goes tonight.

fab_ac_north.0007.desc.text:
All night Brandon and my three wisest maesters crossed and recrossed the Trident, carrying my terms and his. By dawn it was done, and I did what I brought thirty thousand men south to avoid — and what I brought them south, in the end, to survive.

I knelt in the mud of the riverbank, laid Ice at his feet, and gave the Crown of Winter into the conqueror's hands. He raised me up as Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North, and my men marched home again — every one of them alive.

The singers will not be kind. The King Who Knelt, they will call me, and my own lords will say it in their cups for as long as I live. The Field of Fire has a longer list of names, and every name on it is dead.

fab_ac_north.0007.option1.text: Let them call me the King Who Knelt. My men are alive.

fab_ac_north.0008.text: A Bow, a Boat, a Night

fab_ac_north.0008.desc.text:
It is done — Brandon slipped from the camp at moonset with his weirwood bow and two silent men, making for the dark of the far bank where the beasts sleep among the conqueror's tents.

If the gods of our fathers are watching, by dawn one of the dragons is dead, and every man in Westeros learns they can die. If they are not watching, I have spent my brother.

Theon Stark was given worse odds against the Andals, the old tales say, and the Hungry Wolf fed. But the Andals did not have dragons, and I find the night very long.

fab_ac_north.0008.option1.text: Gods of my fathers, watch over him.

fab_ac_north.0009.desc.text:
By the old gods and the new ones too — he did it.

A dragon is dead. Brandon's shaft found its eye in the dark, and the scream of it woke both camps and will wake the whole world after. The beasts of Valyria can die, and it was a bastard of Winterfell with a weirwood bow who proved it.

The dragon's camp is in uproar and my own is roaring Brandon's name. Whatever comes now — and the conqueror's wroth will come — the spell is broken. Sound the horns. If we must fight the storm that follows, we fight it as the first men in three hundred years to know that dragons bleed.

fab_ac_north.0009.option1.text: Dragons can die. Now the world knows.

fab_ac_north.0010.desc.text:
They found what the fire left on the far bank at first light. My brother is dead.

Brandon reached the sleeping beasts — reached them, mind, past every guard the conqueror had — and the shaft flew, and the dragon woke. There is nothing to bury. There is a bow of white weirwood, half-charred, that some brave fool of his men carried back across the river, and I will keep it until I die.

The conqueror's host is stirring and his beasts are in the sky, angry now. I must make what defence I can, knowing it cannot be enough — and knowing that one word of treaty from me, a day sooner, and my brother would be standing at my shoulder still.

fab_ac_north.0010.option1.text: Rest now, brother. The weirwoods keep you.

fab_ac_north.0011.desc.text:
They came across the river at dusk under a peace banner: Brandon Snow, the King in the North's bastard brother, with three maesters in his company. The same man, my scouts swear, who offered to swim the Trident by night and cut the throats of my dragons - sent instead to treat with me. All through the night the messages went back and forth across the dark water, terms drafted and redrafted by candlelight, and I will say this for the northmen: they haggled over their honor, never their lives.

Come morning, Torrhen Stark crossed the Trident. He came before me on the southern bank, in sight of both hosts, and knelt in the river mud. He laid his sword at my feet, and set beside it the Crown of Winter - the ancient crown of the Kings of the North, out of the Age of Heroes, surrendered whole where every other crown in Westeros has had to be burned or beaten from its wearer's brow.

He rises Lord of Winterfell and Warden of the North, his lands and rights affirmed, his people unburned. Thirty thousand northmen will march home to their wives because their king had the courage to bend. Men are already calling him the King Who Knelt, and some of his own lords say it with scorn.

#bold They should say it kneeling. Torrhen Stark saved more lives today than most kings save in a lifetime of ruling.#!

fab_ac_north.0011.option1.text: Torrhen Stark chose his people over his crown.

fab_ac_north.0012.desc.text:
The scream tears me from sleep before the horns begin. Beyond the inn, men flee from a mountain of wings and blood. [global_var:fab_north_slain_dragon.GetName] lies dead upon the riverbank, a white weirwood shaft buried in one great eye.

Brandon Snow crossed the Trident beneath the moon, passed my sentries, and did what every king in Westeros deemed impossible. One of the three dragons who forged my victories will never fly again. Across the water the northmen roar his name, believing the spell of Valyria broken.

Two dragons remain, and two dragons are enough to melt the snows from Moat Cailin to the Wall. House Stark chose blood when I offered the knee. I shall answer in the words of my house.

fab_ac_north.0012.option1.text: Two dragons remain. The North will pay in fire and blood.

fab_ac_north.0013.desc.text:
The alarm is raised in the darkest hour. Brandon Snow has crossed the river with a weirwood bow and crept among the dragons, meaning to loose a shaft into a sleeping eye. He comes close enough to wake one. That is all.

Dragonflame turns night to day. By dawn the bastard's charred bow hangs before my pavilion, and all three dragons are aloft. Torrhen has spent his boldest brother and gained nothing but a tale of failure.

There is no need to make a second Harrenhal of the North. Its king and host stand before me, and I will break those first. Winterfell may yet be spared if the wolf learns obedience upon the field.

fab_ac_north.0013.option1.text: Break his host. Leave the North something worth ruling.

fab_ac_north.0014.desc.text:
The northern host is broken, its king at my mercy. Torrhen Stark kneels where he once meant to give battle, Ice laid naked before him and the battered crown of winter beside it. His lords kneel more slowly. Some do not look at him at all.

The North is too vast to rule from the Blackwater. One house must speak with my voice beyond the Neck, call the banners in my wars, and keep the king's peace through the long winters. House Stark has held these lands for thousands of years, and even defeated wolves command old loyalties. Yet the Dreadfort is strong, and the Boltons have long known how to master fearful men. White Harbor offers ships, silver, and House Manderly's gratitude, though many will remember that its lords came north as exiles from the Reach.

A crown has been taken. A wardenship remains to be bestowed.

fab_ac_north.0014.option1.text: The Starks keep Winterfell and the wardenship.

fab_ac_north.0014.option1.tt.text: House Stark retains the lord paramountcy of the North beneath the Iron Throne.

fab_ac_north.0014.option2.text: Give the North to House Bolton. Fear will keep it quiet.

fab_ac_north.0014.option2.tt.text: The Lord of the Dreadfort receives the lord paramountcy of the North. Torrhen Stark and the northern lords must swear to House Bolton.

fab_ac_north.0014.option3.text: Raise House Manderly. The North needs loyal ships and silver.

fab_ac_north.0014.option3.tt.text: The Lord of White Harbor receives the lord paramountcy of the North. Torrhen Stark and the northern lords must swear to House Manderly.

fab_ac_north.0015.desc.text:
Winterfell's great hall was raised for kings. Smoke gathers among the ancient rafters, and the stone kings in the crypts lie beneath us, but the battered crown of winter rests upon the flagstones below my seat. No living brow shall wear it again.

[fab_north_warden.GetTitledFirstName], of House [fab_north_warden.GetHouse.GetName], comes forward beneath the eyes of the assembled northmen. I grant [fab_north_warden.GetHerHim] no crown, only the obedience of the northern lords and the wardenship of every cold mile from the Neck to the Wall. Whether this is the ruler first named after the battle or the heir whom war and death have placed before me matters little. The title rests upon [fab_north_warden.GetHerHim], and [fab_north_warden.GetSheHe] must swear the oath.

One by one the northmen follow [fab_north_warden.GetHerHim] to their knees. Some bow for old loyalties, some for fear, and some because they remember three dragons above the Trident. Their reasons are their own. Their oath is mine.

#bold The crown is gone. The North remains, and its Warden answers to the Iron Throne.#!

fab_ac_north.0015.option1.text: Rise, [fab_north_warden.GetFirstName]. Guard the North in my name.

fab_ac_north.0016.desc.text:
It is over. The host of the North is broken, the causeway is lost behind me, and the dragons circle where they please. Nothing remains between the conqueror and Winterfell but the miles.

So the last choice left to a King in the North is the manner of the ending. I choose the knee. Not for myself — my pride died with my host — but for every northern village the beasts have not yet found.

Eight thousand years, and it ends with me. I can only pray the dragon is as measured in victory as he has been terrible in war.

fab_ac_north.0016.desc.submit.text: The dragon has crossed into my realm, but the North is not yet broken. I choose the knee before it must be. Not for myself, but for every northern village the beasts have not yet found and every son who need not die proving that fire burns in winter.\n\nEight thousand years of kingship end with my decision. The crown is lost, but the North endures.

fab_ac_vale.0001.desc.text:
A crown wants ports, and the finest port of the east that is not yet mine is Gulltown, the Vale's great city on its bay. While my host settles the matter of the river and the storm, the sea shall carry the war to the Arryns.

I have given the royal fleet to Daemon Velaryon, Lord of the Tides - the master of the greatest war fleet in the narrow sea, my mother's own blood, and the finest sailor ever to weigh anchor off Driftmark. With him goes Visenya upon Vhagar, so that whatever the Arryns muster against him will fight beneath a dragon's shadow. Their orders are simple: take Gulltown, and give the Vale a war on its doorstep.

The Eyrie will not sit idle - our friends across the water write that Sharra Arryn is stripping every port in the Vale to piece a fleet together, and that a dozen Braavosi warships have taken her coin to stiffen it. I will be waiting.

#bold The dragon rules the sky, and Velaryon blood has ruled the narrow sea for a hundred years. What is one hired fleet against that?#!

fab_ac_vale.0001.option1.text: Take Gulltown, my lord of the Tides.

fab_ac_vale.0002.text: The Battle in the Waters off Gulltown

fab_ac_vale.0002.desc.text:
The sea has taught me the lesson the land never dared: the dragon can lose.

The fleets met in the waters off Gulltown - Daemon's war galleys against the Arryns' patched-together strength and their twelve Braavosi hulls. The Braavosi made the difference: purple sails and iron rams, crews bred to war at sea, and captains who did not panic at the sight of a dragon overhead. They broke our line, boarded flagship after flagship, and tore the royal fleet apart plank from plank.

Daemon Velaryon is dead. The Lord of the Tides, the strong right arm of my house upon the sea, my own mother's kin - cut down on his burning deck with his fleet dying around him. Half the strength of Driftmark has gone to the bottom of the bay with him.

#bold The ravens fly to the Eyrie tonight with congratulations, no doubt. The Arryns may savor them. Visenya was above that battle - and Visenya does not forgive.#!

fab_ac_vale.0002.option1.text: Daemon of the Tides. The sea keep him.

fab_ac_vale.0003.desc.text:
The Arryn fleet outlived my own by the better part of an hour.

Visenya watched the royal fleet die from Vhagar's back - and then she came down upon the victors while their crews were still cheering. Back and forth across the bay she flew, unhurried as a farmwife firing stubble, and set the Arryn fleet alight ship by ship: the hulks, the galleys, the proud Braavosi warships with their purple sails. The men of Gulltown watched from their walls as every hull that had won the battle burned to the waterline in the hour after it.

So the singers may call it what they wish. Two fleets sailed into the waters off Gulltown, and no fleet sailed out: a drawn battle, by the arithmetic of hulls. But Gulltown stands untaken behind its walls, and I have no fleet left to take it with - and that makes it a defeat, whatever the singers sing. The first of this war. I mean for it to be the last.

#bold The Vale has bought itself time, at the price of every ship it owns. Let us see what that costs them.#!

fab_ac_vale.0003.option1.text: A victory that leaves no fleet is no victory.

fab_ac_vale.0004.desc.text:
The cost of the Vale's burned fleet has come due already - and it is the Arryns who pay it.

Word comes down the Bite: the Three Sisters have risen. The Sistermen - wreckers, smugglers and fisherfolk who never loved the Eyrie's rule - watched the last Arryn hull burn off Gulltown and understood that no falcon fleet remained to hold them. They cast the Vale's men into the sea, declared their islands free of Mountain and Vale, and raised Marla Sunderland, Lady of Sisterton, as their queen. A crown of the Sisters, worn by a Sunderland - the first in a thousand years.

Sharra Arryn can do precisely nothing about it. Her fleet is ash on the water; the Sisters might as well be across the world. And I confess the arrangement suits me for the present: every man the Eyrie loses is one fewer at the Bloody Gate when my turn comes.

#bold The little queen may keep her wet rocks a while. Crowns put on in a season of chaos have a way of coming off in the season of order - and order is coming.#!

fab_ac_vale.0004.option1.text: One rebellion at a time. The Vale first.

fab_ac_vale.0005.desc.text:
One crown yet stands in open defiance between the Wall and the marches, and it sits on the brow of a wrecker-queen on a wet rock in the Bite. The anointing oils are scarcely dry on my own; it is time Marla Sunderland's came off.

I have given the task to [fab_north_warden.GetFirstName], my Warden of the North - it is [fab_north_warden.GetHerHis] shores her wreckers plague, and it will do the realm good to see the North answer a threat so near its own doorstep. The Vale's fleet is still timber in the shipyards after Gulltown, so the North goes to sea on hired keels: Ser Warrick Manderly leads the northern host down the Bite on galleys engaged from Braavos - the same city whose warships sank my fleet now ferries my armies, for the Braavosi sail for whoever pays. The Eyrie sends what strength it has; White Harbor sails with its own.

And above them all goes Visenya on Vhagar. The Sistermen watched her burn a victorious fleet to the waterline. They will think on that as the sails fill the horizon.

#bold The last crown of the Conquest sits on the smallest throne. Bring it to me.#!

fab_ac_vale.0006.desc.text:
There was no battle. There was barely an argument.

When the Sistermen looked out from Sisterton and saw the horizon full of sails - Ser Warrick Manderly's hired Braavosi galleys black with northern spears, White Harbor's ships behind them, and Visenya circling above it all on Vhagar - the rebellion ended between one tide and the next. They had heard what Vhagar did to a fleet that WON its battle. They did not care to learn what she did to towns.

The Sistermen deposed their queen themselves. Marla Sunderland was delivered up by her own lords, and her younger brother Steffon raised in her place - and Lord Steffon knelt on the strand and yielded the Three Sisters to the Iron Throne and to the Eyrie, whose charge they shall remain. House Manderly takes one of his sons as ward and hostage; House Arryn takes the other. The Sisters will keep faith, one way or the other.

As for the queen of a single winter: she has exchanged her crown for the grey. Marla Sunderland goes to the silent sisters - a mercy, my counsellors call it, and so it is. The silent sisters do not talk of treason. They do not talk at all.

#bold So ends the last crown raised against me. The realm is one - and so it will stay.#!

fab_ac_vale.0006.option1.text: The grey becomes her better than the crown.

fab_ac_vale.0006.desc.kinsman.text:
There was no battle. There was barely an argument.

When the Sistermen looked out from Sisterton and saw the horizon full of sails - hired Braavosi galleys black with northern spears, White Harbor's ships behind them, and Visenya circling above it all on Vhagar - the rebellion ended between one tide and the next. They had heard what Vhagar did to a fleet that WON its battle. They did not care to learn what she did to towns.

The Sistermen deposed their queen themselves. Marla Sunderland was delivered up by her own lords. Her brother Steffon, who ought to have been raised in her place, is dead - so the lordship passes to [fab_sisters_heir.GetFirstName] of her own house, who knelt on the strand and yielded the Three Sisters to the Iron Throne and to the Eyrie, whose charge they shall remain. Hostages of Sunderland blood go to White Harbor and the Eyrie both. The Sisters will keep faith, one way or the other.

As for the queen of a single winter: she has exchanged her crown for the grey. Marla Sunderland goes to the silent sisters - a mercy, my counsellors call it, and so it is. The silent sisters do not talk of treason. They do not talk at all.

#bold So ends the last crown raised against me. The realm is one - and so it will stay.#!

fab_ac_vale.0006.desc.attainted.text:
There was no battle. There was barely an argument.

When the Sistermen looked out from Sisterton and saw the horizon full of sails - hired Braavosi galleys black with northern spears, White Harbor's ships behind them, and Visenya circling above it all on Vhagar - the rebellion ended between one tide and the next. They had heard what Vhagar did to a fleet that WON its battle. They did not care to learn what she did to towns.

The Sistermen deposed their queen themselves. Marla Sunderland was delivered up by her own lords - and behind her stands no one. Her brother Steffon is dead, and with him the last of the Sunderland line; the rebellion has eaten the house that raised it. The Three Sisters pass to the Eyrie's keeping directly, as they were before this madness of a winter crown.

As for the queen herself: she has exchanged her crown for the grey. Marla Sunderland goes to the silent sisters - a mercy, my counsellors call it, and so it is. The silent sisters do not talk of treason. They do not talk at all.

#bold So ends the last crown raised against me. The realm is one - and so it will stay.#!

fab_ac_vale.0007.desc.text:
Everyone in the Eyrie whispers about the dragons now. Kingdoms keep falling and falling, and Mother and the lords sit in council all day with the doors shut, and no one will tell me anything because I am eight.

But I listened at the door. Mother is sending the dragon king a letter — she has offered to MARRY him, and the letter says that since he has no sons, he should make ME his heir!

Heir to all of Westeros. Ser Marwyn says I should not get my hopes up, that it is only Mother buying time. But think of it! I would have the Vale AND everything else, and a dragon would come to my wedding.

fab_ac_vale.0007.option1.text: Now we wait for the dragonlord's answer.

fab_ac_vale.0008.desc.text: The falcon has seen which way the wind blows. A raven from the Eyrie brings word from Sharra Arryn, Queen Regent of the Vale - and this time she does not write of alliances between equals. The kings who defied me are dead or kneeling, and the Vale has no wish to join them; what she offers now is submission. Of a kind.\n\n

fab_ac_vale.0008.option1.text: No marriage. Visenya will answer the Eyrie - her own way.

fab_ac_vale.0008.option2.text: I will wed Sharra. The boy is my heir - until I have a son.

fab_ac_vale.0008.option2.heir.text: I will wed Sharra, but the Iron Throne already has its heir.

fab_ac_vale.0008.option2.heir_tt.text: [fab_ac_eyrie_boy.GetFirstName] will not be named heir: the King already has children of his own blood.

fab_ac_vale.0008.option3.text: #S The Vale shall be won as all the rest: with Fire and Blood. #!

fab_ac_vale.0008.desc.early.text: The falcon has seen which way the wind blows. A raven from the Eyrie brings word from Sharra Arryn, Queen Regent of the Vale - and this time she does not write of alliances between equals. Kings still stand against me, crowns still on their heads - but the Queen Regent does not mean to wait and learn whether they fare better than those already fallen. What she offers now, before any dragon has so much as turned toward her mountains, is submission. Of a kind.\n\n

fab_ac_vale.0008.desc.terms.text: For her terms come wrapped in silk. The Vale will bend the knee, she writes - if I take her to wife, and name her boy Ronnel my heir. My heir! I, who lack a son, am to promise my conquest to the falcon's chick. And folded within the letter, once more, a portrait: the Flower of the Mountain, the singers of the Vale name her, and the painter has been diligent in earning his fee. She is a handsome woman, I will grant - and ten years my senior, and those who name her the fairest in Westeros have plainly never once looked upon a Valyrian.\n\n

fab_ac_vale.0008.desc.terms.heir.text: For her terms come wrapped in silk. The Vale will bend the knee, she writes - if I take her to wife, and name her boy Ronnel my heir. My heir! As though the Iron Throne had no heirs of my own blood already, she would set the falcon's chick above them. And folded within the letter, once more, a portrait: the Flower of the Mountain, the singers of the Vale name her, and the painter has been diligent in earning his fee. She is a handsome woman, I will grant - and ten years my senior, and those who name her the fairest in Westeros have plainly never once looked upon a Valyrian.\n\n

fab_ac_vale.0008.desc.close.text: Still, I do not laugh. Behind that letter stands the one kingdom left that has never been conquered: the Bloody Gate that has broken every host ever sent against it, and the Eyrie above the clouds, which no enemy has taken in six thousand years. Pride wrote those terms - but stone and sky will enforce them, if I answer wrongly.\n\n#bold A widow's hand, a mountain kingdom, and a boy on a too-large throne. There is more than one way to take the Vale.#!

fab_ac_vale.0009.desc.text:
Mother married him! The dragon king is my good-father now, and I am to be his heir just as the letter asked, and NOBODY in the Vale has to fight anybody.

Maester Quince says I must be solemn about it because it is a great matter of state. I am trying very hard to be solemn.

But he has a DRAGON. The biggest one, the black one. And when I am bigger, perhaps he will let me ride it.

fab_ac_vale.0009.desc.no_heir.text:
Mother married him! The dragon king is my good-father now, and NOBODY in the Vale has to fight anybody.

I am not to be his heir after all. He has children of his own already, and Maester Quince says that was always the part of the letter a king would never agree to. He says I must be solemn about it anyway, because it is still a great matter of state. I am trying very hard to be solemn.

But he has a DRAGON. The biggest one, the black one. And when I am bigger, perhaps he will let me ride it.

fab_ac_vale.0009.option1.text: I shall fly above the whole world!

fab_ac_vale.0010.desc.text:
Mother put soldiers everywhere. Gulltown got new walls, and a whole army sat in the Bloody Gate, and Stone and Snow and Sky had three times the men, and everyone said the Eyrie was the safest castle in the world because no army can climb the Giant's Lance.

Only the lady did not bring an army. I was at my lessons when the whole sky went dark and the biggest dragon in the world landed right in the middle of the garden, and sat there folding its wings like our falcons do.

The lady in armour let me sit on her knee and look at it up close. It smells like hot iron and its eyes are like the big kettle-fires. Then Mother came running out with all her guards and went white as milk. The lady just smiled at her. And I asked — Mother, can I go flying with the lady?

fab_ac_vale.0010.option1.text: Give her the crown! I want to go flying!

fab_ac_vale.0010.option2.text: No. I am the king, and kings keep their crowns.

fab_ac_vale.0011.desc.text:
Visenya reached the Eyrie and met young King Ronnel within its own garden. The boy longed to fly upon Vhagar, but Visenya made clear that such a gift would follow only after the Vale submitted. Queen Regent Sharra refused the demand. 
 
Rather than strike at the child, Visenya turned against the regency that sustained his resistance. Sharra is dead, and the Vale has been left to find another hand to govern it. 
 
A wiser regent may yet accept peace. Until then, our armies must look toward the Bloody Gate.

fab_ac_vale.0011.option1.text: Their refusal buys only another war.

fab_ac_vale.0012.desc.text:
Visenya's raven from the Vale reads more like a jest than a report of conquest - and yet the Vale is mine.

Sharra Arryn had done everything a regent should. The Bloody Gate was manned and provisioned; a host stood ready in the Gates of the Moon; the Eyrie itself, which no enemy has ever taken, was stocked for a siege of years. So my sister did not trouble with any of it. Vhagar rose above the Giant's Lance and came down in the Eyrie's own garden - and when the Queen Regent came rushing to her son, she found the boy king of Mountain and Vale seated in Visenya's lap, staring up at the dragon in wonder. #italic 'Mother,'#! he asked her, #italic 'can I go flying with the lady?'#!

Sharra Arryn looked at her child in the dragon-queen's arms, and understood everything that mattered in a single heartbeat. She surrendered the crowns of House Arryn and pledged the Vale's fealty on the spot - and Visenya, who keeps every promise she makes, granted young Ronnel his wish. The boy flew with her upon Vhagar, thrice around the summit of the Giant's Lance, and came back to his mother laughing.

House Arryn shall rule henceforth not as kings, but as Lords of the Eyrie and Wardens of the East. The smallfolk have already found the boy his name: the King Who Flew.

#bold A kingdom no army has ever conquered, won for the price of a dragon ride. Visenya will never let me forget it.#!

fab_ac_vale.0012.option1.text: A crown for a dragon ride.

fab_ac_vale.0013.desc.text:
It is done. The knights of the Vale fought as bravely as any men in Westeros, and it made no difference at all — walls and passes and high places mean nothing to an enemy that owns the sky.

The crowns of Mountain and Vale, worn since the Falcon Knight, are surrendered. We kneel, we swear, we serve. House Arryn keeps the Eyrie and the wardenship of the East, which is more than the defeated are usually given, and I am old enough now to understand that we are fortunate in our conqueror.

As High as Honour, my house has always said. There is honour in keeping faith with a sworn king, too. We will learn it.

fab_ac_vale.0013.desc.submit.text: The Vale's passes remain guarded and the Eyrie remains unbroken, but neither can bar a dragon from the sky. I choose to surrender the crowns of Mountain and Vale before courage becomes only a longer tally of graves.\n\nWe kneel, we swear, and House Arryn keeps the Eyrie beneath Aegon's new throne. As High as Honour, my house has always said. There is honour in preserving those placed in my care.

fab_ac_vale.0014.desc.text:
The Eyrie was said to be beyond conquest. Its towers stand above the clouds, pale against the empty sky, and every winding mile beneath them was bought with blood: the Bloody Gate broken, the Gates of the Moon yielded, and the mountain road opened beneath the shadow of dragons.

Now I sit in the Arryns' high hall with the blue sky beyond its narrow arches. The crowns of Mountain and Vale lie at my feet. [fab_vale_warden.GetTitledFirstName], of House [fab_vale_warden.GetHouse.GetName], kneels where falcon kings once received the homage of lesser men. Whether [fab_vale_warden.GetSheHe] began this war or inherited its ruin matters no more than the names of the dead below. The living must answer for the realm they inherit.

The lords of the Vale kneel after [fab_vale_warden.GetHerHim], proud men bowing stiffly in mail still scarred by the campaign. I leave them their ancient houses, their mountain keeps, and an Arryn Warden if Arryn blood yet holds the title. What I take is their kingship. The falcon may still fly above the Eyrie, but never again above the dragon.

#bold Even the highest castle in Westeros must look upward when dragons pass overhead.#!

fab_ac_vale.0014.option1.text: Rise, [fab_vale_warden.GetFirstName]. Hold the East for the Iron Throne.

fab_ac_vale.0015.desc.text:
A raven from the king's court: Aegon has a son of his own.

Mother's letter said I would be the dragon's heir until that day came, and now it has come, and the heralds have already stopped speaking my name after his. Maester Quince says a promise with an ending is still a promise kept, and that the Vale is no smaller today than it was yesterday.

It is not smaller. It only feels it.

fab_ac_vale.0015.a.text: The Vale was always mine. It still is.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0001.desc.text:
While the Seven Kingdoms feast on the King's Peace, the Iron Islands devour themselves.

When Harren and his line burned, the ironborn on the green lands tried to go home - and the rivermen they had scourged for three generations fell upon them on every road and river mouth, so that few enough ever saw the sea again. On the isles themselves, chaos crowned a dozen heads. Qhorin Volmark, a lord of Harlaw whose grandmother was sister to Harwyn Hardhand, declared himself Harren's rightful heir and king. The priests of the Drowned God would not have him: on Old Wyk they pressed a driftwood crown upon Lodos, a barefoot holy man who names himself the Drowned God's own son. More kings yet sprouted on Great Wyk, on Orkmont, on Pyke.

For above a year they have butchered one another on the islands and across the Sunset Sea. Orkmont's king is already slain. The traders tell of wrecks and corpse-choked tides, and swear that hundreds of krakens have risen to feast on the dead.

#bold I did not break eight kings to suffer a dozen more. The last war of the Conquest begins now - and the fleets of Lannisport and Highgarden, the Arbor and Bear Island sail with the dragon.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0001.option1.text: One realm. One king. The isles as well.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0002.desc.text:
Word comes from the fleets, and it is the strangest dispatch of any war I have fought.

As the sails of Lannisport and Highgarden, the Arbor and Bear Island darkened the western sea, the priest-king Lodos gathered his faithful upon the shore of Old Wyk and called upon his father, the Drowned God, to break the invaders. He stretched out his arms, my captains write, and bade the krakens of the deep rise and drag every ship of the green lands down to the drowned halls.

The faithful watched the water. The sea rolled, and shone, and did nothing at all. Not one kraken rose; not one hull so much as scraped its keel. The fleets came on through a calm sea and fair wind, and the god's son stood dripping on his beach in silence.

#bold Balerion, at least, answers when I call. We press on for Great Wyk.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0002.option1.text: The deep keeps its own counsel.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0003.desc.text:
Great Wyk is ours, and the isles are breaking - and now Qhorin Volmark has come out to end this war the only way his fathers ever knew.

The self-crowned king of the ironborn has landed with his household axes and sent his challenge to my camp: the Old Way, king against king, blade against blade, before both hosts. He is no fool - his cause drowns a little more with every tide, and a dead dragon is the only thing left that can float it. And he is no weakling either: a hard man of the old blood of Hardhand, with an axe that has fed the Drowned God well this past year.

Tired of the fighting, half the isles already whisper for peace; the other half waits only to see whether the dragon dares. I did not cross the Sunset Sea to answer an ironman's challenge with a shield wall.

#bold Blackfyre has drunk nothing since the Field of Fire. The ironborn will see how a king answers.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0005.desc.text:
It was done before both hosts, on the strand of Great Wyk, in the old way that the ironborn hold holier than any sept or septon.

Qhorin Volmark came at me the way his fathers came at the world: roaring, axe swinging, certain the deep was with him. He was strong, and fast for all his bulk, and for a few strokes the ironborn dared to hope. Then Blackfyre turned his axe-haft, and turned it again, and the third exchange opened him from shoulder to breastbone. Valyrian steel keeps no accounts and grants no seconds. The last king of Harwyn Hardhand's blood died on the sand with his crown rolling in the surf.

And the ironborn - these iron men who have terrorized every coast of Westeros since the dawn of days - looked on their dead king, and knelt. The claimants on Great Wyk and Pyke bent the knee before nightfall, racing each other to be first. However this war lingers on paper, it ended on that beach.

#bold They wanted the Old Way. They received it.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0005.option1.text: The Old Way is done. So are its kings.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0006.desc.text:
I will write it plainly, for the singers will not: Qhorin Volmark had the better of me.

We met on the strand of Great Wyk before both hosts, in the old way, and the ironman's axe was every terrible thing his reputation promised. He turned Blackfyre twice, staggered me a third time, and only the quickness of my guard - and, I will own it, of my own feet - carried me back to my lines with my life. The ironborn howled their god's name until the cliffs rang with it.

A duel is a duel; a war is a war. His axe cannot sink my fleets, nor feed his starving isles, nor conjure back the year of blood that brought him his driftwood crown. The blockade holds, the sieges grind on, and the dragon is not required to be gallant twice.

#bold The Old Way won the beach. The new way will win the isles.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0006.option1.text: A duel is not a war.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0007.desc.text:
The priest-king Lodos has answered for his silent krakens.

When word of the war's turning reached Old Wyk, the son of the Drowned God did not flee, nor treat, nor fight. He walked down to the shore where he had once called the krakens, filled his robes with stones, and told his faithful he was going below to take counsel with his father. Then he walked into the sea, and kept walking until the water closed over his head.

Thousands of his followers did the same. For days the tides have carried the drowned back onto the strands of Old Wyk, and the maesters say they will wash ashore for years to come. Of Lodos himself, no body has been found - and I suspect none ever shall be. Already the ignorant whisper that he sits at his father's right hand, and will return.

#bold He may keep his counsel in the drowned halls. The isles above the water are mine.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0007.option1.text: What is dead may stay dead.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0008.desc.text:
The war of the isles is ended. The last claimants knelt on the sands of Pyke and Great Wyk; the driftwood crowns are ash or ocean-bottom; and the ironborn have relinquished, forever, every claim their kings once pressed upon the riverlands. The Isles-and-Rivers of Harwyn Hardhand are unmade for all time.

But the islands themselves must be governed, and there my counsellors divide. Some would set the lion over them: Casterly Rock is near, rich, and eager, and the ironborn fear Lannisport's fleet already. Some would give them to the wolf: the North has salt water in its blood and scores of its own to settle with the reavers. And some counsel a stranger course - that I let the ironborn choose their own lord, as they chose their kings of old. Weary of blood, they would sooner kneel to one of their own than to any green-land master; and a lord who owes his rise to my sufferance, chosen by his own people, is bound to me twice over.

#bold Fire and blood won the isles. Now wisdom must keep them.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0008.option1.text: The ironmen will choose their own lord.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0008.option2.text: The lion shall hold the kraken's leash.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0008.option3.text: The wolf shall watch the western sea.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0011.text: The Black King Will Not Kneel

fab_ac_iron_islands.0011.desc.text:
The King's Peace lies over the Seven Kingdoms - over six of them, at least. Beyond the Sunset Sea, upon his wet and windblown rocks, the last of House Hoare still wears a driftwood crown and still names himself a king.

I left the isles to him when the Trident fell, and I will own now that mercy was a mistake. Harren's blood was never going to sit quiet under a dragon it did not fear. From Pyke his ravens go out styling their master King of the Iron Islands, as though the towers of Harrenhal never stood at all; his longships have begun to trouble the western coast again, testing whether the peace has teeth. The riverlords who bled under three generations of Hoares send me letters begging that the work be finished.

It will be finished. One realm cannot suffer a king upon its western sea, and I did not break Black Harren's kingdom to leave his house a crown to brood over.

#bold The last war of the Conquest begins now - and the fleets of Lannisport and Highgarden, the Arbor and Bear Island sail with the dragon.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0011.option1.text: One realm. One king. The isles as well.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0012.text: The Muster of the Iron Fleet

fab_ac_iron_islands.0012.desc.text:
The black king has called his banners, and to my surprise a great many have answered.

Whatever the Hoares are, they are not the strangers on these islands that Qhorin Volmark or some jumped-up priest would have been. Harren's house has reigned over the ironborn for four generations, and the reavers know that name if they love little else. From Old Wyk and Great Wyk, from Orkmont and Blacktyde and Saltcliffe, the longships come to Pyke - captains who would never kneel to a green-land conqueror, glad of a black king to die for. They mean to fight me the Old Way: ship against ship, axe against sword, boarding through the surf.

My captains count their sails and do not love the number. Every one of those hulls burns as well as any other, and the ironborn have never in their long piratical history faced what waits above their masts.

#bold They have not forgotten how to die well. I mean to remind them how thoroughly.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0012.option1.text: Let them come. The sky is mine.

fab_ac_iron_islands.0013.desc.text:
The war has turned against the isles - and now the black king has come out to end it the only way his house has ever known.

He has landed with his household axes and sent his challenge to my camp: the Old Way, king against king, blade against blade, before both hosts. He is no fool - his cause sinks a little lower with every tide, and a dead dragon is the only thing left that could raise it. And he is no weakling either: a hard man of the old iron blood, raised from the cradle on the certainty that a Hoare bows to no one.

Half the isles are sick of blood and whisper for peace; the other half waits only to see whether the dragon dares. I did not sail the Sunset Sea to answer an ironman's challenge from behind a shield wall.

#bold Blackfyre has drunk nothing since the Field of Fire. The last black king will see how a dragon answers.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0013.desc.champion.text:
The war has turned against the isles - and now the isles have come to end it the only way their kings have ever known.

But the driftwood crown sits on a CHILD. Whatever else the ironborn are, they will not send a boy against a dragon; the Old Way demands a champion, and they have found one - the hardest sword left on those wet rocks, a grown man of the old iron blood who has sworn to stand for his little king before both hosts. The challenge has come to my camp all the same: blade against blade, upon the strand, the boy's crown riding on his champion's arm.

Half the isles are sick of blood and whisper for peace; the other half waits only to see whether the dragon dares. I did not sail the Sunset Sea to answer an ironman's challenge from behind a shield wall.

#bold Blackfyre has drunk nothing since the Field of Fire. The boy-king's champion will see how a dragon answers.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0015.desc.champion.text:
It was done before both hosts, upon the strand, in the old way the ironborn hold holier than any sept.

The boy-king's champion came at me as the ironborn have come at the world since the dawn of days: without doubt, without mercy, certain the Drowned God rode his shoulder. He was strong, and for a few strokes the ironborn dared to roar. Then Blackfyre turned his blade aside, and turned it again, and the third exchange left the champion upon the sand and the boy's cause bleeding out with him. Valyrian steel keeps no accounts and grants no seconds.

And the ironborn - who have terrorized every coast of Westeros since the dawn of days - looked on their fallen champion and their weeping boy-king, and knelt. The child will lose a crown, not his head; I do not make war on children. Whatever remains of this war on paper, it ended on that beach.

#bold House Hoare wore a crown for four generations. It will wear none again.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0015.text: The Last of the Black Kings

fab_ac_iron_islands.0015.desc.text:
It was done before both hosts, upon the strand, in the old way the ironborn hold holier than any sept.

The black king came at me as his house has come at the world for four generations: without doubt, without mercy, certain the Drowned God rode his shoulder. He was strong, and quicker than his bulk promised, and for a few strokes the ironborn dared to roar. Then Blackfyre turned his blade aside, and turned it again, and the third exchange ended the line of Harwyn Hardhand upon the sand. Valyrian steel keeps no accounts and grants no seconds. His crown of driftwood rolled into the surf and was carried out to the deep he had prayed to.

And the ironborn - who have terrorized every coast of Westeros since the dawn of days - looked on their dead king, the last of the black line, and knelt. Whatever remains of this war on paper, it ended on that beach.

#bold House Hoare wore a crown for four generations. It will wear none again.#!

fab_ac_iron_islands.0016.desc.champion.text:
I will set it down plainly, for the singers will not: the boy-king's champion had the better of me.

We met upon the strand before both hosts, in the old way, and the ironman's arm was every terrible thing the isles could have prayed for. He turned Blackfyre aside, staggered me, and only the quickness of my guard - and, I will own it, of my own feet - carried me back to my lines alive.
