One by one they say the words my sister wrote. They give up their lands and their claims, the wives they will never take and the sons they will never father. They serve for life, and the life they guard is mine.

The cloaks go over their shoulders white as new snow, and the hall is very quiet. In the gallery stand the Dornish lords come north to swear their fealty, watching seven swords raised on account of their countrymen's knives. The tale will travel home ahead of them.

#bold Seven kingdoms. Seven gods. Seven swords between the king and every knife in the dark.#!

fab_dorne.0053.option1.text: Rise, Ser Corlys. Guard your king.

fab_dorne.0054.desc.text:
The dragons have come back for Dorne, as the queen promised they would. But promises take years to keep, and we have not spent ours sleeping.

Every smith from the Planky Town to the Prince's Pass has been building to one purpose: great iron scorpions, winched and weighted to throw a spear high enough and hard enough to punch through a dragon's eye or wing. They line the walls of Sunspear now, and the Hellholt, and every tower the beasts must pass. A dragon that fears to fly low is only a horse that eats more.

The sands will empty before their host as they did before, the wells will be fouled behind us, and this time the sky itself will not be safe for them. Nymeria burned her own ships so her people would stand and fight. We are her children still.

fab_dorne.0054.option1.text: Our stand will be sung beside Nymeria's.

fab_dorne.0055.desc.text:
It was not enough. The scorpions took their price — let the dragonlords never say Dorne came cheap — but the sands are ours no longer, and House Martell kneels where my mother swore no Martell ever would.

Bowed, bent, broken: they will throw our own words back at us now, and we must swallow them with the rest.

But Dorne has been conquered before — the Andals thought so, at least, and where are the Andal kings of Dorne today? A knee can bend for a season. A desert remembers longer than a dynasty. We endure, we watch, and we wait for the world to teach the dragons what it taught every conqueror before them.

fab_dorne.0055.desc.submit.text: I will not feed Dorne to the dragons merely to preserve a word. Before the passes fill with ash and the wells with the dead, I accept Aegon Targaryen's terms and bend the knee beneath his Iron Throne.\n\nThey will say that Dorne is bowed, bent, and broken. A knee can bend for a season, and a desert remembers longer than a dynasty. We endure, we watch, and we preserve enough of ourselves to meet whatever history brings next.

setting_fab_aemon_tarth_fate_survives_de.text: The bolt misses its fatal mark and Aemon returns alive.

setting_fab_baelon_final_illness_fate_su.text: The maesters' treatment succeeds and Baelon survives.

fab_death_rebuilding_valyria.text: died of stress while trying to rebuild Valyria

fab_tradition_valyrian_polygamy_desc.text: The dragonlords of Old Valyria wed as they pleased, and often wed more than once. The blood of the Freehold keeps to the customs of the Freehold - whatever gods its neighbors kneel to, and whatever their septons mutter about it.

fab_aegon.0001.desc.text:
Our first progress has borne us at last to Maidenpool, where every gate is hung with flowers and every bell rings for the coming of the King and Queen. Alysanne receives their welcome with one hand resting upon the small swell beneath her gown. If the gods are good, our first child will be born before another year has turned.

Lord Mooton has opened Jonquil's Pool to her. The smallfolk swear its warm waters have healed barren women, eased old wounds, and blessed babes still in the womb. Even the wisest maester cannot make Alysanne scorn so gentle a hope. She laughs when I name it a tale for washerwomen and tells me that kings would be wiser if they listened to washerwomen from time to time.

Only women may enter the bathhouse. Ser Joffrey Doggett and Ser Gyles Morrigen must keep their watch beyond the doors, while Alysanne goes within with her ladies and the holy sisters who tend the pool.

#bold This is a place of peace, beloved of the Maiden. What harm could find her here? #!

fab_aegon.0001.a.text: See the Queen to her rest. The road has wearied her.

fab_aegon.0002.desc.text:
The cry from within the bathhouse stills every bell in Maidenpool.

Three holy sisters drew long knives from beneath their robes as Alysanne stepped toward the water. Rosamund Ball threw herself before the Queen and took a blade deep in the belly. Prudence Celtigar was stabbed through the shoulder. Septa Edyth bears a red ruin across her cheek. They held the women off until Doggett and Morrigen broke down the barred door with swords in hand.

Two of the would-be killers died upon the wet stones. The third lives in Lord Mooton's dungeons, though she has more broken teeth than whole ones. Alysanne is untouched, and the maester swears the child within her yet lives, but my queen cannot cease staring at Rosamund's blood upon her gown.

She came seeking the Maiden's blessing. She found murder in a holy habit.

#bold Whoever sent those knives meant to kill my wife, my unborn child, and the peace we have labored to make. #!

fab_aegon.0002.a.text: Guard Alysanne. Tend her women. Put every gate under watch.

fab_aegon.0004.desc.text:
Rosamund Ball lingered three days before the wound in her belly claimed her. Alysanne sat beside her until the end.

The surviving murderess has named six others in Maidenpool who shared her purpose. Lord Mooton would put every one of them to death, and cast all the holy sisters from Jonquil's Pool besides. He fears that any white robe may hide another knife.

Alysanne will not have it. 'Hang the guilty if their guilt is proved,' she tells us, her cheek pale beneath the stain of sleepless nights. 'But I will not answer Rosamund's courage by visiting vengeance upon women who had no part in her death. The robe did not wield the dagger. A woman did.'

There are lords who will name her mercy weakness. They were not in the blood-slick pool, nor did they watch three loyal women place their bodies before their queen.

#bold Justice must know one face from another, else it is only slaughter dressed in a king's colors. #!

fab_aegon.0004.a.text: Try those she named. The innocent sisters shall go unharmed.

fab_aegon.0005.desc.text:
No white cloak could follow Alysanne into Jonquil's Pool. There will be other doors barred to men, other chambers where the Kingsguard must remain without. I will not leave my queen's life to custom a second time.

Jonquil Darke kneels beneath the Iron Throne in ringmail and a long scarlet cloak. She is a bastard born, but no man in the yard can shame her with sword or spear, and Alysanne trusts her. The court has already found a name for the woman who will walk half a pace behind the Queen wherever men may not: the Scarlet Shadow.

'You shall guard her waking and sleeping,' I tell Jonquil. 'You shall stand where my white cloaks cannot, and place your life before hers if need be.'

Jonquil looks not to me when she makes her vow, but to Alysanne. 'Gladly.'

#bold Henceforth, the Queen shall cast a shadow armed with steel. #!

fab_aegon.0005.a.text: Rise, Jonquil Darke, and keep my queen safe.

fab_aegon.0010.desc.text:
Our son has come before his hour.

The midwife lifts him in hands that seem too large for so small a child. His skin is red and thin, his limbs scarcely thicker than my fingers. For one terrible moment the chamber is silent. Then he draws a ragged breath and gives a cry so faint I must bend close to hear it.

Alysanne names him Aegon. The name of the Conqueror should belong to a strong prince, yet my son can scarcely close his hand about mine. The maesters wrap him in warmed wool and speak softly among themselves. Not one will promise us the dawn.

Alysanne believes the knives at Maidenpool hastened his coming. Worse, she believes that had she bathed in Jonquil's Pool, the waters might have lent him strength. There is no wisdom in telling a grieving mother that such waters hold no power.

#bold He is my firstborn, my blood, and the heir to all the realm. He must live. #!

fab_aegon.0010.a.text: Keep every brazier burning. He shall not want for warmth.

fab_aegon.0011.desc.text:
For three days the world has narrowed to a cradle.

Aegon's breathing comes shallow and uneven. Each pause lasts long enough for Alysanne to seize my hand; each little gasp releases it again. Grand Maester Benifer has tried warm goat's milk, steam, prayers, and every cordial known at the Citadel. At last he can do no more than stand beside us and count the breaths.

Beyond these walls, lords await word of an heir. Bells hang silent over the city. The Iron Throne may command seven kingdoms, yet all my kingly power cannot purchase one stronger beat of this tiny heart.

Night gathers at the windows. Aegon opens his eyes, dark and unfocused, and makes the smallest sound.

#bold Whether it is farewell or defiance, only the gods can know. #!

fab_aegon.0013.desc.text:
Near dawn, Aegon forgets to draw another breath.

The maester waits, listens, and lowers his head. Alysanne gathers our son into her arms before any hand can cover him. He lived three days. Long enough to have a name, long enough to be loved, long enough for every hope we had laid upon him to become a grief with weight and shape.

They will call him Prince Aegon in the annals. My firstborn son. Heir to the Iron Throne for three brief days. A line of ink between a birth and a burial. No quill will write how warm his hand felt curled about the tip of my finger, or how fiercely his mother begged him to remain.

#bold The realm has lost a prince. We have lost our child. #!

fab_aegon.0013.a.text: Ring the bells for Aegon, first of our children.

fab_aegon.0014.desc.text:
The silence breaks.

Aegon drags in a breath deep enough to fill his little chest, then another. When the maester reaches for him, our son answers with a cry louder than any sound he has yet made. It is a thin, angry wail, but Alysanne laughs as though every bell in King's Landing has rung at once.

By sunrise he has taken milk. By noon the grey cast has left his skin. Benifer warns that a child born so small must be watched for many moons, yet even he cannot deny what lies before him: the prince has passed through the shadow and chosen life.

I place one hand upon the cradle and the other in Alysanne's. Our firstborn lives. The realm has its prince, and I have an heir whose first victory was won before he could lift his own head.

#bold The singers will make what omen they like of it. My son breathes. #!

fab_aegon.0014.a.text: Aegon shall be known to all the realm as my heir.

fab_aegon_cradle_shield_desc.text: Maesters and midwives keep ceaseless watch over this frail newborn, whose every breath may be his last.

fab_aegon_survived_cradle_modifier_desc.text: Born before his hour and thought certain to die, this child endured the perilous first days of life.

fab_betrothal.0001.desc.text:
My son grows faster than I can credit. It seems only yesterday that [aemon.GetFirstName] clung to his mother's skirts in the nursery; now he sits a horse like a man grown, and the master-at-arms tells me the boy's wrists are already stronger than his own. Soon enough the realm will look at my heir and ask the question every realm asks of a prince: who is to be his bride?

Lady Jocelyn Baratheon is my mother's last daughter, born at Storm's End the very hour that Alyssa died of her. My own half-sister, if the maesters must have it plain, and so the boy's aunt; the septons will purse their lips at that, as they pursed them at my own marriage. Yet Jocelyn was raised beside my children from the cradle, and I know no fiercer or more loyal heart in the Seven Kingdoms. Black of hair and tall for her years, she could join storm and dragon at last.

Or I might look elsewhere. The great Houses have daughters enough, and every lord of them would give his sword hand to see his blood seated beside the Iron Throne.

fab_betrothal.0001.desc.spare.text:
My son grows faster than I can credit. It seems only yesterday that [aemon.GetFirstName] clung to his mother's skirts in the nursery; now he sits a horse like a man grown, and the master-at-arms tells me the boy's wrists are already stronger than his own. The succession may not fall to Aemon, but a prince of the blood needs a bride all the same.

Lady Jocelyn Baratheon is my mother's last daughter, born at Storm's End the very hour that Alyssa died of her. My own half-sister, if the maesters must have it plain, and so the boy's aunt; the septons will purse their lips at that, as they pursed them at my own marriage. Yet Jocelyn was raised beside my children from the cradle, and I know no fiercer or more loyal heart in the Seven Kingdoms. Black of hair and tall for her years, she could join storm and dragon at last.

Or I might look elsewhere. The great Houses have daughters enough, and a prince's marriage is a coin worth spending on some lord's loyalty.

fab_betrothal.0001.a.text: Lady Jocelyn shall be his bride.

fab_betrothal.0001.a.tt.text: Prince [aemon.GetFirstName] will be betrothed to Lady [fab_jocelyn.GetFirstName] Baratheon. The Faith's scruples do not bind the blood of the dragon.

fab_betrothal.0001.b.text: We will find alliances with other Houses.

fab_betrothal.0001.b.tt.text: The prince remains free to wed where the realm's need is greatest. No betrothal is made.

fab_betrothal.0002.desc.text:
It is done, and proclaimed before the court. My son and Lady Jocelyn stand together beneath the Iron Throne while the herald reads out the betrothal, and if either feels any misgiving, neither shows it. The girl wears black and red—the storm draped in the dragon's colors—and half the hall loses its heart to her on the spot.

The septons may mutter about degrees of kinship; my House has never asked their leave in such matters, and the realm is the stronger for every bond that binds Storm's End to the Iron Throne.

They will wed when they are grown. Until then, they may be children a while longer.

fab_betrothal.0002.a.text: May their days together be long.

fab_betrothal.0003.desc.heir.text:
My son's sixteenth nameday has come. The boy who once chased dragon shadows through these halls now stands before me a man grown, broad of shoulder and steady of eye. With his childhood ended, the promise I made for him must be fulfilled.

Jocelyn has grown no less worthy of him. The black-haired girl from Storm's End is fierce in her loyalties and unbowed by the whispers that follow their kinship. She has worn Aemon's promise for years; neither of them should be made to wait longer.

The marriage of the man who must follow me upon the Iron Throne is no private matter. The realm shall witness storm joined to dragon, and know the future of my House stands secure.

fab_betrothal.0003.desc.prince.text:
My son's sixteenth nameday has come. The boy who once chased dragon shadows through these halls now stands before me a man grown, broad of shoulder and steady of eye. With his childhood ended, the promise I made for him must be fulfilled.

Jocelyn has grown no less worthy of him. The black-haired girl from Storm's End is fierce in her loyalties and unbowed by the whispers that follow their kinship. She has worn Aemon's promise for years; neither of them should be made to wait longer.

The succession may lead elsewhere, but Aemon remains my son and a prince of the blood. His wedding shall be honored before the realm, with all the dignity owed to House Targaryen.

fab_betrothal.0003.a.tt.text: Prince [aemon.GetFirstName] and Lady [fab_jocelyn.GetFirstName] will be wed before the court.

fab_betrothal.0004.desc.heir.text:
The bells begin at dawn and do not cease until Aemon and Jocelyn stand together before the Seven. Every bench is filled, every gallery crowded, while the court watches my son take my sister's hand and speak the vows first promised for them in childhood.

Aemon lays a cloak of black and red across Jocelyn's shoulders. For a moment I see them not as pieces upon the realm's board, but simply as two children of my House whom I have watched grow.

Yet the realm sees more. In Aemon it beholds the man who shall follow me; in Jocelyn, the woman who shall stand beside him. The storm and the dragon are joined, and the line of the Iron Throne is made stronger for it.

fab_betrothal.0004.desc.prince.text:
The bells begin at dawn and do not cease until Aemon and Jocelyn stand together before the Seven. Every bench is filled, every gallery crowded, while the court watches my son take my sister's hand and speak the vows first promised for them in childhood.

Aemon lays a cloak of black and red across Jocelyn's shoulders. For a moment I see them not as pieces upon the realm's board, but simply as two children of my House whom I have watched grow.

Whatever place the succession grants Aemon, today he is my son, a prince of House Targaryen, and a husband. Storm and dragon are joined at last, and our House is stronger for the bond.

fab_betrothal.0004.a.text: May storm and dragon prosper together.

sotd_bloodfyre.0001.desc.text:
Alysanne comes from the dragon yards with soot upon her skirts and wonder in her eyes. Silverwing has laid a single egg, still warm from beneath her wing.

It is red, but no red found in ruby, garnet, or sunset. Its shell is dark and wet-looking, almost black along the ridges, and gleams in the torchlight like something freshly spilled. Even the men of the dragon yards handle it uneasily. One mutters that it has the color of blood.

Yet it is warm. Beneath my palm, something answers with the faintest pulse.

sotd_bloodfyre.0001.a.text: Place it in the royal hatcheries.

sotd_bloodfyre_egg_desc.text: A dark red egg, laid by Silverwing. It will hatch #bold Bloodfyre#!. Give it to whichever child you want to ride it.

agot_bm_sotd_desc.text:
48 AC. Maegor the Cruel lies dead upon the Iron Throne, slain by the very seat he claimed through fire and murder. The broken realm now passes to a boy of four-and-ten: Jaehaerys Targaryen, returned from hiding on the wings of the great bronze dragon Vermithor to claim his uncle's crown.

He does not rule alone. His mother, the Dowager Queen Alyssa Velaryon, sits as Queen Regent, and mighty Rogar Baratheon, Lord of Storm's End, is named Lord Protector of the Realm and Hand of the King. The Faith is in open revolt, the treasury is bare, and the great lords watch to see whether another dragon will burn them.

#bold Can the young dragon heal the wounds Maegor left, make his peace with the Seven, and begin the long golden reign of the Conciliator? #!

bookmark_sotd_jaehaerys_desc.text:
[Concept( 'story_content_fab_jaehaerys', '$bm_story_content_available_icon|q$' )|E] [Concept( 'story_content_fab_jaehaerys', '$bm_story_content_available_copy|q$' )|E]
Jaehaerys Targaryen is but four-and-ten, yet the Iron Throne is his. His uncle Maegor's cruelty has left the realm bleeding - the Faith Militant in arms, the lords wavering, the smallfolk starving. A boy king beneath the shadow of a regency must find a way to bind the wounds of a broken kingdom.

#bold Can Jaehaerys grow into the greatest king the Seven Kingdoms will ever know? #!

bookmark_sotd_rogar_baratheon_desc.text:
[Concept( 'story_content_fab_rogar', '$bm_story_content_available_icon|q$' )|E] [Concept( 'story_content_fab_rogar', '$bm_story_content_available_copy|q$' )|E]
Rogar Baratheon, Lord of Storm's End, is the strong right hand of the young king's regency - Lord Protector of the Realm and Hand of the King, and soon to wed the Dowager Queen herself. An ambitious man now stands closer to the throne than any Baratheon since Orys.

#bold Will Lord Rogar guide the boy king faithfully, or reach for a crown of his own? #!

game_concept_story_content_fab_jaehaerys.text: #tooltip_heading Story Style: Extensive#!\n\nAs Jaehaerys Targaryen, you inherit a realm Maegor broke. Scripted events run from the regency through the long reign after it: peace with the Faith, the Doctrine of Exceptionalism, your marriage to Alysanne, the Shivers, the royal progresses, and the children whose fates shape your legacy.

game_concept_story_content_fab_rogar_des.text: #tooltip_heading Story Style: Light#!\n\nAs Rogar Baratheon, you hold the realm for a boy king as Lord Protector and Hand. A handful of scripted events concern the regency, your marriage to the Dowager Queen Alyssa, and how far your ambition carries you before Jaehaerys comes of age.

SOTD_FAITH_UPRISING_WAR_NAME.text: The Great Uprising of the Faith

sotd_faith_uprising_victory_desc.text: The Faith and the risen realm have humbled the dragon king.

sotd_faith_uprising_defeat_desc.text: The dragon king has broken the risen realm and the hosts of the Faith.

sotd_faith_uprising_white_peace_desc.text: The war between the dragon and the Faith ends without a victor.

SOTD_BRAAVOS_EGGS_WAR_NAME.text: The War for the Stolen Eggs

sotd_braavos_eggs_war_victory_desc.text: The dragon has broken Braavos and reclaimed the stolen eggs.

sotd_braavos_eggs_war_defeat_desc.text: Braavos has weathered the dragon's wrath; the eggs remain in the Sealord's vaults.

sotd_braavos_eggs_war_white_peace_desc.text: The war for the stolen eggs ends without a victor.

sotd_doctrine.0001.desc.text:
The wedding is done, twice over, and yet the matter is not settled. The Faith of the Seven still names a brother wedding his sister an abomination; the Seven-Pointed Star, holy writ born in Andalos of old, denounces incest in the plainest words. Septons mutter it in their septs; the pious lords grumble; and I have not forgotten that it was such muttering that raised the Faith Militant against my father and my uncle, and drowned the realm in blood.

I will not leave this wound to fester. The Seven must be made to accept my marriage - but how? With patience and honeyed words, as befits a Conciliator? Or with fire, as befits a dragon?

#bold The dragon and the Seven cannot both be right. One of us must bend. #!

sotd_doctrine.0001.a.text: Words, not swords. I shall send the Seven Speakers.

sotd_doctrine.0001.b.text: The dragon does not beg. Fire and blood.

sotd_doctrine.0002.desc.text:
I choose the path of my grandsire, not my uncle. I send forth seven of the wisest and most eloquent voices of the Faith - septons and septas both, among them the fierce old Septon Alfyn and clever Elinor Costayne - to preach the #bold Doctrine of Exceptionalism#! throughout the realm. Barefoot and alone they go, from village to village, town to town, telling the smallfolk of my wisdom and Alysanne's kindness.

Their teaching is simple: that the Targaryens, alone in all the world to ride dragons since the Doom of Valyria, sprang not from Andalos but from the Freehold, where different laws held sway and brother wed sister as the gods had made them - and that such blood is not to be judged by the laws of common men.

When a scoffing hedge knight calls out to Septon Baldrick, #italic 'Aye, and if I want to bed my own sister too, do I have your leave?'#!, the septon answers without missing a step: #italic 'Go to Dragonstone and claim a dragon, ser. If you can do that, I will marry you and your sister myself.'#! The smallfolk roar with laughter, and win by win, the realm is turned.

#bold The Speakers will go forth, and the realm will be won with words. #!

sotd_doctrine.0002.a.text: Go forth, and preach the truth of the dragon.

sotd_doctrine.0003.desc.text:
Some years into my doctrine, the old High Septon dies, and the crystal crown stands empty. Now the Most Devout must choose his successor - and one likely candidate is a septon who would denounce my marriage from the Starry Sept itself and light the flames of revolt anew, as they burned only a few years past.

I will not permit it. On Vermithor and Silverwing, Alysanne and I fly to Oldtown, and there I strike a quiet bargain with the Lord of the Hightower, whose voice sways the Most Devout: his support for a High Septon friendly to my doctrine, and in return my royal promise that a son of his own house shall one day wear the crystal crown. The old lord takes my hand. The deal is struck.

#bold A crown for a crown. The Faith's own shall crown my doctrine. #!

sotd_doctrine.0003.a.text: A Hightower for a High Septon. Agreed.

sotd_doctrine.0004.desc.text:
It is done. Beneath the crystal dome of the Starry Sept, the new High Septon lifts his voice before the assembled Most Devout and proclaims the Doctrine of Exceptionalism an official tenet of the Faith of the Seven. The Targaryens are exceptional; the Targaryens are not to be judged as common men; the Targaryens may wed as the dragonlords of old.

Never again shall a septon name my marriage sin, nor my children abominations, without preaching against the Faith itself. The long war between the dragon and the Seven - begun by my father, made monstrous by my uncle - is ended by me, not with fire, but with wisdom and patience. It will be written into the holy books for all the ages to come.

#bold The dragon and the Seven are reconciled, now and forever. #!

sotd_doctrine.0004.a.text: So it is written. So it shall be.

sotd_doctrine.0004.doctrine_tt.text: The #bold Doctrine of Exceptionalism#! becomes a tenet of the #bold Faith of the Seven#!. House Targaryen is henceforth exempt from the Faith's laws against incest, free to wed brother to sister as the dragonlords of old Valyria did.

sotd_doctrine.0005.desc.text:
Word reaches the Red Keep from the kingsroad: the Seven Speakers are working. In a market town in the riverlands, Septon Baldrick preached the Doctrine of Exceptionalism from a wagon bed to a crowd come to jeer - and left them cheering. A miller's wife, they say, put it best: #italic 'The Andals never rode no dragons. Seems to me the gods what gave the dragons to the Targaryens meant for them to keep their blood to themselves.'#!

Every sennight brings another such tale - a village won here, a market square there, alms given and sermons cheered. Slowly, mile by mile and word by word, the smallfolk of Westeros are learning to see my marriage not as sin, but as the way of the dragon.

#bold Patience. Words take longer than fire, but they burn nothing down. #!

sotd_doctrine.0006.desc.text:
A greater victory now, and a harder one: [sotd_convinced_lord.GetTitledFirstName], as pious a lord as any in the realm, has heard septa Elinor Costayne preach the Doctrine of Exceptionalism in his own hall - and has risen to declare himself persuaded. The blood of the dragon, he told his assembled household, is not the blood of common men, and the Seven-Pointed Star was written for Andals, not for the heirs of lost Valyria.

Where one great lord leads, others follow. The lords bannermen take note; the septons of his lands fall quiet; and the muttering against my marriage grows fainter in every hall where the Speakers have passed.

#bold The lords of Westeros begin to bend. Not to fear - to reason. #!

sotd_doctrine.0006.desc.generic.text:
A greater victory now, and a harder one: word comes that one of the realm's most pious lords has heard septa Elinor Costayne preach the Doctrine of Exceptionalism in his own hall - and has risen to declare himself persuaded. The blood of the dragon, he told his assembled household, is not the blood of common men, and the Seven-Pointed Star was written for Andals, not for the heirs of lost Valyria.

Where one great lord leads, others follow. The lords bannermen take note; the septons of his lands fall quiet; and the muttering against my marriage grows fainter in every hall where the Speakers have passed.

#bold The lords of Westeros begin to bend. Not to fear - to reason. #!

sotd_doctrine.0006.a.text: Where one lord leads, others will follow.

sotd_doctrine.0007.desc.text:
Old Septon Alfyn, tireless still at his age, sends word from the Reach that would have been unthinkable two years past: a septon who dared preach against my marriage from his own altar was shouted down - #bold by his own flock#!. The smallfolk pelted him with turnips and quoted the Speakers' teaching back at him, word for word: the dragon is not judged as common men are judged.

From the Vale to the Stormlands the tale is the same. The realm that once muttered against the abomination on the Iron Throne now argues my case in every tavern and every sept. The Doctrine of Exceptionalism is no longer the Crown's plea - it is becoming the people's creed.

Only the Starry Sept itself still holds out. But the old High Septon is very old, and the gods will call him soon enough.

#bold The realm is won. Now only the crystal crown remains. #!

sotd_doctrine.0007.a.text: The people speak for the dragon now.

sotd_doctrine.0010.desc.text:
Why should I, the blood of the dragon, come cap in hand to grey old men in grey old robes, begging their leave to love my own wife? My uncle Maegor answered the Faith with fire and blood, and though he was a monster, in this one thing perhaps he was not wholly wrong: the dragon rules, and the sheep obey.

And yet - to make war upon the Faith of the Seven is to make war upon half the realm; the Faith Militant nearly pulled down my house within living memory. I feel Alysanne's eyes upon me, uncertain. The road forks here, and there is no coming back easily from the wrong turning.

#bold What is a dragon to do, when the sheep will not obey? #!

sotd_doctrine.0010.a.text: Fly to Oldtown. The High Septon will bend, or burn.

sotd_doctrine.0010.b.text: No. I will not be my uncle. The Speakers will do their work.

sotd_doctrine.0010.c.text: Why bow to Andal gods at all? We are the blood of Valyria.

sotd_doctrine.0011.desc.text:
Vermithor's vast bronze shadow falls across the holy city as I circle the Starry Sept, and all of Oldtown cowers beneath the beat of his wings. I land before the High Septon and his Most Devout, and I demand it plainly: proclaim the Doctrine of Exceptionalism, bless my marriage, and name my children trueborn - or answer to the Bronze Fury.

But the old man is made of sterner stuff than I had hoped. He does not flinch. He names me sinner and abomination to my very face, though my dragon could swallow him in a single bite, and tells me the Seven do not bargain with monsters.

#bold He will not bend. Now I must choose what manner of king I am. #!

sotd_doctrine.0011.a.text: Then burn. Burn, as my uncle should have burned you all!

sotd_doctrine.0011.b.text: A Trial of Seven! The gods themselves will judge who is righteous.

sotd_doctrine.0012.desc.text:
I loose the Bronze Fury. Vermithor descends upon Oldtown, and the Starry Sept - the oldest and holiest seat of the Faith in all Westeros, where the Andal kings were blessed a thousand years before my house was born - is drowned in dragonfire. Its crystal dome shatters like an eggshell; the High Septon and the Most Devout burn to ash within.

The realm recoils in horror. From the Reach to the Vale to the stony Vale of Arryn, the pious lords take up the old cry of the Faith Militant: the dragon king is a monster, and must be pulled down as his uncle nearly was. I have made war upon the Seven, and the Seven have answered with the wrath of half my kingdom.

#bold Fire and blood. The whole realm may come, if it dares. #!

sotd_doctrine.0012.a.text: So be it. The dragon fears no army of sheep.

sotd_doctrine.0013.desc.text:
I will not burn them as my uncle would have. Instead I demand the oldest and most sacred of the Faith's own judgments: a #bold Trial of Seven#!. Seven champions shall fight for the Crown, and seven for the Faith, and the gods themselves will declare, through blood and steel, who is righteous.

The High Septon is too frail to lift a sword, so the Faith turns to its mightiest son: the #bold Lord of Oldtown#! himself shall champion the Seven, and the knights of the Hightower shall fill out his seven. And I shall fight in my own name - for the gods' verdict is not a thing a king may delegate. Each of us must now gather our champions, the finest swords who will stand with us in the yard before the Starry Sept.

If my seven prevail, then the gods have spoken: the Doctrine of Exceptionalism is proven true, and the Faith must bow to the verdict of its own holy trial. But if we fall, then I am judged a sinner before gods and men - and there is no appeal from such a judgment, nor will I survive it. The septons pray. The gods are watching.

#bold For the dragon, and for the truth. The champions will be gathered. #!

sotd_doctrine.0013.a.text: Seven for the dragon. Let the gods decide.

sotd_doctrine.0014.desc.text:
The last of my champions falls in the bloodied mud before the sept, and the septons raise their voices to the heavens in triumph. The gods have spoken - and their verdict is against me. I staked my marriage on their judgment before ten thousand witnesses, and there is no appeal from a Trial of Seven: to defy it now would be to hand the Faith Militant half my realm.

So the price is paid, and it is crueler than any sword. The High Septon declares my marriage to Alysanne dissolved in the eyes of gods and men, sinful and void from its first hour - and any children born of it are named abominations, unfit to ever sit the Iron Throne. And for Alysanne herself, the Faith claims its most terrible mercy: the grey robes of the #bold Silent Sisters#!, that she might atone for our sin in service to the Stranger, wordless until her dying day.

The sisters come for her at dusk. She does not weep where they can see her; that mercy she leaves for me alone. At the door she turns - and says nothing, for she has already begun her silence. But her eyes say what her tongue may never speak again: #italic it was never sin.#!

#bold I have lost her - to the gods who judged us, and the silence they demand. #!

sotd_doctrine.0014.a.text: The gods have judged. (She will never speak again.)

sotd_doctrine.0017.desc.text:
It is over. The last of the Faith's champions lies broken in the red mud before the Starry Sept, and a terrible hush falls over Oldtown. Seven fought for the Seven, and seven fought for the dragon - and the gods have rendered their verdict in blood and steel, as the Faith's own holiest law demands.

The septons stare at the carnage, ashen-faced. There is no appeal from a Trial of Seven; the judgment is holy, and final, and it is #bold mine#!. The Doctrine of Exceptionalism is no longer the plea of a king - it is the proven will of the gods, declared before ten thousand witnesses in the shadow of the Faith's own great sept.

The Most Devout may write it into their holy books, for the gods themselves have written it first, in blood.

#bold The gods are with the dragon. The Faith will bow. #!

sotd_doctrine.0017.a.text: The verdict is holy, and final. Proclaim the doctrine.

sotd_doctrine.0018.desc.text:
Beneath the crystal dome of the Starry Sept, the High Septon lifts his voice before the assembled Most Devout and proclaims the Doctrine of Exceptionalism an official tenet of the Faith of the Seven. His voice does not waver, though every soul beneath the dome knows why he speaks: the Faith called upon the gods to judge the dragon, and the gods answered - for the dragon.

I did not burn them, as my uncle would have. I did not beg them, as they expected. I gave the Seven their own holiest trial and let their own gods speak - and now no septon may name my marriage sin, nor my children abominations, without calling the gods themselves liars. The verdict was written in blood before ten thousand witnesses, and it shall be written in the holy books for all the ages to come.

#bold The gods have judged, and the Faith must bow. The dragon and the Seven are reconciled - on the dragon's terms. #!

sotd_doctrine.0018.desc.forfeit.text:
It ends not with blood, but with silence. The appointed day comes, and the Crown's seven stand armed and ready in the yard before the Starry Sept - and across from them, no one. The Faith, for all its thundering, could not find seven champions willing to stake their lives on its accusation. By the Faith's own holiest law, an accusation that cannot be championed is no accusation at all: the gods find for the accused.

The High Septon has no choice. Beneath the crystal dome, before the assembled Most Devout, he proclaims the Doctrine of Exceptionalism a tenet of the Faith of the Seven. No septon may now name my marriage sin, nor my children abominations - for when the gods were asked to judge the dragon, not one man of the Faith dared carry their sword.

#bold The Seven were called to battle, and none came. The doctrine stands, now and forever. #!

sotd_doctrine.0018.a.text: So it is written - in blood, and for all time.

sotd_doctrine.0020.desc.text:
Enough of this. Why should the blood of Old Valyria - who ride dragons, who rule the greatest realm the world has known - bow and scrape before the pale gods of the Andals, who came crawling to Westeros long after my forefathers ruled the skies?

The dragonlords of the Freehold worshipped the fourteen flames and the fire made flesh, and asked no septon's leave to wed as they pleased. So shall we. I proclaim before the court that House Targaryen forsakes the Faith of the Seven and returns to the old gods of Valyria. The septons may wail and the smallfolk gape. We are dragons; we shall make our own gods, as we always have.

#bold We are the blood of the dragon. We will worship as Valyria did. #!

sotd_doctrine.0020.a.text: Forsake the Seven. We return to the fires of Valyria.

sotd_doctrine.0030.desc.text:
The ravens fly, and every one carries the same word: war. The Lord of the Reach - in whose lands the Starry Sept lies in ashes and whose smallfolk sifted the bones of the High Septon from the ruin - has declared for the Faith, and the realm rises with him. The Riverlands. The Vale. The Westerlands. And the North - the Starks keep the old gods and care nothing for the Seven, but the burning of holy men alive in their own temple is a crime no honourable northman will suffer: they march not for the Faith, but against me.

Only the ironborn sit apart, praying to their drowned god and caring nothing for burned septs. The Crownlands stand by their king, and the Stormlands, who remember whose sword set me on this throne. Two kingdoms against five, and every sept in Westeros preaching holy war against the dragon who burned the gods' own house. My uncle faced the Faith Militant; I have made the whole realm my Faith Militant.

So be it. They wanted a monster on the Iron Throne. They will come and find one.

#bold Two kingdoms, two dragons, and fire and blood. The realm may come. #!

sotd_doctrine.0030.a.text: Fire and blood, then. They will find me waiting.

sotd_doctrine.0031.desc.text:
It is finished. Against five kingdoms and every sept in Westeros, the dragon has won. The hosts of the Faith lie broken from the Mander to the Trident; the lords who rose against me kneel in the ashes of their own fields, one by one, and press their lips to my ring while their eyes burn with hate.

My uncle told me once, in his way: the dragon rules, and the sheep obey. I did not wish to be my uncle - but they would not let me be anything else. The realm will remember what it cost to rise against Vermithor, and the memory will keep the peace better than love ever did.

There remains only one thing to take from them: the word they denied me, spoken from the ruin of their holiest place.

#bold The realm is broken to the saddle. Now the Faith will say the words. #!

sotd_doctrine.0031.a.text: Now bring me what remains of the Most Devout.

sotd_doctrine.0032.desc.text:
They crown a new High Septon in a borrowed sept, for the old one is ash - and his first act, before septons whose hands shake as they hold the crystal, is to proclaim the Doctrine of Exceptionalism a holy tenet of the Faith of the Seven. His voice breaks as he says the words. No one beneath that roof believes them. Every one of them will repeat them until the day they die.

The Targaryens are exceptional. The Targaryens are not to be judged as common men. The Targaryens may wed as the dragonlords of old. So says the Faith - because the alternative is the fire.

My grandsire won his crown with dragons and kept it with mercy. My uncle had the dragons and not the mercy. And I? I offered the realm wisdom, and it chose to teach me that only the fire is ever truly heard.

#bold The doctrine stands - written not in ink, nor in blood, but in fire. #!

sotd_doctrine.0032.a.text: So says the Faith. So say the flames.

sotd_doctrine.0033.desc.text:
The realm has won. Five kingdoms broke my hosts, my banners burned from the Mander to the kingsroad, and the men who marched beneath the seven-pointed star now dictate their peace beneath my own roof. They leave me my throne - a king they can point to, chastened, is worth more to them than a martyr - but they take everything else.

The marriage is declared an abomination, dissolved in the sight of gods and men. My children are named unfit to inherit, their blood tainted by sin. And Alysanne - Alysanne is given to the Silent Sisters, to atone in grey wordlessness for the crime of loving me. The sisters come for her while the septons watch, so that none may say the dragon hid his sin away.

She does not weep where they can see her. At the door she turns and says nothing, for her silence has already begun - but her eyes say what her tongue may never speak again: #italic it was never sin.#!

I burned the Starry Sept, and the realm burned my whole world in answer.

#bold The dragon reigns still - over the ashes of everything he loved. #!

sotd_doctrine.0033.a.text: The realm has judged. (I have lost her.)

sotd_dragonpit.0001.desc.text:
It is finished. Where once the Sept of Remembrance stood in ashes upon Rhaenys's Hill, there now rises the mightiest structure in all King's Landing - the Dragonpit, a vast dome of stone and iron seven acres wide, its bronze doors tall enough to admit a dragon in full flight. Years of labour and a king's fortune in gold have gone into its making, and now the great beasts of my house have a hall worthy of them.

From the walls of the Red Keep I can see it crowning the city, and the smallfolk gather in their thousands to marvel. All the world will see the power and the glory of House Targaryen made manifest in stone. A thing so grand should not pass unmarked - the realm shall have a grand tournament to celebrate it, the like of which has not been seen since my grandsire's day.

#bold The dragons have their pit. Now let the lords come and break their lances in its shadow. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0001.b.text: A proud day - let it be kept simply.

sotd_dragonpit.0002.desc.text:
Lord Manfryd Redwyne, my master of ships, has proved as deft with celebration as with fleets. At his urging, the completion of the Dragonpit is to be marked with a tourney fit for the wonder it honors.

The lists rise beneath the great dome itself. No dragon has yet settled in the pit, and so the vast hollow of stone and bronze becomes a field of banners, galleries, sand, barriers, and shouting men. Lords arrive with their retinues, freeriders with polished hopes, and hedge knights with armor beaten bright for one more chance at glory.

I take my place above the field with Alysanne beside me. Others may break lances and bones. A king need only watch, judge, and remember who shines when all the realm is looking.

#bold The Dragonpit is open. The tournament begins. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0003.desc.text:
The squires ride first, all long limbs, borrowed armor, and fierce young pride. More than one boy forgets his reins when the crowd roars; more than one learns, flat on his back in the sand, that glory has a hard edge.

Rickard Redwyne does not forget. He rides as if the din of the Dragonpit is only wind, taking each tilt cleanly, lowering his lance at the proper breath, and sending better-born boys tumbling before him. By the final pass even the hardened knights are nodding to one another.

When he kneels before me, dusty, flushed, and trying not to grin, I draw steel and touch it to his shoulders. The dome carries my words until every gallery hears them.

#bold Rise, Ser Rickard Redwyne. You have earned your spurs. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0004.desc.text:
The joust belongs to Ser Simon Dondarrion of Blackhaven.

Ser Robert Redwyne gives him a splendid contest, and others make him work harder still, but Simon only grows brighter with each broken lance. He smiles for the smallfolk, bows to the ladies, and rides like a song made flesh. By the final tilt the commons are chanting his name, and Alysanne herself is laughing behind her hand.

Then comes the choice all champions must make. Simon takes the wreath of flowers, turns beneath the thunder of the dome, and lays it before the young princess in the royal gallery.

#bold The Dragonpit shakes with cheers. Even Alysanne is won. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0005.desc.text:
The grand melee is too large for any field in the city, and so the empty Dragonpit receives it.

Seventy-seven knights are divided into eleven teams. They begin mounted, circling beneath the dome in colors bright as dragonfire, then crash together with a sound like a gatehouse falling. Men go down. Horses scream. Blunted weapons rise and fall, and those unhorsed fight on afoot until one team remains.

Alysanne forbids Jonquil Darke and Tom the Strummer from joining them, though neither takes the command kindly. I cannot fault her. This is sport only by courtesy. From the royal gallery it looks very much like war.

#bold The last team standing must still turn upon itself. Only one knight can leave champion. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0005.a.text: End it before the pit drinks too much blood.

sotd_dragonpit.0006.desc.text:
By the end, the sand beneath the Dragonpit is churned to red mud.

Borys, Garon, and Ronnal Baratheon all make a brutal accounting of themselves. Harys Hogg, Alyn Bullock, Willam Stafford, Guyle the Cunning, and Alastor Reyne leave their marks as well. Two men are dead before the horns sound, and more than twoscore are carried or helped from the field.

Yet when the last shield is split and the last knight yields, it is Ser Lucamore Strong who remains standing. His helm is dented, his surcoat torn, and his grin entirely unrepentant as the crowd names him champion of the melee.

#bold The Dragonpit has seen its first blood, and the realm will speak of this day for years. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0006.a.text: Crown the champion. Then send for the maesters.

sotd_dragonpit.0010.desc.text:
Eight months into the great work on Rhaenys's Hill, and the first truth of building has announced itself: stone is cheap, but the men who shape it are not. The master of the stonemasons' guild comes before the throne, cap literally in hand, to report that the coin set aside for the foundations has run dry before the foundations have - and that half his best men are drifting off to easier work on merchants' manses.

The work will not stop, he hastens to add. It will merely... slow. Unless, of course, the crown wished to open its purse a little wider, in which case he could put three hundred more men on the hill by the new moon, working double shifts by torchlight.

#bold Every great work eats gold. The question is only how fast I wish it to eat. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0010.a.text: Open the purse. Three hundred more men by the new moon.

sotd_dragonpit.0010.b.text: The crown is not a bottomless purse. It takes what time it takes.

sotd_dragonpit.0011.desc.text:
A ship out of Lys has brought a curious visitor to court: a master builder who names himself a descendant of the stonewrights of old Valyria, and who has heard - all the world has heard, it seems - that the dragon king is raising a great dome upon a hill. He has studied the drawings in the harbormaster's office, he says, uninvited, and pronounces them 'admirable, for Andal work.'

He then unrolls drawings of his own: cranes of a design our masons have never seen, scaffolds that climb with the wall, a method for raising the dome's ribs in half the time. The septons mutter about Valyrian sorcery; my own master builder mutters rather louder about foreign vultures. But I have looked at the drawings, and the drawings are #italic better#!.

#bold Genius asks a steep fee. It is still cheaper than mediocrity. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0011.a.text: Hire him. The septons can mutter.

sotd_dragonpit.0011.b.text: Westerosi stone shall be raised by Westerosi hands.

sotd_dragonpit.0012.desc.text:
The dome's great ribs stand against the sky now, and the whole city cranes its neck at them - but the walls beneath eat stone faster than the quarries of the Crownlands can cut it. The master of works lays the arithmetic before me: at the present rate of supply, the work will crawl for years yet, with the finest masons in the realm standing idle between barge-loads.

Or: the crown charters a fleet of stone-barges to run day and night from the deep quarries up the coast, and the flow of stone doubles. The harbourmasters have the ships. The quarrymen have the stone. All that is wanting, as ever, is the gold.

#bold I can see it finished from the walls of my keep - if I am willing to pay to see it sooner. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0012.a.text: Buy the barges. I will see the dome crowned in my prime.

sotd_dragonpit.0012.b.text: The stone will come as the stone comes.

sotd_dragonpit.0013.desc.text:
The master of works comes before the throne wearing the expression of a man who scarcely believes his own ledgers: the great work on Rhaenys's Hill is all but done - #bold years ahead of every projection#!.

The royal gold bore fruit. The extra crews, the foreign cranes, the barge-fleets of stone - each purchase fed the next, until the hill swarmed like a kicked anthill from first light to last torch. The last of the dome's plates is being set as he speaks; the great bronze doors are hung; the smiths are polishing the hinges.

#bold They said it would take the better part of a decade. Gold, well spent, is time. #!

sotd_dragonpit.0013.a.text: Then let us open the doors.

great_project_type_sotd_great_dragonpit_.text: The greatest structure ever raised in King's Landing: a colossal dome of stone and iron upon Rhaenys's Hill, beneath which the dragons of House Targaryen may be housed, sheltered, and tamed. Its construction is the work of years and a king's fortune in gold.

sotd_great_dragonpit_location_tt.text: Can only be raised on Rhaenys's Hill in King's Landing.

sotd_great_dragonpit_not_already_built_t.text: The Great Dragonpit has not yet been raised here.

fab_children.0900.desc.text: I have scarcely begun to mourn my mother before Rhaena descends upon Storm's End. She takes [storm_lord.GetTitledFirstName] by the beard in front of his whole court and lays Mother's death at his feet. He is to cherish the children Mother left behind. Should he take another wife or use them badly, she tells him, Storm's End will burn as Harrenhal burned. The lord answers boldly enough. His hands give him away.

fab_children.0900.a.text: My sister has said what I would have said.

fab_children.1000.desc.holder_dragon.text: [lord_tarth.GetTitledFirstName] sends ravens by every ship that escapes the Sapphire Isle. Myrish exiles have crossed the water, seized Tarth's eastern shore, and put villages to sword and flame. [aemon.GetFirstName] asks leave to mount [aemon_dragon.GetFirstName] and go ahead of the royal fleet. He would join Tarth's lord, learn the enemy's strength, and hold the heights until our sails appear. His reasoning is sound. I have heard worse from commanders twice his age, and I would give a great deal for a reason to refuse him.

fab_children.1006.t.text: The Ninth Day of the Third Moon

fab_children.1006.desc.rhaenys_dragon.text: On the ninth day of the third moon I walk [aemon.GetFirstName] out to [aemon_dragon.GetFirstName]. He has just learned that [rhaenys.GetFirstName] carries a child, and the news has made his leave-taking gentler without making it easier. He promises her a short war. To me he talks of winds and scouts and the fleet's slow mustering while [aemon_dragon.GetFirstName] claws at the stones. I fasten my son's cloak myself, as I did when he was a boy, and I tell him nothing of what I fear.

fab_children.1006.desc.rhaenys.text: On the ninth day of the third moon I walk [aemon.GetFirstName] down to the waiting ships. He has just learned that [rhaenys.GetFirstName] carries a child, and the news has made his leave-taking gentler without making it easier. He promises her a short war. To me he talks of winds and scouts and the fleet's slow mustering, as though careful plans could stand in for the thing neither of us will say. I fasten his cloak myself, as I did when he was a boy, and I tell him nothing of what I fear.

fab_children.1006.desc.dragon.text: On the ninth day of the third moon I walk [aemon.GetFirstName] out to [aemon_dragon.GetFirstName]. I fasten my son's cloak myself, as I did when he was a boy, and I tell him nothing of what I fear.

fab_children.1006.a.text: Go on, then. The wind is with you.

fab_children.1007.desc.holder_dragon.text: [aemon_dragon.GetFirstName]'s shadow crosses Tarth before [lord_tarth.GetTitledFirstName]'s horizon shows a single royal sail. The Myrish hold the eastern coast, but Tarth's ruler has withdrawn into the mountains with the men still loyal to the island. My son comes down among their campfires and begins the work I set him: counting ships, marking paths, preparing the heights for the army behind him. His raven is calm. I read it three times looking for what he has left out.

The other levels a crossbow at Tarth's lord, and my son is standing at his shoulder.

fab_children.1008.a.text: Read me the rest of it.

fab_children.1002.desc.text: The bolt meant for Tarth's lord misses its mark and takes [aemon.GetFirstName] through the throat. There is no last command and no farewell. No maester in that camp is quick enough to matter, and the men around my son can do nothing but hold him while his own blood drowns him. I read the raven once, then again, until the ink stops meaning anything at all. He will come home to the pyre, as our blood always does, and there will be nothing of him left to bury in the Westerosi way.

fab_children.1003.desc.text: The crossbowman looses, but [aemon.GetFirstName] turns at the shout. Iron tears the side of his neck instead of burying itself in his throat. Fever follows the wound, and for three nights the camp makes ready for a victory and a prince's pyre together. On the fourth morning he drinks, speaks, and wants to know whether the fleet has finally arrived.

fab_children.1003.a.text: Bring him home to me. Slowly, and by ship.

fab_children.1004.desc.text: [baelon.GetFirstName] does not ask for my leave. He mounts [baelon_dragon.GetFirstName], crosses the water, and falls upon the Myrish ships while men are still carrying his brother down from the mountain. Masts become torches. Decks split in the heat, and those who reach the shore find Tarth's swords waiting for them. The singers will call it a victory. It was a brother with nowhere to put his grief. When he returns he still smells of smoke, and I embrace him without a word about the leave he never asked for.

fab_children.1005.desc.text: I dismiss the court and sit with [alysanne.GetFirstName] where no councillor can watch us fail to be strong. We talk of the dragon's egg I laid in his cradle the night after he was born, of Daenerys ordering her little brother about the yard, of the prince we asked him to be without once asking what it weighed. Alysanne says his name until her voice gives out. Then we sit, and neither of us gets up to light the candles.

fab_children.1005.a.text: Say his name as often as you need to, Alysanne.

fab_children.1010.desc.baelon.text: Aemon's chair stands empty, but his place in the succession does not go into the ground with him. [senior_claimant.GetTitledFirstName], his living child, stands first in the senior line. [baelon.GetTitledFirstName] has age, service, and the preference of every lord who insists the crown must pass through a man. The laws I spent a lifetime ordering give me no clean answer here. The throne follows the elder branch, or the nearer man, or some other living claim of my blood, and I must say which.

fab_children.1010.desc.rhaenys.text: Aemon's chair stands empty, but his place in the succession does not go into the ground with him. [senior_claimant.GetTitledFirstName], his living child, stands first in the senior line, and others of my blood will press their own claims of age, sex, service, and proximity. The laws I spent a lifetime ordering give me no clean answer here. Whichever name I speak, someone in my own family learns today that it was not theirs.

fab_children.1010.a.text: Aemon's line does not end with Aemon. I name [senior_claimant.GetFirstName].

fab_children.1010.b.text: The realm needs a man grown. I name [baelon.GetFirstName].

fab_children.1010.c.text: Set every living claim of my blood before me.
