fab_children.1010.desc.none.text: Aemon's chair stands empty, and this time nothing of his remains to fill it. No child of his lives, no brother stands ready, and the petitions on my table argue for men and women I can scarcely place on a diagram. The laws I spent a lifetime ordering give me no clean answer here, and today they give me no candidate either.

fab_children.1010.d.text: There is no one. The matter waits, and it will cost me sleep.

fab_children.1014.desc.baelon.text: Alysanne receives my proclamation without a courtier present to soften it. She asks why [rhaenys.GetFirstName] should lose an inheritance that would have been hers without argument had she been born a son. I answer with peace, precedent, and the dangers that gather around a woman's crown. Every reason sounds colder spoken aloud to the woman who helped me build this realm. If a woman is of less use to me than a man, she says, then I can have no further need of her. Before I can call the words back she has her household making ready for Dragonstone.

fab_children.1014.desc.other.text: Alysanne receives my proclamation without a courtier present to soften it. She asks why [rhaenys.GetFirstName] should lose Aemon's inheritance to [chosen_heir.GetTitledFirstName]. I answer with peace, precedent, and the burdens of rule. Every reason sounds colder spoken aloud to the woman who helped me build this realm. If her counsel and a woman's claim mean so little, she says, then I can have no further need of her. Before I can call the words back she has her household making ready for Dragonstone.

fab_children.1014.desc.fallback.text: Alysanne receives my proclamation without a courtier present to soften it. She asks how I can answer one death by setting the senior line aside for [chosen_heir.GetTitledFirstName]. I answer with peace, precedent, and the burdens of rule. Every reason sounds colder spoken aloud to the woman who helped me build this realm. If her counsel means so little, she says, then I can have no further need of her. Before I can call the words back she has her household making ready for Dragonstone.

fab_children.1014.a.text: If you must go, then go.

fab_children.1015.desc.text: Alysanne reads the proclamation twice before she looks up. I have named [chosen_heir.GetTitledFirstName], keeping Aemon's place alive through his daughter rather than treating his death as the death of his whole line. My queen does not pretend the lords will swallow it quietly. She only takes my hand and says that today I remembered the law of blood as well as the habits of men.

fab_children.1015.a.text: Whatever resistance comes, we will meet it together.

fab_children.1011.desc.text: I let [maegelle.GetFirstName] speak where pride had kept me silent. She asks me to remember that [alysanne.GetFirstName] and I have survived too much together to let a throne stand between us now. My judgment will stand. My silence need not.

fab_children.1100.desc.text: Beside [alyssa_daughter.GetFirstName]'s bed, the joy of a newborn son curdles into dread. The bleeding has slowed, but a burning sickness has taken hold of her, and the maesters lower their eyes when I demand certainty. A septa kneels at the foot of the bed and prays to the Mother for mercy, and I have never in my life wanted so badly to believe she is heard. My laughing, fearless daughter reaches for my hand and asks me, twice, whether the boy is well.

fab_children.1100.a.text: I am not leaving this room.

fab_children.1100.a.tt.text: Baelon is shattered by Alyssa's death. He becomes #V Widowed#! and will honor her memory by never marrying again.

fab_children.1101.desc.text: Little [infant_aegon.GetFirstName] fights for every shallow breath. The wet nurse tells me he has his father's hands. The maester tells me nothing at all. In the hour of the wolf, when the oldest die and the youngest are born, the tiny fingers close once around mine and then fall still.

fab_children.1101.a.text: The Stranger is gentle with the very small. I will hold to that tonight.

fab_children.1150.desc.alysanne.text:
[alyssa_daughter.GetFirstName] followed [baelon.GetFirstName] from the day she could walk. For years he complained that his sister trailed him about like a puppy and had the poor judgment to be born a girl. She was six when a wooden sword came round in the training yard and broke her nose; it healed crooked, and she has never once asked a maester to trouble himself over it.

Somewhere between then and now the complaining stopped.

[alysanne.GetFirstName] settled the matter long ago and has never pretended otherwise. When other names were set beside our daughter’s, my queen answered that the girl was meant for [baelon.GetFirstName], and would hear nothing further about it.

fab_children.1150.desc.fallback.text: [alyssa_daughter.GetFirstName] followed [baelon.GetFirstName] from the day she could walk. For years he complained that his sister trailed him about like a puppy and had the poor judgment to be born a girl. She was six when a wooden sword came round in the training yard and broke her nose; it healed crooked, and she has never once asked a maester to trouble himself over it.\n\nSomewhere between then and now the complaining stopped. Her mother saw it before I did, and said so often enough that the court repeats it back to me still: that girl was meant for [baelon.GetFirstName], and no other name was ever going to be heard.

fab_children.1150.b.text: Their marriages are mine to arrange, and not yet.

fab_children.1150.b.tt.text: Alyssa and Baelon remain unbetrothed and may receive other proposals. Alyssa will not face her last childbed unless she weds Baelon and bears his son.

fab_children.1200.desc.text: [baelon.GetFirstName] comes back from the hunt complaining of a stitch in his side. By the hour of the bat he cannot stand. The pain settles deep in his belly, fever follows it, and every hour takes more out of him. I summon the Grand Maester and tell him to try everything the Citadel taught him, and then whatever it did not.

fab_children.1200.a.text: Spare nothing. Not one draught, not one hour.

fab_children.1202.desc.text: Five dawns have come and gone beside [baelon.GetFirstName]'s bed. The maesters' draughts dull the pain but cannot touch whatever is killing him beneath it. My son wakes long enough to know me, squeezes my hand, and says that he is tired. I tell him to sleep, then. I sit through the sixth dawn alone.

fab_children.1202.a.text: The Stranger has taken my son.

fab_children.1203.desc.text: I scarcely trust the Grand Maester when he tells me the swelling has eased. Then [baelon.GetFirstName] drinks without retching, sleeps without fever, and wakes demanding to know how long I mean to keep him abed. The recovery is slow. Every step of it gives me back a son I had already begun to bury.

fab_children.1203.a.text: Reward every hand that tended him.

fab_children.1250.desc.text: Every night [maegelle.GetFirstName] reads from the #italic Seven-Pointed Star#! before she sleeps. She is gentle where some of her sisters are fierce, quiet where the court demands display, and happiest when a septa lets her tend a sick child or copy out a page of doctrine. Alysanne reminds me of the promise she made the Mother at this daughter's birth: one girl given to the Faith in thanks. I expected tears when we put it to her. Maegelle asks when she may begin.

fab_children.1250.a.text: Then Oldtown has her, and the Seven a servant better than I deserve.

fab_children.1260.desc.text: Neither sword nor horse nor dragon has ever held [vaegon.GetFirstName]'s attention for long. Books do. The Grand Maester tells me plainly that my son wants the patience for ravens and the warmth for a castle, but that the Citadel might yet make an archmaester of him if numbers and higher mysteries are allowed to take his life. I tell Vaegon that a ship sails for Oldtown within the fortnight. For once I almost see him smile. “Yes, Father,” he says. “Good.”

fab_children.1260.b.text: A Prince of the Blood will not be a servant.

fab_children.1300.desc.rodrik_holder.text: When I ask [daella.GetFirstName] what she remembers of the Vale and of [eyrie_lord.GetTitledFirstName]'s court, she speaks warmly of its courtesy, and warmest of all about [rodrik.GetTitledFirstName]'s kindness to her. Gentleness will matter more to this daughter than splendor. I could also leave her hand unpromised a while longer and look for another man worth her trust.

fab_children.1300.desc.rodrik.text: When I ask [daella.GetFirstName] what she remembers of the Eyrie, she speaks warmly of its courtesy, and warmest of all about [rodrik.GetTitledFirstName]'s kindness to her. Gentleness will matter more to this daughter than splendor. I could also leave her hand unpromised a while longer and look for another man worth her trust.

fab_children.1300.desc.fallback.text: When I ask [daella.GetFirstName] what she remembers of the Eyrie, her answer is all courtesy and no hope. The Arryn boy once spoken of for her is beyond reach now, by death or by another man's contract. Gentleness will matter more to this daughter than splendor, and I would sooner keep her waiting than hand her to the wrong house.

fab_children.1300.a.text: Then it will be [rodrik.GetTitledFirstName]. She will have kindness, at least.

fab_children.1300.b.text: No promises yet. There may be a better man for her.

fab_children.1300.b.tt.text: Daella remains unbetrothed and may receive another marriage proposal.

fab_children.1301.desc.text: Grave news comes down from the Eyrie. [eyrie_lady.GetTitledFirstName] has taken suddenly ill, and the Vale's maesters hold little hope of her. I cannot welcome a death that clears Daella's road. I can only notice that the road has opened.

fab_children.1301.a.text: The Vale buries her first. My daughter’s name can wait on their grief.

fab_children.1310.desc.text: [alysanne.GetFirstName] is climbing onto Silverwing before [daella.GetFirstName]'s letter has left my hand. Our daughter is with child and frightened, and my queen will not have the width of the realm between them for it. I tell myself the Eyrie's maesters are skilled. Alysanne does not argue. She only looks at me the way she looked at me when I dismissed the first warning about this match.

fab_children.1310.a.text: Fly fast. I will send word ahead to the Eyrie.

fab_children.1311.desc.text: One mercy and one cruelty come in the same raven. [daella.GetFirstName] has borne a healthy girl, and the labor has left her burning with a fever the maesters cannot reach. She is not alone. I am the width of a kingdom away, and the raven was days in coming. In the sept below they are already lighting candles to the Mother, which is what men do when the maesters have stopped promising.

fab_children.1311.a.text: I forced too much, too soon. Forgive me, sweet girl.

fab_children.1400.desc.holder.text: Alysanne proposes [white_harbor_lord.GetTitledFirstName] for [viserra.GetFirstName]. The lord of White Harbor is older than our daughter and has been married before, but he is canny, courteous, and master of the greatest port in the North. Viserra hears only age and distance. If her mother admires the man so greatly, she says, her mother is welcome to marry him herself. Beneath the insult sits another ambition. Viserra has been watching the Iron Throne for years, and an unwed brother would keep her close to it.

fab_children.1400.desc.fallback.text: Alysanne's White Harbor match for [viserra.GetFirstName] has come to nothing. The lord she chose is dead, or else pledged elsewhere. Viserra takes the failure for a victory and turns her eyes back toward the Iron Throne. If a brother of hers is still unwed, the old customs of our blood offer one road. Otherwise her hand stays unpromised until I find something better.

fab_children.1400.a.text: Approve the match with White Harbor.

fab_children.1400.b.text: Find Viserra a better match than White Harbor.

fab_children.1400.b.tt.text: No royal betrothal is made. Viserra remains free to receive another proposal.

fab_children.1401.desc.text: On the eve of her departure [viserra.GetFirstName] begs one last night among the friends of her girlhood, and I allow it. The rest I have from the gold cloaks and from companions too frightened to lie well: inn after inn, wine and laughter and all the freedom she was certain White Harbor would take from her, then a race home through the dark in the hour of the owl. A mare came down in the Street of Flour. They carry her to me before dawn with her neck broken, and she cannot hear a word I say.

fab_children.1403.desc.kingsguard.text:
The hammering on the door comes in the hour of the wolf, and it is [bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] of the Kingsguard who brings her, white cloak spoiled to the elbow and my daughter senseless in his arms. [alysanne.GetFirstName] is out of the bed before I am.

[bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] tells it to me as the companions told it to him, and no two of them told it alike: inn after inn, a race home through the dark, a mare down in the Street of Flour. By every reckoning [viserra.GetFirstName] should have gone into the stones head-first. She did not. Whether her hands remembered what the wine had drowned, or the Mother was minding a girl who had not thought to ask her, I will never be told plainly. Two ribs are broken and there is wine still sour on her.

When the maester has gone she opens her eyes, sees the pair of us standing over her, and has the gall to smile.

fab_children.1403.desc.kingsguard_alone.text:
The hammering on the door comes in the hour of the wolf, and it is [bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] of the Kingsguard who brings her, white cloak spoiled to the elbow and my daughter senseless in his arms.

[bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] tells it to me as the companions told it to him, and no two of them told it alike: inn after inn, a race home through the dark, a mare down in the Street of Flour. By every reckoning [viserra.GetFirstName] should have gone into the stones head-first. She did not. Whether her hands remembered what the wine had drowned, or the Mother was minding a girl who had not thought to ask her, I will never be told plainly. Two ribs are broken and there is wine still sour on her.

When the maester has gone she opens her eyes, sees me standing over her alone, and has the gall to smile.

fab_children.1403.desc.captain.text:
The hammering on the door comes in the hour of the wolf, and it is [bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] who brings her, mail still on him and my daughter senseless in his arms. [alysanne.GetFirstName] is out of the bed before I am.

[bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] tells it to me as the companions told it to him, and no two of them told it alike: inn after inn, a race home through the dark, a mare down in the Street of Flour. By every reckoning [viserra.GetFirstName] should have gone into the stones head-first. She did not. Whether her hands remembered what the wine had drowned, or the Mother was minding a girl who had not thought to ask her, I will never be told plainly. Two ribs are broken and there is wine still sour on her.

When the maester has gone she opens her eyes, sees the pair of us standing over her, and has the gall to smile.

fab_children.1403.desc.captain_alone.text:
The hammering on the door comes in the hour of the wolf, and it is [bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] who brings her, mail still on him and my daughter senseless in his arms.

[bedchamber_witness.GetFirstName] tells it to me as the companions told it to him, and no two of them told it alike: inn after inn, a race home through the dark, a mare down in the Street of Flour. By every reckoning [viserra.GetFirstName] should have gone into the stones head-first. She did not. Whether her hands remembered what the wine had drowned, or the Mother was minding a girl who had not thought to ask her, I will never be told plainly. Two ribs are broken and there is wine still sour on her.

When the maester has gone she opens her eyes, sees me standing over her alone, and has the gall to smile.

fab_children.1403.desc.fallback.text:
They carry [viserra.GetFirstName] up to our chamber in the hour of the wolf, senseless, with wine still sour on her and two ribs broken.

What I have of it comes secondhand and drunk: inn after inn, a race home through the dark, a mare down in the Street of Flour. By every reckoning she should have gone into the stones head-first. She did not. Whether her hands remembered what the wine had drowned, or the Mother was minding a girl who had not thought to ask her, no one can tell me.

When the maester has gone she opens her eyes, sees me standing over her, and has the gall to smile.

fab_children.1403.a.text: You will hear me before you sleep. White Harbor waits on a maester now.

fab_children.1403.b.text: The Seven kept you when I could not. I will not spend that gift shouting.

fab_children.1490.desc.text: [saera.GetFirstName] has gathered five young courtiers around her. [braxton.GetFirstName] Beesbury, whom the court already calls the Stinger for his tongue, is handsome, proud, and dangerously pleased with himself. [jonah.GetFirstName] Mooton and red-haired [roy.GetFirstName] Connington are heirs with more courage than caution. [alys_turnberry.GetFirstName] Turnberry and [perianne.GetFirstName] Moore match my daughter in age, in beauty, and in appetite for mischief. They feast and hawk and hunt and sail as one company. I see harmless youth in their laughter, and also the beginning of a court inside my court.

fab_children.1490.a.text: Under my roof, where I can see them. Better that than Flea Bottom.

fab_children.1490.b.text: This is not proper company for a princess.

fab_children.1500.t.text: Tom Turnip at the Blue Pearl

fab_children.1500.desc.text: The fool Tom Turnip is found at a pleasure house called the Blue Pearl, so drunk he can scarcely stand. [braxton.GetFirstName], [jonah.GetFirstName], and [roy.GetFirstName] are there beside him, laughing at whatever humiliation carried a royal fool into such a place. The servants say this is no single night's folly. For more than a year Saera's companions have been trading rooms and gifts and secrets beneath my own roof. I have let the rumors pass because I wanted them to be nothing. They are not nothing.

fab_children.1500.a.text: Confine the men. Alysanne and I will learn the truth.

fab_children.1501.desc.text: Alysanne questions the girls apart. Perianne Moore weeps. Alys Turnberry confesses that she is with child and cannot say with any certainty which of the young men fathered it. The stories differ in small details and agree in every important one. Saera was not led astray by one seducer. She chose the game, she kept it going, and she made her friends players in it. My queen brings me their answers with her anger held so tightly that her hands shake.

fab_children.1501.a.text: Bring Saera before the Iron Throne.

fab_children.1502.desc.text: [saera.GetFirstName] denies nothing. Braxton Beesbury, Jonah Mooton, and Roy Connington have all been her lovers. When I demand to know which man she means to wed, she smiles and offers to take all three, as Aegon the Conqueror took two wives. Then she invokes Maegor as well, and the name empties the hall of sound. I hear my daughter set her appetites beside a conqueror's, and something in me goes very quiet. Across the hall Alysanne's eyes find mine. She is asking me not to say the thing I am about to say.

fab_children.1502.a.text: Confine her. I will judge every culprit.

fab_children.1502.b.text: She is the blood of the dragon. I will hear no more of this.

fab_children.1503.desc.text: Confinement holds [saera.GetFirstName] less than a night. She slips her guards, crosses the city, and is taken at the doors of the Dragonpit. Whether she meant to claim a dragon or only to frighten me, I cannot know. I know what a dragon in her present temper would make of a family disgrace. I have her locked high in a tower under constant guard. The men who shared her sport will face judgment below.

fab_children.1503.a.text: No more evasions. I will pass sentence.

fab_children.1507.desc.text: Jonah Mooton accepts marriage to Perianne Moore and the work of making something honorable out of their folly. Roy Connington is offered the Wall or ten years across the narrow sea, and chooses exile. Alys Turnberry will go to a motherhouse until her child is born. Only Braxton Beesbury refuses every mercy. The Stinger demands trial by combat, certain that youth and strength and a morningstar will shame whatever grey champion I put in front of him.

fab_children.1507.a.text: The others have their sentences. Bring Beesbury before me.

fab_children.1508.desc.text: Braxton stands before the throne in polished armor, his arrogance untouched by chains. “Then I choose trial by combat. Which of these old men do you mean for me to fight?” I am down the steps before any of my Kingsguard can answer him. Behind him, [saera.GetFirstName] is staring at me as though she has never seen her father before.

fab_children.1508.a.text: This old man. The one whose daughter you seduced and despoiled.

fab_children.1509.desc.text: We meet in full armor with our shields up. He carries a morningstar and all the strength of nineteen years. I carry Blackfyre and the patience of a man who has outlived a war, a rebellion, and most of the people he began with. He comes at me the moment the herald steps back, hammering iron against my shield, certain that age must give way if it is struck often enough. I give ground. I let him spend pride as though it were strength. Then I begin to press forward.

fab_children.1509.a.text: Then the Warrior judges between us.

fab_children.1511.desc.text: His blows slow. The shield sags, the morningstar drags at his arm, and when he stumbles Blackfyre's point finds the narrow opening of his visor. The yard is silent before the body has finished settling. My daughter does not look away, and neither do I. Afterward I give the order that sends [saera.GetFirstName] to Oldtown, where prayer and discipline may do what my anger cannot.

fab_children.1511.a.text: The Silent Sisters will receive her.

fab_children.1513.desc.text: The Stinger's morningstar breaks my guard and puts me down in the dirt. The yard erupts before the Kingsguard can close around us. By the law I invoked myself, Braxton Beesbury has proved his innocence before gods and men. By every face in that yard, he has also wounded the crown. I will not have him murdered for winning a trial I demanded. Saera must still go from this court before her defiance finishes what is left of my family.

fab_children.1513.a.text: Honor the trial. Then Saera goes to Oldtown.

fab_children.1514.desc.maegelle.text: [maegelle.GetFirstName] writes from Oldtown. [saera.GetFirstName]'s silks have been taken, her hair shorn, her days divided among prayer, silence, rough cloth, and humble labor. Maegelle does not pretend her sister has embraced any of it. She asks me for patience and promises to instruct Saera herself. My gentle daughter has made peace between Alysanne and me before now.

fab_children.1514.desc.fallback.text: The motherhouse writes from Oldtown. [saera.GetFirstName]'s silks have been taken, her hair shorn, her days divided among prayer, silence, rough cloth, and humble labor. The septas do not pretend she has embraced any of it. They ask me for patience, and I grant it, though every report says my daughter studies doors and walls more diligently than scripture.

fab_children.1514.a.text: Firm, then. Never cruel. I have seen what cruelty makes of my blood.

fab_children.1515.desc.holder.text: After a year and a half the motherhouse finds an empty bed and a novice's robe left folded on it. [saera.GetFirstName] has gone from Oldtown, taken ship, and crossed the narrow sea to Lys, where she now lives under [lys_ruler.GetTitledFirstName]'s peace. She has traded prayer for a pleasure garden and my judgment for her own keeping. I send men to search docks she left weeks ago. It is something to do with my hands.

fab_children.1515.desc.fallback.text: After a year and a half the motherhouse finds an empty bed and a novice's robe left folded on it. [saera.GetFirstName] has gone from Oldtown, taken ship, and crossed the narrow sea to Lys. She has traded prayer for a pleasure garden and my judgment for her own keeping. I send men to search docks she left weeks ago. It is something to do with my hands.

fab_children.1515.a.text: For now, the narrow sea stands between us.

fab_children.1504.t.text: The Daughter I Will Not Name

fab_children.1504.desc.text: Years pass. [saera.GetFirstName] leaves Lys for Volantis, grows rich, and comes to keep a house grander than many lords possess. When someone asks whether I will call her home, I answer that I have no daughter in Volantis. The court is satisfied with that. I am not, and I can still remember fastening her cloak for her when she was too small to manage the clasp.

fab_children.1504.a.text: I will not send for her.

fab_children.1505.desc.text: I know [saera.GetFirstName]'s hand before I break the seal. The letter comes from Volantis, written by a woman who owns her own house and asks me for neither coin nor rescue. She does not excuse what passed between us, and neither do I. She asks one thing only: whether a daughter may cross the sea and speak with her father, without chains or vows or old accusations waiting for her at the quay.

fab_children.1505.a.text: Tell her there will be no chains on the quay.

fab_children.1600.desc.text: [gael.GetFirstName] keeps out of my sight and away from the household, and has done for a turn of the moon. A traveling singer has left court without taking his leave of anyone, and the servants have begun counting months on their fingers. I have learned what silence can cost this family.

fab_children.1600.a.text: Gently. She is not to be frightened.

fab_children.1601.desc.text: Grief has hollowed [gael.GetFirstName] out. The singer left her with a child. The child came too early and never cried. There was no name given and no septon called, because to call one would have been to tell the realm. She has carried all of it alone, certain that shame was the only answer she would get if she asked for help. I tell her she is not alone. I cannot tell whether the words reach her.

fab_children.1601.a.text: She is not to be left alone. Not for an hour.

fab_children.1602.desc.text: [gael.GetFirstName] is standing where the black water folds around her feet when I reach the shore. She looks back once, not startled, only tired, and walks on. I call her name. I am still calling it when the tide takes her out of sight. The Faith has no gentle word for what she has done. It will not be said over her while I draw breath.

fab_children.1603.desc.alysanne.text: I follow [alysanne.GetFirstName] down to the shore and we reach [gael.GetFirstName] before the tide can have her. Our daughter breaks in her mother's arms and speaks at last of the singer, of the lost babe, of the shame that walked her down to the water. We take her home between us.

fab_children.1603.desc.jaehaerys.text: [gael.GetFirstName] is knee-deep in it when I reach the shore, and the tide does not get her. My daughter breaks in my arms and speaks at last of the singer, of the lost babe, of the shame that walked her down to the water. I carry her back up the strand myself.

fab_children.1603.a.text: Come away from the water, sweetling.

fab_children.2000.desc.text: Baelon is scarcely buried before the petitions reach the Red Keep. One letter argues for the senior branch, another for the nearest living man, a third for age and proven service. Lords who agree on nothing else agree that delay will harden every preference into a faction. I have spent a reign closing the wounds left by disputed crowns. I will not leave a fresh one under my shroud.

fab_children.2000.a.vaegon.text: Summon Vaegon and hear his counsel.

fab_children.2000.a.citadel.text: Send to the Citadel and hear its Seneschal.

fab_children.2000.a.council.text: Hear the counsel of the most learned men in Westeros.

fab_children.2000.b.text: The choice is mine. I will name an heir now.

fab_children.2002.desc.vaegon.text: [vaegon.GetFirstName] returns from the Citadel in a maester's robes, leaner and greyer and no freer with courtesy than the day he left. I set the rival claims before him and ask which name will keep the peace. My son refuses to give me one. “Let the lords decide,” he says. Not a council of flatterers in my chamber, but every lord with a claim and every lord sworn to judge it. The realm may accept from its own assembled voice what it would resist from an old king's grief.

fab_children.2002.desc.citadel.text: The Citadel sends its Seneschal. [council_maester.GetFirstName] comes up from Oldtown with the road still on [council_maester.GetHerHis] robes and spends no more courtesy on a king than the chain requires. I set the rival claims before [council_maester.GetHerHim] and ask which name will keep the peace. The answer is that there is no name to give. “Let the lords decide,” [council_maester.GetSheHe] says. Not a council of flatterers in my chamber, but every lord with a claim and every lord sworn to judge it. The realm may accept from its own assembled voice what it would resist from an old king's grief.

fab_children.2002.desc.grand_maester.text: I put the question to the Grand Maester, who has kept the ravens and the ledgers of this reign. [council_maester.GetFirstName] weighs the rival claims a long while and then declines to give me a name at all. “Let the lords decide,” [council_maester.GetSheHe] says. Not a council of flatterers in my chamber, but every lord with a claim and every lord sworn to judge it. The realm may accept from its own assembled voice what it would resist from an old king's grief.

fab_children.2002.desc.maester.text: I put the question to a maester of my court. [council_maester.GetFirstName] hears the rival claims out to the end and then declines to give me a name at all. “Let the lords decide,” [council_maester.GetSheHe] says. Not a council of flatterers in my chamber, but every lord with a claim and every lord sworn to judge it. The realm may accept from its own assembled voice what it would resist from an old king's grief.

fab_children.2002.desc.fallback.text: My councillors lay the rival claims across the table until there is more ink than wood in front of us, and no name among them promises peace. At last one of them offers a harder answer: let every lord with a claim be heard, and let the assembled realm judge among them. The lords may accept from their own gathered voice what they would resist from an old king's grief.

fab_children.2002.a.text: Then I will summon a Great Council.

fab_children.2002.b.text: No. I will not surrender the judgment of my house to lesser lords.

fab_children.2003.desc.holder.text: I choose Harrenhal, where [harrenhal_lord.GetTitledFirstName] can house more claimants than any living lord should wish to meet at once. Ravens go out from the Red Keep in every direction. For half a year the roads fill with banners, wagons, sworn swords, petitioners, hedge lords, and princely entourages. More than five hundred may sleep within the walls; twice that number will raise tents beneath the black towers. I stay in King's Landing. If the council is to speak freely, it must not mistake my presence for an answer.

fab_children.2003.desc.fallback.text: I choose Harrenhal, whose ruined halls can house more claimants than any living lord should wish to meet at once. Ravens go out from the Red Keep in every direction. For half a year the roads fill with banners, wagons, sworn swords, petitioners, hedge lords, and princely entourages. More than five hundred may sleep within the walls; twice that number will raise tents beneath the black towers. I stay in King's Landing. If the council is to speak freely, it must not mistake my presence for an answer.

fab_children.2003.a.text: Summon them to Harrenhal. Every claimant, and every lord sworn to judge one.

fab_children.2004.desc.three.text: Dispatches from Harrenhal arrive in bundles thick enough to bend a maester's back. The claims of [heir_candidate_1.GetTitledFirstName], [heir_candidate_2.GetTitledFirstName], and [heir_candidate_3.GetTitledFirstName] are among those getting a serious hearing, but no two letters agree on what ought to matter most. Lord Baratheon writes that the elder branch cannot be passed over without unmaking every inheritance in the Stormlands. Lord Hightower answers that no woman has ever sat the Iron Throne and none ever should. A Blackwood and a Bracken have found the same side of the question, which unsettles me more than the quarrel did. I stay in King's Landing and read every name that survives them.

fab_children.2004.desc.two.text: Dispatches from Harrenhal arrive in bundles thick enough to bend a maester's back. The claims of [heir_candidate_1.GetTitledFirstName] and [heir_candidate_2.GetTitledFirstName] are getting a serious hearing, but no two letters agree on what ought to matter most. Lord Baratheon writes that the elder branch cannot be passed over without unmaking every inheritance in the Stormlands. Lord Hightower answers that no woman has ever sat the Iron Throne and none ever should. A Blackwood and a Bracken have found the same side of the question, which unsettles me more than the quarrel did. I stay in King's Landing and read every name that survives them.

fab_children.2004.desc.one.text: Dispatches from Harrenhal arrive in bundles thick enough to bend a maester's back. [heir_candidate_1.GetTitledFirstName] stands foremost among the living claims, and even one name sets Storm’s End against Oldtown, and a Blackwood agreeing with a Bracken for the first time in three hundred years. I stay in King's Landing and read every argument the council sends me.

fab_children.2005.desc.council.text: The sealed judgments are opened in front of me. Arguments, tallies, warnings, names, and one septon’s letter begging me to remember that the Father judges kings last and hardest. Everything except a law that might have spared me the act itself. Deaths, marriages, vows, and choices made across my whole reign have shaped a family no maester's diagram reduces to a rule. The council has spoken. I must put a living face beneath the words #italic heir to the Iron Throne#!.

fab_children.2005.desc.fallback.text: I have refused myself the shelter of a council. The living claims are brought to me bare, with no tally to divide the blame afterward. I must put a living face beneath the words #italic heir to the Iron Throne#!, and the choice will be mine, and so will every grievance it makes.

fab_children.2007.desc.aemon.text: Aemon's death has left more than an empty chair. I have the living members of House Targaryen brought before me one at a time. A pedigree can trace a right through the dead. Only the living can inherit. I mean to look at each of them before I choose.

fab_children.2007.desc.council.text: The council's register runs on past the first page. Each leaf carries the name of a living Targaryen and the arguments made for and against that claim. No tally can choose in my place. I mean to look at every eligible member of my House before I bind the realm to one of them.

fab_children.2006.desc.council.text: The last raven from Harrenhal is put into my hand. Beside the council's arguments I write the name that will govern the realm after me: [gc_winner.GetTitledFirstName]. Whether I have followed the lords or defied them, the uncertainty is over. I order the court assembled and the succession proclaimed before rumor can sharpen itself into rebellion.

fab_children.2006.desc.direct.text: I write the name that will govern the realm after me: [gc_winner.GetTitledFirstName]. No council shields the choice and no tally dilutes it. This is the judgment of Jaehaerys, first of his name, made while I still have the strength to enforce it. I order the court assembled and the succession proclaimed before rumor can sharpen itself into rebellion.

fab_children.2006.a.text: Open the throne room. The realm will hear my judgment.

fab_children.2001.desc.text: I rise before the Iron Throne and name [gc_winner.GetTitledFirstName] my lawful heir. The cheers come first, then the muttering, then the careful silence of men already reckoning what my judgment has cost them. No council could have made every line of my blood equal, and no king could have satisfied every claimant. The realm would have bled far longer over a question left open than it will over an answer it dislikes.

fab_children.2001.a.text: Write it into the record. No lord leaves this hall able to say he did not hear.

fab_children.heir_candidates.review.text: Show me the first names again.

fab_aemon_tarth_survivor_modifier_desc.text: A Myrish crossbow bolt passed a finger's width from the throat on Tarth. The scar has not faded.

fab_alyssa_childbed_survivor_modifier_de.text: Survived a labor the maesters had already given up as fatal.

fab_alyssa_late_fertility_modifier_desc.text: The maesters had thought her years of bearing behind her. They were wrong.

fab_baelon_recovered_modifier_desc.text: A sickness of the belly that should have been the end of him, and was not.

fab_viserra_broken_ribs_modifier.text: Thrown in the Street of Flour

fab_viserra_broken_ribs_modifier_desc.text: Two ribs cracked against the cobbles, bound tight by a maester who did not trouble to hide what he thought of the hour she came home at. They will knit. Until they do she cannot draw a full breath without remembering the fall.

fab_infant_vigour_modifier_desc.text: This child came into the world ailing and was not expected to keep it. Someone refused to let go.

jaehaerys.0001.desc.text:
Word reaches me as I shelter far from court: Maegor is dead. They found my uncle slumped upon the Iron Throne, pale and cold, his own blood pooled beneath him and the barbs of that cruel seat sunk deep into his flesh. Whether the throne claimed him or a hand unseen, no man can say - and few will mourn.

I will not wait for leave. I mount Vermithor, the Bronze Fury, and turn his wings toward King's Landing. The lords and the smallfolk will look up and see a dragon returning - not to burn them, as Maegor did, but to end the terror at last.

I am Jaehaerys of House Targaryen. I mean to take my father's throne and my uncle's ruin and make of them something worthy. My mother shall guide my hand, and Lord Rogar his sword. The work of healing a broken realm begins now.

jaehaerys.0002.desc.text:
The war for the throne is won before it is truly begun. Most of my uncle's supporters have fled the city; the few who remained, I have taken in chains.

Yet I am a boy of four-and-ten, and a boy cannot rule the Seven Kingdoms alone. So it is agreed. My mother, the Dowager Queen Alyssa Velaryon, shall rule as Queen Regent until I come of age. And Lord Rogar Baratheon of Storm's End - the strong sword who marched to set me upon the throne - I name Lord Protector of the Realm and Hand of the King, to guide my hand in the years to come.

#bold Together, we shall begin to bind the wounds my uncle left. #!

jaehaerys.0003.desc.text: The realm is full of men who served the Cruel - lords who bent the knee to my uncle, gaolers and confessors who tortured my brother Viserys to death in the black cells, and Maegor's own Kingsguard, white cloaks sworn to a monster.\n\nSome kneel and beg the black. Ser Harrold Langward, once Maegor's Lord Commander, kneels to no one - he denies my right to judge him and demands trial by combat. My mother and Lord Rogar counsel restraint, but the choice is mine alone. How shall the reign of Jaehaerys begin?

jaehaerys.0003.trial_tt.text: Ser Maladon Moore is executed for his part in the murder of Queen Tyanna. Ser Harrold Langward demands trial by combat; I would take up the sword myself, but the Queen Regent forbids it, and our champion Ser Gyles Morrigen strikes him down. Ser Jon Tollett, Ser Symond Crayne, Ser Olyver Bracken and Ser Raymund Mallery take the black.

jaehaerys.0003.option3.text: Pardon them all. The realm has bled enough.

jaehaerys.0003.exile_tt.text: Maegor's six are spared the sword and the Wall alike - but mercy is not restoration. Their white cloaks are taken from them, and they are exiled across the narrow sea, to live out their days as hedge knights at the Sealord's court in Braavos. They shall never again stand guard over a king of Westeros.

jaehaerys.0004.text: The King's Peace with the Faith

jaehaerys.0004.desc.text:
Word comes from the south: Septon Moon is dead, and the Poor Fellows who besieged Oldtown have melted away like snow. The long war between the dragon and the Seven can end at last - if I will let it.

I will. I swear that the Iron Throne shall protect and defend the Faith of the Seven for all time - but I will not raise the Warrior's Sons and Poor Fellows again, and the Faith Militant shall lay down its swords forever. I lift my uncle Maegor's bounties from the heads of the faithful, and pardon all who repent; in return, the Most Devout acknowledge the King's justice, and the High Septon himself agrees to set the crown upon my head at the Starry Sept. The road to Oldtown lies open.

#bold Men will say I am a king who reconciles, not one who burns. #!

jaehaerys.0004.option1.text: Then let us to Oldtown, and the crown.

jaehaerys.0005.text: A White Cloak for a Warrior's Son

jaehaerys.0005.desc.text:
There is one more oath to be sworn. Ser Joffrey Doggett kneels before me - once Grand Captain of the Warrior's Sons, the Red Dog who bore sword and star against my house in the name of the Seven. He is the finest blade the Faith Militant ever raised, and I would far rather have such a man guarding my back than see him hunted through the hills like a beast.

I offer him a white cloak and a place among my Kingsguard. He bows his head, sets aside the star of the Warrior's Sons, and takes the cloak, swearing to shield the king and the royal family with his life.

#bold A former foe of the crown becomes one of its truest swords. #!

jaehaerys.0006.desc.text:
In this, the nine-and-fortieth year after the Conquest, my mother the Dowager Queen weds Lord Rogar Baratheon in a wedding so lavish the smallfolk are already calling it the Golden Wedding. Storm's End empties its coffers; the feasting will run a fortnight.

I like Lord Rogar well enough, and I respect his strength. Yet he did not think to ask my leave before taking my mother to wife - and I am the King. He names it a love match; I am not so certain. A man who is already my Hand and Lord Protector now weds himself to the Queen as well. I wonder how much of Rogar's heart is truly for my mother, and how much is for the crown that sits so near his hand.

#bold I say nothing. A boy king learns to hold his tongue - and to remember. #!

jaehaerys.0006.option1.text: He might at least have asked my leave.

jaehaerys.0007.text: The War for the White Cloaks

jaehaerys.0007.desc.text:
Five white cloaks have hung empty since I cast out my uncle's Kingsguard, and my mother has a notion to fill them: let the finest knights of the realm win their places in a great tourney to follow her wedding. I agree - but I decree the contenders shall fight on foot, not horsed. A foe seldom strikes a king from the saddle.

For seven days they fight, and the jousting is soon forgotten amid wild melees and bloody duels; hundreds of knights vie with axe, spear and sword for the honour of the white. The smallfolk roar themselves hoarse for their favourites - Ser Willam Stafford, Ser Tom the Strummer, a mystery knight who proves to be the woman Jonquil Darke - but when the dust settles, five stand above the rest.

Ser Lorence Roxton, Ser Victor the Valiant, Ser Willam the Wasp, Ser Pate the Woodcock, and old one-eyed Ser Samgood of Sour Hill kneel before me. I bid them rise, sworn brothers of my Kingsguard.

#bold My white cloaks are seven once more. #!

jaehaerys.0008.desc.text:
The Golden Wedding done, Lord Rogar turns his ambition to me. A king must have a queen, he says, and my hand is the richest prize in the realm - a bride from Casterly Rock, perhaps, or Highgarden, to bind a great house to the throne. He has candidates already; my mother nods along. And for my sister Alysanne, some lord's heir far away.

They speak of alliances and armies. They do not speak of what Alysanne and I have known since we were children - that we love one another, and mean to wed no one else. I am the blood of the dragon, and the dragon does not bend to a Lord Protector's schemes.

#bold If they will not give us leave, we shall not ask it. #!

jaehaerys.0009.desc.text:
We tell no one. In the black before dawn, Alysanne and I steal from the Red Keep to the dragonpit, where Vermithor and Silverwing wait. The Bronze Fury spreads his wings, my sister's she-dragon answers with a cry, and we are gone into the night sky before the regents so much as stir.

Beneath us King's Landing shrinks to a scatter of torches, then the black water of the bay, and then only the wind and the wings and Alysanne laughing beside me. We fly east, toward the ancient seat of our house, where no Hand and no Septon can keep us apart.

#bold To Dragonstone - and to each other. #!

jaehaerys.0010.desc.text:
In the ancient sept of Dragonstone, beneath the painted gods and the smoke of a hundred candles, Septon Oswyck weds us. There is no court, no lords, no feast - only my sister's hand in mine, a few loyal witnesses, and the vows themselves.

We are man and wife now, Alysanne and I, king and queen in truth. The High Septon and the Most Devout may gnash their teeth; Lord Rogar may rage until Storm's End trembles. A marriage sworn before the Seven and made whole cannot be unmade.

#bold I take you, Alysanne, and no other, for all the days of my life. #!

jaehaerys.0010.option1.text: Let no one put us asunder.

jaehaerys.0011.desc.text:
The word reaches King's Landing within days, and the storm breaks. Lord Rogar is beside himself - cheated of his schemes, made a fool before the realm, roaring that the marriage must be annulled and the boy king brought to heel. My mother weeps, torn between her son and her new husband.

But rage as they might, the thing is done. I am wed, and soon I shall be a man grown and free of any regent's leash. Yet I am not blind: the Faith will not suffer a brother to bed his sister quietly. When I come into my crown in truth, the Seven will demand their reckoning - and I must be ready to answer it.

#bold The deed is done. Now let the Faith have its say. #!

jaehaerys.0011.option1.text: I am ready for whatever comes.

jaehaerys.0012.desc.text:
Balked of the marriage, Lord Rogar plays his last and boldest card. Before the small council he declares that a king who defies his Protector and beds his own sister is no fit king at all - and that the throne should pass to my niece Aerea, daughter of Aegon the Uncrowned, whose line ran senior to mine own. A girl of six, whom Rogar would rule through until she was grown and safely wed to a candidate of his choosing.

For a moment the chamber is silent. Then my mother the Queen Regent rises - and against her own husband, she speaks for me. One by one the council follows her: Lord Rogar's design is refused, and his reach for a puppet-queen dies on the council table.

#bold He has overreached, and the realm has seen it. #!

jaehaerys.0013.desc.text:
On the twentieth day of the ninth moon, in the fiftieth year since my grandsire's Conquest, I turn six-and-ten upon the windswept rock of Dragonstone. I am a man grown now, in the eyes of gods and men alike, and the regency ends as all regencies must. No Protector rules in my name; no Hand schemes to unmake my marriage. Alysanne stands beside me, my queen in truth.

Before I go to claim my throne in earnest, I send five knights of my Kingsguard ahead to King's Landing, to see that all is made ready for the king's return. The Red Keep is to be swept and its gates thrown open. The dragon comes home.

#bold Ready the city. In three days I fly for the capital. #!

jaehaerys.0013.option1.text: Have them make the city ready.

jaehaerys.0014.text: The King Returns to the Red Keep

jaehaerys.0014.desc.text:
Three days after my nameday I mount Vermithor and take wing from Dragonstone, and the Bronze Fury bears me over the bay to King's Landing. The smallfolk crowd the streets to cheer as my dragon circles the hill of Aegon and settles in the yard of the Red Keep.

My mother is waiting for me. There has been coldness between us - her marriage to Rogar, his schemes, the crisis over my own wedding - but she is my mother still, and I am her son, and we have both grieved and lost too much to remain estranged. We speak long and privately, and when we are done, the breach between us is healed. Whatever passed between me and her husband, the Dowager Queen Alyssa Velaryon and her king are reconciled.

#bold She is my mother. There will be peace between us. #!

jaehaerys.0015.desc.text:
A king must be served by able men, and my uncle and the regency alike left me a council of the idle, the timid, and the merely fortunate. So I set to work. Some I dismiss outright; some I confirm in their offices, having proven their worth; and to the empty seats I raise men of my own choosing.

Hardest of all to replace is my master of coin, Lord Edwell Celtigar - a man as greedy as he is useless, who understands the counting of his own coppers far better than the treasury of a realm. For a time I despair of finding his equal in incompetence's opposite. In the end I look beyond Westeros entirely, and name a shrewd Pentoshi named Rego Draz to keep the Crown's gold. I fill the lesser offices with my own men, and open the black cells and dungeons of King's Landing, that my uncle's prisoners may see the sun again.

#bold A new council for a new reign. #!

jaehaerys.0015.option1.text: Out with the old, in with the able.

jaehaerys.0016.desc.text:
One matter remains: Lord Rogar Baratheon. I summon him to the throne room and receive him seated upon the Iron Throne, my council ranged about me, that all might see it is a king who judges him now and no boy. Rogar comes expecting harsh words, perhaps worse - and he is not wrong to fear, for he reached for my crown and would have set a child in my place.

Yet I have not forgotten the other truth: that when Maegor's shadow lay over us all, it was Rogar's strong sword that shielded me and mine, and set me on this throne. So I temper justice with memory. I will pardon him - upon his oath that he shall never again speak a word against me or my queen, and that he shall be an honourable husband to my mother. And his brother Orryn, who on Rogar's word tried to steal the novice Rhaella from her motherhouse to raise a rival against me, I sentence to ten years' exile beyond the narrow sea.

When Rogar, humbled, asks whether the Crown will require hostages of House Baratheon, I say nothing. I only rise, and lead him out to where Vermithor waits - and let the Bronze Fury make my answer for me.

#bold Kneel, my lord, and let this be the end of it. #!

jaehaerys.0016.pardon_tt.text: Lord Rogar Baratheon is pardoned upon his oath, and sent home to Storm's End. His brother Orryn is exiled ten years.

jaehaerys.0016.dragon_tt.text: The king needs no hostages of House Baratheon - not while Vermithor lives. Lord Rogar takes the meaning well.

jaehaerys.0016.option1.text: I have not forgotten what you did for us. Be at peace.

jaehaerys.0016.option2.text: Hostages? Come, my lord - let me show you Vermithor.

jaehaerys.0016.option3.text: #bold (An Alternate History)#! I will NOT kneel to this boy and his sister-wife.

jaehaerys.0016.warpath_tt.text: ALTERNATE HISTORY: Refuse the dragon king's judgement. You take up the cause of Lord Rogar Baratheon, crown the girl Aerea Targaryen, and go to war for the Iron Throne. #bold You will play as Lord Rogar. #!

jaehaerys.0017.desc.text:
The Starry Sept of Oldtown is the oldest and holiest seat of the Faith in all Westeros, and beneath its great dome of black marble and crystal the light falls in a thousand colours upon the assembled Most Devout. Here, where the Andal kings of old were blessed, I kneel before the High Septon of the Seven.

He anoints me with the seven holy oils - upon my brow for the Father's justice, my eyes for the Crone's wisdom, my hands for the Warrior's strength, and so through all the Seven who are One. I bow my head and swear before gods and men to defend the Faith and rule justly over the realms of men. The old septon's hands tremble as he raises them over me in blessing.

#bold In the sight of the Seven, the anointing is done. #!

jaehaerys.0017.option1.text: I so swear, before the Seven Who Are One.

jaehaerys.0018.desc.text:
The High Septon lifts the crown - and sets it upon my brow. It is done. I rise, no longer a boy king holding a throne by the sufferance of regents, but an anointed sovereign, crowned and blessed before the eyes of the Seven and all the great lords of the realm.

The septon's voice rings out beneath the dome, and the herald takes up the cry, and it echoes from the crystal above:

#bold "All hail Jaehaerys of House Targaryen, the First of His Name, King of the Andals, the Rhoynar, and the First Men, Lord of the Seven Kingdoms, and Protector of the Realm!" #!

The hall thunders it back at me. The dragon and the Seven are reconciled, and my reign begins not in fire, but in blessing. They will call me the Conciliator.

jaehaerys.0019.desc.text:
There is a gentleness owed to the Faith now that the wars are done, and I mean to show it. My niece Rhaella - daughter of my late brother Aegon and my sister Rhaena, and twin to little Aerea - is a solemn, pious child, happier at her prayers than at any dance or feast.

So she is given to the Faith, and sent to a motherhouse at Oldtown to be raised among the septas, to take the white of a novice and one day swear her vows. A princess of House Targaryen serving the Seven: there is no truer sign that the dragon and the Faith are at peace. She goes willingly, and the Most Devout are well pleased.

#bold May the Mother watch over her, and the Crone light her way. #!

jaehaerys.0019.option1.text: She will be raised gently among the septas.

jaehaerys.0020.desc.text:
So this is how the dragon rewards the sword that saved him. Stripped of the Protectorship, sent home like a scolded boy, made to bend the knee to a stripling who beds his own sister in defiance of gods and men. I marched an army to set this ungrateful whelp upon the Iron Throne - and this is my thanks.

The sword is not yet sheathed. The Faith itself calls their marriage an abomination, and there is another with a better right: Aerea, daughter of Aegon the Uncrowned, of the elder line. A girl, yes - but a girl may be guided, and a realm ruled well through her. And I would not rise alone: the pious Reach, whose lands hold Oldtown and the Starry Sept and the High Septon himself, has no love for a king who weds his sister - the Lord of Highgarden would call his banners to Aerea's cause. Storm's End and the Reach need not kneel to Jaehaerys and Alysanne.

And yet - the boy rides Vermithor, and his sister Silverwing. My brother Orryn is banished, my seat watched, my wife the king's own mother. A wise man knows which storms to ride out.

#bold The storm gathers in my breast. Do I loose it - or swallow it? #!

jaehaerys.0020.option2.text: No. I swallow my pride, and keep the king's peace.

jaehaerys.0021.text: A Girl Upon the Iron Throne

jaehaerys.0021.desc.text:
It is done. The dragon king is fallen, his sister-queen scattered to the winds, and the great hall of the Red Keep echoes with a new cry: Aerea, First of Her Name, Queen of the Seven Kingdoms. She is but a child, sitting small and solemn upon that monstrous chair of melted swords - but the crown is on her brow, and it was my sword that put it there.

The realm is mine to shape now, through her. Or - the thought comes unbidden, gazing at that great black throne - a strong hand might do more than merely guide a queen. But no. She is my queen, and I made her. For now.

#bold The Iron Throne answers to House Baratheon at last. #!

jaehaerys.0021.option1.text: Rule through her. I am the power behind the throne.

jaehaerys.0021.option2.text: #bold (Play as Aerea)#! Take up the girl-queen herself.

jaehaerys.0022.desc.text:
They took Lord Rogar in chains to the foot of the Iron Throne, and there, before the whole court, King Jaehaerys had his head struck from his shoulders. The rebellion is broken. Aerea's cause is ash, her banners burned, and the storm that Rogar raised has blown itself out against the dragon's walls.

The lordship of Storm's End falls to me now, and with it the ruin of his ambition. What is left to House Baratheon is our seat, our pride, and the long memory of how close we came. The dragon reigns, and we endure - as we always have. The dream of a Baratheon-made throne dies upon the block.

#bold The storm is spent. But House Baratheon endures. #!

jaehaerys.0022.option1.text: We endure. There will be other days.

jaehaerys.0023.desc.text:
Word comes from the far west, from Fair Isle in the Sunset Sea. My elder sister Rhaena has known little joy in her life - wed first to our brother Aegon, whom Maegor slew, and then forced into our monstrous uncle's bed as one of his Black Brides. Thrice a queen, and thrice sorrowed. Small wonder she has fled the court and its dragons.

Now she has taken a new husband, on her own terms this time: Androw Farman, second son of the Lord of Fair Isle - a gentle, mild-mannered youth, no warrior and no schemer. It is no great love match, all say, and Rhaena weds him more for the quiet of Fair Isle than for the man himself. But it is her choice, freely made, and after all she has endured she has earned that much.

#bold May my sister find some measure of peace at last. #!

jaehaerys.0023.option1.text: I wish her well, and gladly.

jaehaerys.0024.desc.text:
The Protectorship is ended and the office of the Hand stands empty. Rogar Baratheon taught me the danger of a Hand who is also the mightiest lord in the realm, with armies and ambitions of his own. This time I will have a Hand who serves the Crown and not himself - a steady man, wise in coin and law and the workings of the realm, whom I can trust as I trust few others.

I find him near to home. Lord Daemon Velaryon of Driftmark, the Lord of the Tides and my mother's kinsman, has served ably as my master of ships. He is no warlord and no schemer, only a capable and loyal man - and that is precisely what I need. I name him Hand of the King, and so begins a partnership that I mean to last the length of my reign.

#bold Rise, Lord Daemon, Hand of the King. #!

jaehaerys.0024.hand_tt.text: Lord Daemon Velaryon, the Lord of the Tides, is raised from Master of Ships to Hand of the King.

jaehaerys.0024.option1.text: The realm is the better for it. Rise, my lord Hand.

jaehaerys.0025.desc.text:
My new master of coin proves his worth at once. Lord Rego - for I have raised the Pentoshi to a lordship, that the Iron Throne need not blush to be served by him - stems the bleeding of the Crown's debts, enough that the great works upon Rhaenys's Hill may resume. But it is not enough to see the Dragonpit finished, and so together we devise a cleverer way to fill the coffers.

We lay a tax upon luxuries and exotic goods - Myrish lace and Volantene silk, Qartheen spices and Lyseni perfumes. It touches no smallfolk, and no honest lord shall feel it; only those who would flaunt their wealth and splendour before the world. And flaunt it they will, Rego assures me, laughing - a vain man will pay any price to be envied. He is right. The coppers become dragons, and the dragons a river of gold.

To this I add a second tax, with a purpose beyond mere coin: henceforth any lord who would raise a new castle, or repair or enlarge an old one, shall pay a heavy toll reckoned by the count of his crenellations. The great lords will think twice before raising their walls higher - and pay the Crown handsomely if they do.

#bold The treasury swells, and the Dragonpit shall be finished after all. #!

jaehaerys.0025.a.text: A shrewd design, my lord. Proclaim it.

jaehaerys.0026.desc.text:
Half a year after I came at last to King's Landing, Alysanne departs Dragonstone to join me, and a moon's turn later we are wed a second time - not in secret as before, but openly, before the Iron Throne and the eyes of the realm. There can be no whispering now that the King and Queen are not truly married.

The rites are performed by a septon new-come to my service: Barth, a smith's son of humble birth and boundless mind, the most learned man I have ever met. I mark him well; I think he shall rise far. The ceremony itself is a modest thing - the treasury is bare, and barely a thousand guests attend, a poor show beside the splendour of Rogar and my mother's Golden Wedding. Yet I would not trade it for a thousand golden weddings.

Alysanne is my sister, my queen, and my truest friend in all the world; there is no one living who knows my heart as she does, nor I hers. That night, as man and wife before gods and men at last, we lie together.

#bold Whatever storms may come, we shall face them as one. #!

jaehaerys.0026.a.text: My queen. My sister. My soulmate.

jaehaerys.0027.desc.text:
Lord Daemon Velaryon has served the crown long and faithfully, but the Lord of the Tides grows old, and the tides call him home. The realm expects me to reach for a great lord to take up the chain - a Tully, a Tyrell, an Arryn, some proud name with proud banners.

The realm will be disappointed. There is one man at this court who has read every book in the Red Keep's library and written better ones; who argued the Doctrine with septons and the harbor accounts with Rego Draz, and bested both; who fears neither gods, nor lords, nor telling his king that his king is wrong. He is the son of a blacksmith. He wears a septon's robes. And he has the finest mind I have ever met.

The great lords may gnash their teeth. Wisdom does not wear a house's colors.

#bold Septon Barth shall be my Hand. The realm will laugh - and then, for forty years, it will marvel. #!

jaehaerys.0027.desc.daemon_dead.text:
The Handship stands empty, and the realm expects me to reach for a great lord to fill it - a Tully, a Tyrell, an Arryn, some proud name with proud banners.

The realm will be disappointed. There is one man at this court who has read every book in the Red Keep's library and written better ones; who argued the Doctrine with septons and the harbor accounts with Rego Draz, and bested both; who fears neither gods, nor lords, nor telling his king that his king is wrong. He is the son of a blacksmith. He wears a septon's robes. And he has the finest mind I have ever met.

The great lords may gnash their teeth. Wisdom does not wear a house's colors.

#bold Septon Barth shall be my Hand. The realm will laugh - and then, for forty years, it will marvel. #!

jaehaerys.0027.option1.text: The chain goes to the finest mind in the realm.

jaehaerys.0027.hand_tt.text: Lord Daemon Velaryon steps down with honor, and #bold Septon Barth#! - the blacksmith's son who kept the Red Keep's library - becomes Hand of the King.

jaehaerys.0028.desc.text:
Baelon has begun to chase every shadow shaped like wings. He is still small, but he is dragon's blood, and fear taught too late can curdle into something worse.

The Dragonpit stands ready. Balerion sleeps within its dark. I should show my son what our house has kept, and what it must never take lightly.

#bold A prince of the blood must meet what makes his House great. #!

jaehaerys.0029.desc.text:
I had meant only to let Baelon look.

Balerion lies before us like a hill of black iron, smoke leaking between teeth longer than my son's arm. Before I can catch him, Baelon darts forward laughing and strikes the Black Dread upon the snout.

For one heartbeat, the world holds still. Then Balerion opens a molten eye, and Baelon laughs harder.

A white cloak lets out the breath the rest of us had forgotten to take. "That boy is brave," he says, "or mad."

#bold By nightfall the whole Red Keep has chosen the kinder word. #!

jaehaerys.0029.a.text: Seven save us from fearless sons.

sotd_soulmate_reason.text: [Select_CString(Or(CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer, TARGET_CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer), 'You have', 'They have')] belonged to one another since [Select_CString(Or(CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer, TARGET_CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer), 'you were', 'they were')] two silver-haired children trading secrets in the dark of the [GetTitleByKey('b_the_red_keep').GetNameNoTier]. Wed once in a stolen midnight flight to [GetTitleByKey('c_dragonstone').GetNameNoTier], and once more before all the realm, [CHARACTER.GetShortUIName] and [TARGET_CHARACTER.GetShortUIName] are far more than husband and wife - [Select_CString(Or(CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer, TARGET_CHARACTER.IsLocalPlayer), 'you are', 'they are')] the dearest of friends and two halves of a single beating heart. Where one dreams, the other dreams beside them; and not the gods, nor the Seven, nor all the wide world shall ever put them asunder.

sotd_lifeline.0002.desc.text:
I receive word from Storm's End that stills the court: the Queen Dowager, my mother Alyssa, is with child again at six-and-forty. [storm_lord.GetTitledFirstName] boasts of the child, while the maesters write far more carefully. Her last confinement nearly killed her, and she has never been strong since.

My mother writes that she is content and that the gods will do as they will. That is what frightens me most.

#bold When her time comes, I will ride for Storm's End.#!

sotd_lifeline.0002.desc.no_holder.text:
I receive word from Storm's End that stills the court: the Queen Dowager, my mother Alyssa, is with child again at six-and-forty. The castle rejoices, while the maesters write far more carefully. Her last confinement nearly killed her, and she has never been strong since.

My mother writes that she is content and that the gods will do as they will. That is what frightens me most.

#bold When her time comes, I will ride for Storm's End.#!

sotd_lifeline.0002.a.text: When her time comes, we ride for Storm's End.

sotd_lifeline.0003.desc.text:
I came too late for anything but grief. When Alysanne and I arrived at Storm's End, we found [storm_lord.GetTitledFirstName] drunk in the hall and unable to face my mother's bedchamber. The maester told us plainly that she was dying, though the child might be saved if he cut the babe from her.

I forced the lord into the room and made him speak the choice that was his. Alysanne never left Mother's side. Some swear my mother woke and consented; others swear she never woke at all. I know only that she died giving birth to a daughter, Jocelyn.

#bold The storm has taken the gentlest soul it ever held.#!

sotd_lifeline.0003.desc.no_alysanne.text:
I came too late for anything but grief. At Storm's End I found [storm_lord.GetTitledFirstName] drunk in the hall and unable to face my mother's bedchamber. The maester told me plainly that she was dying, though the child might be saved if he cut the babe from her.

I forced the lord into the room and made him speak the choice that was his. Some swear my mother woke and consented; others swear she never woke at all. I know only that she died giving birth to a daughter, Jocelyn.

#bold The storm has taken the gentlest soul it ever held.#!

I know only that she died giving birth to a daughter, Jocelyn.\n\n#bold The storm has taken the gentlest soul it ever held.#!
