His bearers set him down and ran.

One of them worked a cobblestone loose from the street I paved and brought it down on him again and again until the work was done.

I made Rego a lord because the magisters of Pentos would not have him, low-born and rich as he was. He had no land, no castle, no sworn sword; my own court named him the Lord of Air for it, and he laughed louder at that jest than any man in the hall. He filled my treasury for eleven years and never once lied to me about a figure. He was murdered a quarter mile from my gates for having been born across the narrow sea.

#bold There is a stone somewhere in Flea Bottom with my friend's blood on it, and a hand that lifted it. #!

fab_rego.0001.a.text: Take him up out of the mud. Then find me the hand that held the stone.

fab_rego.0001.a.tt.text: Lord Rego's body is recovered from the street and given the rites of his own gods. The hunt for his killers begins.

fab_rego.0001.b.text: Ring Flea Bottom with steel. No one leaves it until I have names.

fab_rego.0001.b.tt.text: The gold cloaks seal the poorest quarter of King's Landing street by street. The city will give up its names, and hate the king for the asking.

fab_rego.0001.c.text: It was the winter that killed him, not men. Leave it.

fab_rego.0001.c.tt.text: No hunt is called. The murderers of the king's own master of coin walk free, and every lord in the realm will mark what the king's peace is worth.

fab_rego.0010.desc.text:
They have the alley roped off, for whatever that is worth. The palanquin is still lying on its side where it fell, the gilt scraped down to the bare wood by people helping themselves. The stone was found four steps from him, and it is not a small stone.

No one saw anything. That is the answer at every door on that street, and at every door on the three streets behind it. Flea Bottom has lived under the King's Peace for eleven years and has learned precisely how much of itself it may keep back from me.

A dozen men, in a city of forty thousand, in a winter, in the dark. My council tells me the smallfolk will close over this like water over a dropped coin, and that a king is wiser to mourn than to hunt.

#bold My council has forgotten who paid to pave that street. #!

fab_rego.0010.a.text: Then I will walk it myself, and Vermithor will wait above the rooftops.

fab_rego.0010.a.tt.text: The king goes down into Flea Bottom in person, with a dragon's shadow crossing the roofs behind him. Terror will pry the names loose faster than any search. #bold Very likely to find the killers.#!

fab_rego.0010.b.text: Gold cloaks. Every hovel, every cellar, door by door.

fab_rego.0010.b.tt.text: The City Watch searches the quarter house by house. Slower, cruder, and the city will remember the boots on its stairs. #bold An even chance of finding the killers.#!

fab_rego.0010.c.text: A dragon of gold for a name. Flea Bottom has never yet refused coin.

fab_rego.0010.c.tt.text: The crown buys informers in the poorest quarter of the city. Flea Bottom will sell its own. #bold Likely to find the killers.#!

fab_rego.0020.desc.king.text:
It took two days once I walked in myself.

A king in Flea Bottom is a strange animal, and a king in Flea Bottom with a bronze dragon turning slow circles over the rooftops is a thing that loosens tongues no coin could. By the second evening I had eleven names, and by the third night I had eleven men.

I think I wanted monsters. What is kneeling in the yard beneath the Red Keep is a fishmonger, two dyer's apprentices, a man who buried three children this winter, and seven more cut from the same cloth. Thin. Filthy. More frightened of me than Rogar Baratheon ever was in the whole of his life.

The one who lifted the stone will not stop saying that he has a wife. He has said it perhaps forty times. He has not once said that he is sorry, and I do not believe he understands, even now, that he has done a thing a man could be sorry for.

Alysanne asks what good their deaths will do a man already dead. Rego would have asked me the price. But I have held a peace over this city for eleven years, and a peace that will not answer murder is only a word.

#bold Whatever I do in that yard tomorrow, the whole realm will learn it by heart. #!

fab_rego.0020.desc.coin.text:
It cost me less than a good horse.

Eleven names, bought one at a time in the back of a wineshop off the Street of Flour, each one sold by a neighbour who had drunk with these men a week before. The gold cloaks had only to walk to the doors and knock.

I think I wanted monsters. What is kneeling in the yard beneath the Red Keep is a fishmonger, two dyer's apprentices, a man who buried three children this winter, and seven more cut from the same cloth. Thin. Filthy. More frightened of me than Rogar Baratheon ever was in the whole of his life.

The one who lifted the stone will not stop saying that he has a wife. He has said it perhaps forty times. He has not once said that he is sorry, and I do not believe he understands, even now, that he has done a thing a man could be sorry for.

Alysanne asks what good their deaths will do a man already dead. Rego would have asked me the price. But I have held a peace over this city for eleven years, and a peace that will not answer murder is only a word.

#bold Whatever I do in that yard tomorrow, the whole realm will learn it by heart. #!

fab_rego.0020.desc.text:
It took the gold cloaks eleven days and a great many broken doors.

They went through the quarter cellar by cellar, and by the end of it Flea Bottom hated the Watch rather more than it had hated Rego. But they came out with eleven men.

I think I wanted monsters. What is kneeling in the yard beneath the Red Keep is a fishmonger, two dyer's apprentices, a man who buried three children this winter, and seven more cut from the same cloth. Thin. Filthy. More frightened of me than Rogar Baratheon ever was in the whole of his life.

The one who lifted the stone will not stop saying that he has a wife. He has said it perhaps forty times. He has not once said that he is sorry, and I do not believe he understands, even now, that he has done a thing a man could be sorry for.

Alysanne asks what good their deaths will do a man already dead. Rego would have asked me the price. But I have held a peace over this city for eleven years, and a peace that will not answer murder is only a word.

#bold Whatever I do in that yard tomorrow, the whole realm will learn it by heart. #!

fab_rego.0020.a.text: Open them from throat to groin, and hang what is left from my walls.

fab_rego.0020.a.tt.text: The killers are disembowelled and their bodies hung from the walls of the Red Keep, where the city cannot look away from them. King's Landing will be a very quiet city for a very long time.

fab_rego.0020.b.text: Hang them. It is a death, and a death is enough.

fab_rego.0020.b.tt.text: Eleven men hang at the gallows in the ordinary way. The city takes the lesson, though not so deeply as it might have.

fab_rego.0020.c.text: The Wall. Men who cursed the cold can go and live in it.

fab_rego.0020.c.tt.text: The killers take the black. The Night's Watch is given eleven men who will not enjoy the north, and the Faith is given a king who did not spill blood he could have spared.

fab_rego.0020.d.text: The hand that held the stone will hang. The rest go home as hungry as they came.

fab_rego.0020.d.tt.text: One man dies. Ten walk out of the yard alive, and tell every soul in Flea Bottom what the king did. The lords of the realm will call it weakness.

fab_rego.0021.desc.text:
Nothing. Not one name.

Eleven or twelve men beat a lord to death in a public street in the middle of the afternoon, in a quarter where four thousand people live stacked on top of one another, and there is not a witness in all of King's Landing. Doors that were open are shut. Men who were drinking in the Street of Flour that day were, it turns out, all of them at their mothers' bedsides.

The commander of my gold cloaks stands in front of me and tells me that Flea Bottom protects its own, and that this is not defiance so much as a habit older than my house. He is right, and I would very much like to strike him for it.

Rego Draz sailed across the narrow sea because I asked him to. He served eleven years and made this crown solvent for the first time since my grandsire took it. And I cannot give him the one thing a king is supposed to be able to give anyone.

#bold I have paved these streets, walled this city and fed it through a winter, and it will not give me eleven names. #!

fab_rego.0021.a.text: Flea Bottom keeps its own. So be it. Call off the search.

fab_rego.0021.a.tt.text: The hunt ends with nothing. The lords of the realm will note that a man may murder the king's master of coin in the king's own capital and grow old.

fab_rego.0021.b.text: Then all Flea Bottom answers for it. Fines, whippings, and the Watch.

fab_rego.0021.b.tt.text: The whole quarter is punished for what a dozen men did. No justice is done, but no one in King's Landing will mistake the king for a soft man.

fab_rego.0030.desc.text:
Three young men are waiting in my audience chamber, and every one of them has his father's nose.

Gessio is nineteen and has had the ledgers open for four days already; he can tell me to the copper what the crown owes and to whom, without notes. Illyrio is seventeen and cannot make himself look at me. Myrio is fifteen and is weeping, and is trying very hard to do it without moving his face.

All three are baseborn, got on women Rego never married and never pretended to have married, and all three are the only heirs he troubled to acknowledge. Behind them stands the manse on the Street of Silk, the warehouses along the river, four ships, the debts of half the lords of the Reach, and a fortune that my master of laws describes, carefully, as an embarrassment.

None of it is bound to them. A lord with no lands leaves nothing his king may not simply take, and there is not a septon in this city who would trouble to call it theft.

#bold Rego Draz crossed the narrow sea because Pentos would not have him. Today I decide what Westeros gives him back. #!

fab_rego.0030.a.text: Every coin of it goes home to Pentos with them. My own ships will carry it.

fab_rego.0030.a.tt.text: The Draz fortune leaves Westeros whole, in the hands of Rego's sons. They will build houses of their own on it in Pentos - and every free city will hear how the Dragon treats a foreigner who served him faithfully.

fab_rego.0030.b.text: Gessio stays. His father's head for figures did not die in that alley.

fab_rego.0030.b.tt.text: Gessio Draz is taken into the king's court. The rest of his father's wealth sails for Pentos with his brothers.

fab_rego.0030.c.text: He left no lawful heirs. Count every coin of it into my treasury.

fab_rego.0030.c.tt.text: The crown takes everything Rego Draz owned. The gold is real and it is needed - and so is the reputation the crown is spending to get it.

fab_rego.0040.desc.text:
The small council meets with a gap in it that no one will look at directly.

A name has already been put forward, and it is a good name, which is what a Hand is for. Ser Martyn Tyrell of Highgarden: heir to nothing in particular, pleasant, well-liked, married these three years to Florence of House Fossoway. No lord in the Reach could take offence at him, and lords taking offence is a thing I have had a bellyful of this winter.

He is also, and I say this having now spoken with him twice, not a clever man.

Rego could hold four ledgers in his head and lie to me about none of them. Whoever sits in that chair inherits a treasury that has just paid for a plague, a famine and a winter, and inherits it in the middle of all three.

#bold The chair is only a chair. What matters is who does the counting. #!

fab_rego.0040.a.text: Ser Martyn, then. The Reach will be pleased, and the Reach is worth pleasing.

fab_rego.0040.a.tt.text: Ser Martyn Tyrell is named master of coin. He is agreeable, he is safe, and he cannot add.

fab_rego.0040.b.text: Gessio Draz. He has held those ledgers well since his father died.

fab_rego.0040.b.tt.text: Rego's bastard son takes his father's seat at nineteen. He is the ablest man in the room by a wide margin, and every lord in the realm will be told that the Dragon has given the treasury to a foreign whore's son.

fab_rego.0040.c.text: No one. I will count it myself until I find a man who can.

fab_rego.0040.c.tt.text: The king keeps the treasury in his own hands. It will be well kept, and it will cost him every hour he does not have.

fab_rego.0041.desc.text:
It has taken me the better part of a year to work out why the accounts stopped being wrong.

Ser Martyn brings them to me himself every moon's turn, and answers well enough at first, and badly the moment I go past the second page. Last week I went past the second page. He went red, and glanced at the door, and said he would have the figure by evening. He had it by evening. It was correct to the copper.

His lady wife does the counting. She has done all of it since the day he sat down. Florence of House Fossoway, taught her letters and her sums by an uncle who had no sons and no fixed notion of what a daughter is for, has been running the treasury of the Seven Kingdoms for a year out of a solar in the Tower of the Hand, while her husband carries her arithmetic downstairs and puts his name to the bottom of it.

Alysanne has known for at least six moons. Alysanne did not think it worth troubling me with.

#bold The realm's coin is in excellent hands. They are simply not the hands the realm believes. #!

fab_rego.0041.a.text: It works. Leave the ledgers be, and Ser Martyn his dignity.

fab_rego.0041.a.tt.text: Nothing is said aloud. Ser Martyn remains master of coin in name, and grows a great deal better at the office, for reasons the court is content not to examine.

fab_rego.0041.b.text: Then let her have the chair, and the name that goes with it.

fab_rego.0041.b.tt.text: Lady Florence Fossoway is named master of coin openly, the first woman ever to sit that seat. She will be very good at it. The lords of the Seven Kingdoms will be very loud about it.

fab_rego.0041.c.text: A master of coin who cannot count is no master of coin. Both of them, out.

fab_rego.0041.c.tt.text: Ser Martyn is dismissed and his wife with him. House Tyrell and House Fossoway will both remember the humiliation.

fab_flea_bottom_sealed_modifier_desc.text: Gold cloaks stand at every mouth of every alley. The city obeys, and the city remembers.

fab_flea_bottom_cowed_modifier_desc.text: What was done to Lord Rego's killers was done where the whole city could see it. King's Landing has not forgotten, and does not intend to.

fab_kings_mercy_modifier_desc.text: The king was murdered of a friend and answered with bread. The smallfolk of King's Landing will speak of it for a generation.

fab_rego_fortune_seized_modifier_desc.text: The crown took a foreign lord's wealth the week he was buried. Every merchant from Braavos to Volantis heard of it, and the ships put in elsewhere.

fab_rego_plot_armor_modifier_desc.text: The master of coin is a stout man past his best years, and the crown cannot spare him. The maesters of the Red Keep attend him whether he wishes it or not.

fab_florence_counts_modifier_desc.text: Ser Martyn carries the ledgers down from the solar and puts his name to them. His wife wrote every figure in them.

fab_rego_justice_opinion.text: Answered the murder of a king's servant

fab_foreign_coin_opinion.text: Seated a foreign bastard on the small council

fab_lady_of_coin_opinion.text: Seated a woman as master of coin

sotd_rhaena.0001.desc.text:
My sister Rhaena comes to me now that the wedding feasts are done - twice a queen, twice widowed, hounded from refuge to refuge through all of Maegor's reign. Of the three heads of my father's line, hers has borne the heaviest crown of griefs, and she asks now for the only thing she has ever asked of me: a place that is hers, where no one may ever again bid her come or go.

There is only one seat worthy of her: Dragonstone, the ancient citadel of our house, where Aegon dreamed his conquest and the dragons nest in the smoking mountain. She will rule it in her own right, with her own court about her and Dreamfyre in the yards. The realm will call her the Queen in the East, and the realm will not be wrong.

#bold The eldest line takes the eldest seat. It is her due, and long past owed. #!

sotd_rhaena.0001.a.text: Dragonstone is yours, sweet sister. No one shall move you again.

sotd_rhaena.0002.desc.text:
Dreamfyre's wings darken the courtyard of the Red Keep, and my sister storms from the saddle in a fury I have not seen since Maegor lived. Lady Elissa Farman - her dearest friend, mistress of Dragonstone's ships, sister to her own husband - is gone. Fled in the night, west then east, and with her three dragon eggs out of the hatcheries beneath the Dragonmont.

Rhaena begged me keep it quiet, and quiet it must be kept: if the realm learns that dragon eggs can be plucked from Dragonstone like apples from an orchard, every thief and every foreign prince will dream the same dream. But quiet is not the same as idle. Elissa sold her jewels in Pentos, and men who describe her all mention the same thing: she means to build a ship, the like of which no one has seen, and sail beyond the maps.

The eggs will not sail with her. Eggs are heavy, and gold is heavier still. She will sell them - and there is one buyer rich enough, close enough, and hungry enough.

#bold Follow the gold. All gold flows to Braavos. #!

sotd_rhaena.0002.a.text: Quiet ships and quiet coin. Find where she has taken them.

sotd_rhaena.0003.desc.text:
The answer comes back across the narrow sea wrapped in silk and insolence. The Sealord of Braavos regrets that he knows nothing of any stolen eggs; and even if he possessed such curiosities, he observes, unhatched dragon eggs are nothing more than #italic 'pretty stones'#!. In the same breath - the same letter, all but the same sentence - the Iron Bank announces that, as a token of its high regard for the Iron Throne, it is prepared to forgive the greater part of the crown's debts.

So that is the price of three dragons: my debts, and my silence. Rego Draz calls it the finest bargain the crown will ever be offered. Perhaps he is right. But let the Sealord hear this much, and hear it plainly: eggs are stone until they are not.

#bold If ever those eggs hatch, the Sealord's Palace will be the first thing to burn. #!

sotd_rhaena.0003.debt_tt.text: The Iron Bank forgives the greater part of the crown's debts - #bold 1000 gold#! - and the matter is buried. The three eggs remain in the Sealord's vaults... unhatched. For now.

sotd_rhaena.0003.a.text: Take the bargain. But they have been warned.

sotd_rhaena.0003.b.text: #bold (An Alternate History)#! No bank buys the blood of the dragon. WAR.

sotd_rhaena.0004.desc.text:
The Titan of Braavos watched my fleets pass beneath its legs, and the lagoon burned. The Sealord who called the eggs of Dragonstone 'pretty stones' has learned what stone becomes in dragonfire; his successor was pleased to discover the three eggs in the palace vaults after all, and more pleased still to hand them over.

Three eggs - one black as midnight, one green as summer, one cream and gold - ride home to Westeros in a chest of iron, under guard no thief alive could pass. Whatever sleeps within them will sleep beneath the Dragonmont, where it belongs, or hatch in a Targaryen cradle.

#bold What was taken from the dragon has been taken back. Every vault across the narrow sea will take note. #!

sotd_rhaena.0004.a.text: What was stolen from dragons, dragons reclaim.

sotd_rhaena.0005.desc.text:
Braavos does not kneel. The lagoon city has no fields to burn and no castles to break - only water, stone, mist and money, and all four defeated me. My fleets came home fewer than they sailed, the Iron Bank has called in every debt with interest, and the Sealord keeps his 'pretty stones' with a courtesy more wounding than any taunt.

The realm whispers that the Old King reached across the sea and came back with an empty hand. The whispers are true. The eggs sleep in Braavos still, and I must live with the knowing.

#bold Some wars are lost in fog and ledgers. But eggs are stone until they are not - and Braavos should still remember it. #!

sotd_rhaena.0005.a.text: The sea has beaten better men. But the warning stands.

sotd_rhaena.0010.desc.text:
Grim word from my sister's island seat, and it comes sealed thrice over. Death has crept through Dragonstone like a fog: old Maester Culiper, dead at his letters. Then, one after another, the ladies of Rhaena's own court - Cassella Staunton, Septa Maryam, Alayne Royce, and last Samantha Stokeworth, who fought it for a day and a night, screaming. Rhaena has barred her own gates, and begs to know what curse has come to her hall.

It is no curse. When I read the letter to the council, Lord Rego Draz went very still, and then named it: the tears of Lys, the poisoner's poison, rare and beyond price - a clear sweet water that eats the bowels away and leaves no mark. Someone within those walls, someone who sups at my sister's own table, is murdering her court lady by lady.

#bold A raven to Dragonstone, flying faster than fear: it is poison. Look beside you. #!

sotd_rhaena.0010.a.text: Send the raven. And gods help whoever it names.

sotd_rhaena.0011.desc.text:
The tale comes back in pieces, and every piece is worse. When my raven reached Dragonstone and Rhaena read the words #italic 'tears of Lys'#!, she did not have to wonder. She summoned her husband to the Chamber of the Painted Table and set the letter before him - and Androw Farman, that soft smiling nothing of a man, did not even deny it. He #bold boasted#!. His sister gone, his wife's love never his, mocked by ladies who thought him furniture - so he fed them poison and watched them die, and called it the only power he was ever given.

Rhaena told him he was free to go: by the window or the door, as he pleased. He chose the window of the Painted Table chamber, where Aegon once plotted the conquest of a continent, and leapt.

What remained of him, my sister had hacked to pieces and fed to Dreamfyre and the dragons of the yards. She has that of Maegor in her too, whatever the septons pretend.

#bold So die poisoners. But five good souls are gone, and Dragonstone will never feel clean to her again. #!

sotd_rhaena.0011.a.text: So die poisoners. Gods rest the ladies of Dragonstone.

sotd_rhaena.0020.t.text: The Black Dread Has a Rider

sotd_rhaena.0020.desc.text:
A raven from Dragonstone, and the words freeze the blood in my veins: Aerea is gone - and she has taken #bold BALERION#!.

My brother's daughter, sent from my court back to a mother she barely knew, lonely and furious on that grim rock, walked into the smoking yards at dawn and claimed the Black Dread himself. Not some hatchling, not one of the yard's young dragons - the beast that was old when Valyria burned, the dragon of Aegon and of Maegor, the largest living thing in the known world. The guards say she laughed as he took wing.

They flew east over the sea, and no eye has seen them since. A girl of thirteen, on a monster that answers to no chain ever forged, gone beyond my reach and perhaps beyond anyone's.

#bold Find her. Every ship, every raven, every coin. Find her. #!

sotd_rhaena.0020.a.text: Every ship, every raven, every coin. Find her.

sotd_rhaena.0021.desc.text:
Half a year, and nothing. My envoys have knocked at the doors of Pentos, Tyrosh, Myr and Volantis; the Iron Bank itself - eager to be helpful, since the matter of the eggs - has set its thousand eyes looking. A black dragon was seen over the Disputed Lands, they say. A black dragon was seen off Lys. A black dragon was seen where no black dragon was, by men who wanted my gold.

Rhaena flies the coasts on Dreamfyre until her hands crack from the wind. Alysanne lights candles. I sit with Barth late into the nights, and he says the thing neither of us wants said: no one has seen them because Balerion has not gone to the lands of men. There is one place in this world that dragon knows better than any living creature, one place he alone remembers - and it is the place from which nothing returns.

#bold Valyria. Gods be good, he has taken her home to Valyria. #!

sotd_rhaena.0021.a.text: Keep searching. She is blood of the dragon. She lives.

sotd_rhaena.0022.desc.text:
On the thirteenth day of the fourth moon, the guards on the walls of the Red Keep began to shout - and the shadow of vast black wings fell over King's Landing for the first time since Maegor died. Balerion came home.

But gods, what came home with him. Down the Black Dread's left side runs a wound near nine feet long, half-healed and hideous, and his flight is a broken, laboring thing. And clinging to his back, lashed there by rags that were once clothes - Aerea. She is a skeleton wrapped in skin, her hair a mat, her eyes brimming red. She is burning. Not with fever as maesters know it: the heat pours off her small body till the air above her shimmers, and when Benifer touched her brow he snatched his hand back as from a kettle. And beneath her skin - I will not write what I saw moving beneath her skin.

Grand Maester Benifer has taken her to his chambers. I have sent for Septon Barth. No one else is to be admitted.

#bold Whatever she found in the ruins of Valyria, it has come back inside her. #!

sotd_rhaena.0022.a.text: Benifer and Barth, no one else. And pray.

sotd_rhaena.0023.desc.text:
Princess Aerea Targaryen died an hour before dawn. Only two men witnessed her last hours, and one of them will never speak of it and the other has written an account and sealed it, to be read - he says - by no king now living.

Barth told me only this much, and his hands shook as he told it: they did all that men could do, and at the end they did the only mercy left, and it was not enough, and the things that killed her were not of this world nor meant for it. She was thirteen years old. She wanted her mother's love, and her father's throne, and a dragon of her own - and the dragon she chose was the one beast alive that remembered the road home to hell.

Rhaena came too late to hear her daughter speak. She took the ashes up on Dreamfyre, alone, higher than any man could see, and scattered them upon the winds. When she landed she had no more tears. I do not believe she will ever have any again.

#bold The account stays sealed. Some knowledge is a wound in the world. #!

sotd_rhaena.0023.a.text: Seal the account. Some things must never be read.

sotd_rhaena.0024.desc.text:
Never again. That is the whole of the law I take from this sorrow: never again shall a child of my house walk unwatched into a dragon's yard and fly away to her death.

Balerion, too broken and too old for the wild, I have returned to the smoking yards of Dragonstone, where the Dragonmont shall house him under guard. And about him I have raised a new order: the #bold Dragonkeepers#!, seven-and-seventy men in suits of black scale, sworn to guard the dragons of House Targaryen day and night - and to guard the world from them, and them from the follies of children.

My sister Rhaena flew from Dragonstone the day after the ashes were scattered. She will not keep the island, she says: #italic 'It is yours again, brother. I want no seat that Androw poisoned and no yard that gave my daughter to Valyria. Dragonstone holds nothing for me now but ghosts.'#! I have taken it back into the crown, and she wanders now, from castle to castle, a queen of griefs.

#bold Out of fire, order. Never again. #!

sotd_rhaena.0024.desc.no_rhaena.text:
Never again. That is the whole of the law I take from this sorrow: never again shall a child of my house walk unwatched into a dragon's yard and fly away to her death.

Balerion, too broken and too old for the wild, I have returned to the smoking yards of Dragonstone, where the Dragonmont shall house him under guard. And about him I have raised a new order: the #bold Dragonkeepers#!, seven-and-seventy men in suits of black scale, sworn to guard the dragons of House Targaryen day and night - and to guard the world from them, and them from the follies of children.

#bold Out of fire, order. Never again. #!

sotd_rhaena.0024.a.text: Out of fire, order. Never again.

sotd_rhaena.0025.desc.text:
One of the black-dragon rumours seemed worth the chasing. Word came out of the Velvet Hills north of Pentos: a great winged shadow roosting in the high country, and a guide who swore he could lead armed men to its lair. I sent Ser Willam the Wasp with a dozen good swords to learn the truth of it.

There was no dragon. There never had been. Brigands had spread the tale to draw the curious into the hills, and the guide led Ser Willam and his men straight into an ambush. They were cut down to the last, in a gully with no name, for the price of my gold and a lie.

They tell me the Wasp gave a good account of himself - that he was the last to fall, and that the ground about him was thick with the men he took along. One of Lord Rego's agents bought back his head from the killers, so that I might be certain. I am certain. I have lost a white cloak to a fool's errand, and it was I who sent him on it.

#bold Ser Willam the Wasp. A brave knight, dead for a rumour. The realm is poorer for it. #!

sotd_rhaena.0025.a.text: Bury what they returned to us with honour.

sotd_rhaena.0026.t.text: A White Cloak for the Wasp

sotd_rhaena.0026.desc.text:
A year has passed since Ser Willam died in that nameless gully, and his place among the Seven has stood empty long enough. A king is judged by the swords he keeps closest, and I have taken my time choosing.

The knight who kneels before the Iron Throne this morning is Ser Lucamore Strong - big, bluff, and tireless, a lance that has unhorsed better-born men in tourney after tourney, and a blade that never seems to weary. The commons have taken to calling him a lusty sort, and there are whispers about the women of the Kingswood, but no man questions his courage or his skill at arms. Ser Gyles vouches for him, and that is enough for me.

I lay the white cloak across his shoulders myself, where the Wasp's once hung.

#bold Rise, Ser Lucamore of the Kingsguard. Serve better than I served the man whose cloak you wear. #!

sotd_rhaena.0026.a.text: Rise, Ser Lucamore. The white is yours.

sotd_rhaena_barren_modifier_desc.text: Twice widowed and wedded now to a man she cannot love, Rhaena Targaryen will bear no more children.

fab_shivers.0001.desc.text:
The ravens come from the east, and each one carries the same word: cold.

It began on the islands - Dragonstone, Driftmark, the little rocks off the mouth of the Blackwater - and it does not care that it is not yet winter. A man complains of a chill he cannot shake. By the next morning his skin is frost to the touch, his lips gone blue, and he shakes so hard the bed rattles beneath him. By the morning after that, more often than not, he is dead. The maesters have already given it a name: the Shivers.

Grand Maester Benifer tells me it moves faster than any pestilence in the histories, and that it does not spare the strong. It is climbing the Blackwater toward my city even as I read of it. I have a court, a council, a wife, and children under this roof.

#bold The gods send the cold. Let us see how many of my people it means to take. #!

fab_shivers.0001.a.text: Close the gates. Ready the maesters. Pray.

fab_shivers.0009.desc.text:
As suddenly as it came, it is gone.

The spring of the year sixty comes late and grudging, but it comes, and with the first true warmth the Shivers loses its grip. Those still shaking in their sickbeds wake to find the fever broken and the cold fled from their bones. No more than one in five of those it touched ever rose again - but those it spared, it spared for good.

When I ask for the tally I almost wish I had not. Half my small council, gone. A third of the maesters of the Citadel. Great lords in their halls and washerwomen in the gutters, taken alike. And the High Septon dead in the Starry Sept, which the Faith will spend a long winter making sense of.

#bold The realm will mourn a long while. But the realm endures. #!

fab_shivers.0009.a.text: Bury the dead. Count the living. Begin again.

fab_shivers.0100.desc.text:
It has come into my own house.

At supper my daughter Daenerys - six years old, quick and bright and never still - complained that she was cold, though the fires roared and the hall was warm. Alysanne wrapped her in furs and sent her early to bed. By the time the maester was fetched she was shaking under three blankets, her small teeth chattering, her lips already darkening.

The Doctrine I built with my own hands says this cannot be. Targaryens do not sicken with the ills of common men; it is written, it is proclaimed, it is the very thing that makes my marriage lawful in the eyes of the realm. And my daughter lies in her bed and shakes, and the words turn to ash in my mouth.

#bold They say a day and a half. From the first cold word to the last. #!

fab_shivers.0100.a.text: No. Not her. Fetch me the maesters - all of them.

fab_shivers.0101.desc.text:
The maesters have done all they know, and it is not enough. Benifer's successor will not meet my eyes. Alysanne has not left the bedside in a day and a night, and Daenerys grows colder in her arms.

There is one thing left. It is not in any maester's book. Since Rhaena laid an egg in the cradles of my sister and me when we were babes, it has been the way of my House to give a dragon's egg to our children - and the old tales, the ones the maesters sniff at, say that a dragon's egg laid warm beside dragon's blood can wake a fire that even death fears.

I could send for an egg from the Dragonstone hatcheries and lay it in her bed. It is superstition. It is a father with nothing left. It is the barest, coldest chance.

#bold Or I could kneel, and pray, and let the Seven do as they will. #!

fab_shivers.0101.a.text: Bring me an egg. Lay it beside her, and stoke the fire high.

fab_shivers.0101.egg_tt.text: The egg will almost certainly lie cold and dead. But if the blood of the dragon runs true in her - it might, just might, quicken. A slim hope against a certain grief.

fab_shivers.0101.b.text: There is no magic in an egg. I will pray, as any father would.

fab_shivers.0102.desc.text:
She died before the dawn.

Just as the maesters foretold - a day and a half from her first small complaint of cold to the last shudder that passed through her and did not come again. Alysanne held her through all of it, and holds her still, and will not let them take her.

I am the King of the Seven Kingdoms. I made a doctrine that told all the world my blood was not as other blood, that the dragon did not sicken and die as common men do. I believed it. I needed to believe it. And I buried my daughter in the cold ground of the year sixty, and every septon and every lord who ever doubted me now has his proof, laid in a child's grave.

#bold Daenerys of House Targaryen. Six years old. The dragon can die after all. #!

fab_shivers.0102.a.text: Leave us. Leave us both with her.

fab_shivers.0103.hatch_tt.text: Daenerys survives the Shivers. A dragon has hatched at her side, and is bonded to her.

fab_shivers.0103.desc.text:
In the blackest hour of the night, the egg cracked.

I was there, and Alysanne was there, and we both heard it - a sound like green wood splitting in a hot fire, from the egg nestled in the furs against our daughter's side. By the time the candle was lit the shell had fallen open, and a wet and hissing wyrmling was pressing itself against Daenerys's cold skin, and where it touched her the shaking eased.

By morning her fever had broken. By midday she was sitting up, weak as a kitten and twice as fierce, demanding to know the name of the little dragon that would not leave her side. The maesters have no explanation and the septons are already calling it a miracle of the Seven, and I will let them, for it serves. But I know what I saw. The oldest magic of my House woke in the dark and reached into the cold and pulled my daughter back.

#bold The Doctrine is true. My blood is not as other blood. And I have the dragon in her cradle to prove it. #!

fab_shivers.0103.a.text: She may name him. She has earned the right.

fab_shivers.0105.desc.text:
The bedchamber has emptied, save for Alysanne and me.

For a long while she made no sound at all. She only stared at the small shape beneath the linen, one hand pressed to her mouth as if she could hold her grief inside by force. Then the strength went from her knees, and I caught her before she struck the floor.

After her daughter's death, Alysanne collapsed in my arms, shaking so hard that some worried that she had the Shivers too. I held her as tightly as I dared, feeling every tremor pass through her body and into mine. No crown, no doctrine, no prayer, no dragon could answer her. There was only the cold room, our dead child, and the terrible weight of being left alive.

#bold I am her husband before I am her king. Tonight, that is all I can be. #!

fab_shivers.0105.a.text: Hold her until the shaking passes.

fab_shivers.0106.desc.text:
The first true warmth returns to the room with Daenerys's breath.

Alysanne kneels beside the bed, weeping again, but now the tears are bright and disbelieving. Our daughter sleeps, flushed with life instead of fever, while the newborn dragon curls close against her side like a coal banked beneath ash. I take Alysanne's hand, and together we give thanks to the Seven for the mercy they have shown our house.

Yet the gods did not work through herbs, nor prayers alone, nor any maester's wisdom. They answered through fire. Through the egg. Through the old blood that Valyria carried out of doom and into our veins.

#bold Our blood is the blood of the dragon, closer to gods than men. This night has proved it. #!

fab_shivers.0106.desc.dragon.text:
The first true warmth returns to the room with Daenerys's breath.

Alysanne kneels beside the bed, weeping again, but now the tears are bright and disbelieving. Our daughter sleeps, flushed with life instead of fever, while [daenerys_dragon.GetName] keeps watch beside her, smoke rising softly from its nostrils. I take Alysanne's hand, and together we give thanks to the Seven for the mercy they have shown our house.

Yet the gods did not work through herbs, nor prayers alone, nor any maester's wisdom. They answered through the living bond between our daughter and her dragon. The fire had chosen Daenerys before the cold ever came for her.

#bold Our blood is the blood of the dragon, closer to gods than men. This night has proved it. #!

fab_shivers.0106.a.text: The gods have shown the truth of our blood.

fab_shivers.0108.desc.text:
The maesters have spent their learning, and Daenerys grows colder beneath their hands. Yet there is one creature in all the Red Keep that will not leave her door.

[daenerys_dragon.GetName] has felt her pain through the bond between them. The hatchling claws at the stones beyond the sickroom, hissing smoke at every man who bars the way. When Daenerys shudders, the little dragon answers. When her breathing falters, its cries shake the hinges.

The Grand Maester warns that no man can say what a frightened dragon might do in a child's chamber. Alysanne answers that it is no man Daenerys calls for. This beast is hers, blood bound to blood, and perhaps the fire already joined to her is stronger than the cold.

#bold The gods have set a dragon at my daughter's door. Shall I dare keep it from her? #!

fab_shivers.0108.a.text: Bring [daenerys_dragon.GetName] to her. Dragonfire will answer the cold.

fab_shivers.0108.dragon_tt.text: Daenerys's own bonded dragon will be brought to her sickbed. There is but a slender hope that the warmth of their bond will draw her back.

fab_shivers.0108.b.text: Keep the beast without. We shall trust in the mercy of the Seven.

fab_shivers.0110.desc.text:
The Shivers spared neither smallfolk nor sworn sword. Two of my Kingsguard lie in the crypts beneath the Red Keep, their white cloaks folded and still, and the Seven who guard my life are but five.

A king cannot go long so ill-defended, and the whole realm has watched to see whom I would honour. Two knights kneel before the Iron Throne this morning. Ser Ryam Redwyne of the Arbor is barely a man grown, yet already there is no finer lance in the Reach; the old knights say he will be the best of us before he is done. Beside him kneels Ser Robin Shaw, a quieter blade, steady as stone, the sort who never tires and never boasts.

Grand Maester and Lord Commander both approve. The white cloaks are brought forth, and I speak the words that bind these two to my service until death.

#bold Rise, sers, and take your place among the Kingsguard. The realm has bled enough; let it see the white cloaks whole again. #!

fab_shivers.0120.desc.text:
A moon's turn has passed since fire woke in Daenerys's bed, yet the little dragon will not leave her. It rides her shoulder through the halls, sleeps curled against her breast, and bares needle teeth at any maester who reaches for her overboldly. The court calls it a wonder. The septons call it an omen.

Alysanne calls it the judgement of the gods.

'They reached into the cold and gave our daughter back to us,' she says when we are alone. 'They sent dragonfire to preserve her, Jaehaerys. Daenerys is the eldest of our living children. She came before Aemon, and girl or no, you must name her your heir before all the realm.'

There is no wrath in her voice, only that hard certainty which has made lords bow and septons hold their tongues. I have called Aemon my heir since first I held him in my arms. Alysanne has never suffered the word gladly. Now it seems the gods have lent her cause a voice of flame.

#bold A king should not settle the succession by portents. Yet only a fool turns his face from a sign sent in fire and blood. #!

fab_shivers.0120.a.text: I am king of Westeros, and in Westeros a son comes before a daughter.

fab_shivers.0120.b.text: By that reckoning, Rhaena has the better right to my crown.

fab_shivers.0120.c.text: What of Aemon? I named him heir from the day of his birth.

fab_shivers.0121.desc.text:
'The usages of the Andals are not the Conqueror's law,' Alysanne answers. 'Aegon never commanded that every daughter must give way to every son. No such words were set down by his hand, nor spoken from the Iron Throne. The throne is not yet threescore years old, Jaehaerys. Do not make an ancient law of what was never more than an unasked question.'

I remind her that the lords of Westeros gave their swords and seats to sons for thousands of years before our dragons came. She does not yield.

'Our father followed Aegon because he was the elder. Aenys was a son, aye, but Maegor was a son as well. What set one before the other was birth. Aenys came first. If the Conqueror meant the crown to pass by some other rule, he had seven-and-thirty years to proclaim it.'

It is the sort of answer Barth might give, close-woven and keen enough to draw blood. Yet the lords who bent the knee to Aegon did not cast aside all their old ways when they laid down their swords. A king may speak a new law before sunset. To root out a custom held since the Age of Heroes may take a lifetime - or a war.

#bold The Iron Throne is young. The kingdoms beneath it are old. #!

fab_shivers.0121.a.text: Aegon left no such command. That much is true.

fab_shivers.0122.desc.text:
The words strike home; I see it before she stills her face. Rhaena is our sister, and elder than us both. If the firstborn must always stand before those born after, I am no rightful king. Rhaena is the queen, and the crown upon my head is hers.

'Perhaps hers was the better claim,' Alysanne says at last. 'Yet there was no peaceful passing of the crown for Rhaena to be denied. Maegor stole our father's throne, slew her husband Aegon beneath the Gods Eye, took Rhaena to wife by force, and kept her daughters as hostages to her obedience. He named Aerea his heir when it pleased him and would have cast her aside the instant a son was born to him. When the usurper died, Rhaena came with us to King's Landing. She raised no banner against you. She gave you her strength.'

Hard need does not make my crown weigh any less, I tell her.

'No. But a choice made with Maegor's blood still wet upon the throne is no holy writ. The realm had been torn open, and it cried out for a king all men would follow. Must our daughter be robbed of her place because our sister would not begin another war for hers?'

For a long while neither of us speaks. The crown stands between us: taken from an uncle's corpse, placed upon my brow with the leave of an elder sister.

#bold Some customs are born in wisdom. Others are born in fear. #!

fab_shivers.0122.a.text: Maegor left naught untouched by blood. Not even the succession.

fab_shivers.0123.desc.text:
Aemon is but five. He is solemn where Daenerys is quick, cautious where she is bold, and already follows me through the yard with a wooden sword dragging in the dust. Before court and council I have named him my heir. To unsay those words now would taste of oathbreaking.

Alysanne's face softens. 'I would take nothing from our son. I ask only that you cease taking from our daughter.'

'There is one crown.'

'Yet you and I bear its weight together.' She reaches across the table for my hand. 'Betroth them, if that will quiet your doubts. Daenerys shall bring the elder right, and Aemon the favour of those lords who will have a man. They will rule side by side as we have done. A strong king need not make his queen a shadow.'

It is the answer I have given her before: Aemon as king, Daenerys as his queen, their claims bound as tightly as their blood. No lord could set one against the other without setting brother against sister, husband against wife. Yet to share a husband's crown is not the same as wearing one's own, and Alysanne knows it.

#bold A marriage may join two claims. It cannot tell us which stands above the other. #!

fab_shivers.0123.a.text: As we have borne the crown together, so might they.

fab_shivers.0124.desc.text:
The candles gutter as our quarrel goes round the painted table. Alysanne does not press me to speak in haste, but neither will she suffer me to answer with silence. Beyond the door, Daenerys laughs as her hatchling snaps at shadows on the wall. Aemon's voice soon joins hers. They are children still, heedless of crowns. Their mother and father must choose what singers and maesters will one day name their birthright.

Aegon left no command. Aenys came before Maegor, but no elder sister stood before him. Maegor so befouled the succession that my own crown may serve any tale a man cares to tell. The lords cling to the ways of their fathers; the gods have sent a sign in living flame; and my queen sits across from me, awaiting the answer of her king and husband.

#bold Before these candles die, House Targaryen must know whose name comes after mine. #!

fab_shivers.0124.custom.text: Aegon may have been silent, but the old laws of the kingdoms are not.

fab_shivers.0124.rhaena.text: Then answer me plainly: why am I king instead of Rhaena?

fab_shivers.0124.aemon.text: Enough of claims and customs. Aemon is our son, and I have named him heir.

fab_shivers.0124.a.text: I will honour the laws of the lands I rule. Aemon shall remain my heir.

fab_shivers.0124.a.tt.text: Prince Aemon is confirmed as heir to the Iron Throne. Queen Alysanne will not soon forget that the King denied her plea.

fab_shivers.0124.b.text: Daenerys shall wed Aemon. They will rule together, as we have.

fab_shivers.0124.b.tt.text: Princess Daenerys and Prince Aemon are betrothed. Aemon remains heir to the Iron Throne.

fab_shivers.0124.c.text: The gods answered in dragonfire. Daenerys shall be my heir.

fab_shivers.0124.c.tt.text: Princess Daenerys is named heir to the Iron Throne, though no marriage is promised for her. Every direct vassal of Andal or First Man heritage loses #N 50#! Opinion of King Jaehaerys for 20 years.

fab_shivers.0130.desc.text:
They carry [daenerys_dragon.GetName] into the chamber beneath a cloak of heavy chains, though the hatchling has eyes only for Daenerys. The instant it sees her, it wrenches free, scrambles across the coverlets, and presses itself against her breast.

Smoke curls from between its teeth. Heat gathers beneath its scales until the furs steam and the maesters draw back in fear. Daenerys ceases to shake. Her little hand closes about one warm horn, and [daenerys_dragon.GetName] folds its wings around her as though it would shield her from winter itself.

At dawn her lips are red once more. Before midday she wakes and whispers her dragon's name. No egg was needed, for the fire had chosen her long before the cold came.

#bold The bond between dragon and rider has reached where all the wisdom of men could not. #!

fab_shivers.0130.a.text: They were bound before this night. Now even death knows it.

fab_shivers.0130.saved_tt.text: Daenerys survives the Shivers. [daenerys_dragon.GetName], her existing bonded dragon, remains at her side.

fab_shivers_sickbed_modifier_desc.text: Wrapped in furs and watched over day and night, the princess clings to life - the cold cannot take her while her fate is still being decided.

fab_shivers.daenerys_fate_guaranteed_sur.text: The selected #bold Children of Jaehaerys#! game rule guarantees that Daenerys will survive the Shivers.

fab_shivers.daenerys_fate_guaranteed_dea.text: The selected #bold Children of Jaehaerys#! game rule guarantees that Daenerys will die during the Shivers.

fab_female_heir_outrage_opinion.text: Set aside the ancient laws of inheritance

fab_vulture.0002.t.text: A King in the Red Mountains

fab_vulture.0002.desc.text:
The realm has scarcely finished burying its dead, and now this.

Ravens from the stormlands, from the marches, from Blackhaven and Stonehelm and half the holdfasts between: a brigand has crowned himself in the high passes of the Red Mountains. His men paint a vulture on their shields and call him king — the Vulture King, no more name than that. No maester can tell me his house, his birth, or so much as the color of his eyes. He is Dornish, they say, mountain-born, and he has made himself lord of every goat track and hidden spring from Wyl to Kingsgrave.

Broken men flock to him by the hundred — and lately by the thousand. They come down out of the mountains at dusk, burn a village, empty a sept, and are gone into the rocks before any lord can horse his knights.

The Shivers took my brother and sisters, my friends, near a fifth of my realm. I had hoped the gods were done testing us for a year or two. It seems they are not.

fab_vulture.0002.a.text: Kings are made of more than a painted shield.

fab_vulture.0003.desc.text:
There is worse. The raiders strike too surely — every weak garrison found, every beacon-line avoided, every marcher lord's muster anticipated. Survivors from a burned holdfast on Cape Wrath swear they heard a knight among the raiders speaking with a stormlander's tongue, calling the passes by their names.

Now I know why. Ser Borys Baratheon rides with the Vulture King.

Lord Rogar's own brother. Heir to Storm's End for a dozen years, until Boremund came squalling into the world and took the place he had grown to think his own. Borys took ship for Myr soon after, then Volantis, trailing his bitterness across the Narrow Sea like a torn cloak — and now he has carried it home and laid it at the feet of a brigand who makes war on his own house.

A Baratheon, guiding vultures to the carrion of the stormlands. My uncle Orys carried that house's banner at the Last Storm. It is a vile thing, what envy makes of men.

fab_vulture.0003.a.text: Treason wears no man well. On a Baratheon it is obscene.

fab_vulture.0004.desc.text:
With a Baratheon to guide him, the vulture grows bold.

It is no longer a village here and a sept there. Holdfasts burn now — holdfasts that thought themselves safe, whose lords learn too late that the man choosing the vulture's targets once hawked and hunted across their very lands. The raiders come through passes no map shows, strike where the levies are thinnest, and vanish with their plunder before the smoke can summon help. The marcher lords ride out and find nothing but ashes and arrows; the smallfolk have begun to whisper that the Vulture King cannot be caught, that the mountains themselves hide him.

The Dornish princess in Sunspear disavows him, for what such words are worth — he is no more hers than mine, a king of carrion and nothing else. But he flies his banner in my realm's despite, and the marches bleed.

This cannot stand through winter.

fab_vulture.0004.a.text: The mountains hide him. Nothing hides from a dragon.

fab_vulture.0005.desc.text:
Lord Rogar Baratheon stands before the Iron Throne today, and I have never seen him so grim — not at the Golden Wedding, not in the council chamber in all his years as Hand, not even when we quarreled and half the realm held its breath.

His brother burns the stormlands. His own blood shows the vulture where to strike. Every raid is a wound to his lands and a mock upon his name, and every lord in the hall knows it.

He does not rage. He asks, simply and correctly, as a leal bannerman must: the king's leave to take up arms, cross into the mountains, and put an end to the Vulture King and every man who rides with him.

He shall have more than that. The Shivers taught me what my crown weighs; I did not wear it to watch my lords fight my wars from a cushioned seat. Vermithor is saddled. The vulture will learn what wings truly are.

fab_vulture.0005.desc.norogar.text:
The Lord of Storm's End stands before the Iron Throne today, come on behalf of a bleeding house. The vulture's raiders burn the stormlands, and Ser Borys Baratheon — blood of Storm's End itself — shows them where to strike. Every raid is a wound to their lands and a mock upon their name.

The stormlords ask, simply and correctly, as leal bannermen must: the king's leave to take up arms, cross into the mountains, and put an end to the Vulture King and every man who rides with him.

They shall have more than that. The Shivers taught me what my crown weighs; I did not wear it to watch my lords fight my wars from a cushioned seat. Vermithor is saddled. The vulture will learn what wings truly are.

fab_vulture.0005.a.text: You shall have not my leave alone, my lord. You shall have my sword.

fab_vulture.0006.desc.text:
The Red Mountains earn their name at dawn. From Vermithor's back they roll away beneath me like a frozen sea of rust and blood, ridge after ridge after ridge, and I begin to understand how a man might hide an army in them for a lifetime.

But every camp needs fire, and fire needs smoke, and smoke rises.

We fly the passes in long sweeps, the Bronze Fury and I, from the Wyl's headwaters to the peaks above Kingsgrave. Lord Rogar's column is on the march below, east of the mountains, ahorse where the tracks allow and afoot where they do not. Lord Simon Dondarrion leads his marcher knights up from Blackhaven to stopper the western passes. The fist closes on the ground.

And from the sky, I find the camps.

fab_vulture.0007.t.text: The Burning of the High Camps

fab_vulture.0007.desc.text:
The first camp was a scatter of tents and stolen wagons in a hanging valley, crude as a crow's nest. Vermithor took it in a single pass.

Since then we have burned a dozen more. Palisades of mountain pine, caves with their mouths walled in rubble, a shepherd's village the raiders had taken for their own — dragonflame does not care how high a man climbs or how deep he digs. Each time, the survivors scatter upward, to some higher, colder, hungrier refuge, and each time the smoke betrays them again within days.

The smallfolk called him the king the mountains hide. Now they can look up and see the mountains burning, lair by lair, and say who keeps whom.

The vulture has stopped raiding. He is running.

fab_vulture.0007.a.text: Wings, brigand. You chose the wrong sigil.

fab_vulture.0008.desc.text:
The ground closes like a fist.

Lord Rogar's stormlanders came into the mountains from the east — ahorse at first, then afoot when the tracks narrowed to goat paths, hauling their spears up slopes where a laden man must climb with both hands. His men grumble that the Lord of Storm's End sets a pace no goat would suffer; they follow him all the same, higher every day.

To the west, Lord Simon Dondarrion of Blackhaven has done quieter, colder work: a small host of marcher knights strung across every western pass worth the name. The marchers have hunted Dornish raiders through these mountains for generations — they know the bolt-holes, and now they hold them. There will be no slipping away toward the sands.

East, steel. West, steel. Above, fire. The vulture's sky is closing.

fab_vulture.0009.desc.text:
Ser Borys was the first to be run to ground.

Cornered in a high defile with the last of his sworn men, he made his stand. Rogar's stormlanders made short work of them — and then the press parted, and there they stood at last, brother facing brother across ten feet of bloody scree. I saw Rogar's hand on his sword. I saw what it cost him. Whatever else Borys has made of himself, they shared a mother's lap once.

No. Not that. The Seven curse the kinslayer above all men, and Rogar Baratheon has served the Iron Throne too well to be damned for its sake.

I stepped between them and drew Blackfyre. Aegon's sword, for a traitor's justice — Borys sneered and hefted his blade, and named it an honor to die on Valyrian steel.

It is the only honor left to him.

fab_vulture.0009.a.text: Your quarrel is with the crown, ser. Come claim it.

fab_vulture.0009.b.tt.text: Ser Borys Baratheon will not leave this defile alive — by the king's blade, or, should the traitor somehow prevail, cut down by the stormlanders around him. The fight resolves on the morrow.

fab_vulture.0011.desc.text:
It was not a long fight.

He came at me hard, all bitterness and Baratheon strength, and for three exchanges he was very good. But anger is a poor swordmaster, and Blackfyre is a better one. The fourth exchange, I found the gap between gorget and pauldron, and Ser Borys Baratheon went to his knees on the stones of the mountains he had betrayed his house to haunt.

Rogar did not look away. When it was done he knelt beside his brother and closed his eyes, and said no word, and no man in that defile was fool enough to speak to him.

Such are the wages of treason. I take no joy in it. But every lord in my realm has now seen what the king's justice looks like when the king must carry it himself — and that a Baratheon's hands are clean of a brother's blood.

fab_vulture.0011.a.text: Rest now, ser. Your war is over.

fab_vulture.0012.desc.text:
The histories will be kind, because the histories are mine to keep. The truth is that Ser Borys was better than I allowed for, and strong as a bull besides, and there is a dint in my breastplate and a ringing in my skull to prove it. He put me on one knee in the scree, and for a heartbeat his blade was rising over me.

Only a heartbeat. He had beaten his king, and it bought him three steps of mountain air. Then the stormlanders closed over him — his own countrymen, men whose villages he had marked for the vulture's torches — and no royal command on earth would have held them back. He died on a dozen spears, still snarling.

Rogar pulled me to my feet himself. Neither of us spoke of what we had both seen. A king may stumble; it is the crown that must not fall.

The traitor is dead. That is what the ravens will carry.

fab_vulture.0012.a.text: See him buried. He was a knight once.

fab_vulture.0013.desc.text:
In the end, the mountains gave him up.

With his camps in ashes and his bands scattered, the Vulture King fled to the one refuge he judged we would never search: a lair Vermithor had already burned, high on a shoulder of bare rock, where his men could huddle among the char and trust that lightning does not strike twice. It was a clever thought. It kept him free for half a month.

But Lord Dondarrion's trackers found the carrion birds circling — fitting, that — and Rogar's men went up the goat tracks in the dark. There was a brief red business among the burned tents, and then it was over.

They led him before us in chains this morning. I confess I had expected more: a giant, a terror, some black legend of the heights. He is only a man — lean and hawk-faced and hard as the rocks that bred him, with a vulture's patience in his eyes. No name, even now. He offers none and his men know none.

A man crowned him. It remains to be seen what unmakes him.

fab_vulture.0013.a.text: So this is the king the mountains hid.

fab_vulture.0014.desc.text:
I had thought to hang him. Rogar Baratheon has other ideas, and after all this war has cost his house, I find I cannot refuse him.

'Strike off his chains,' he commands, before the assembled host. 'Give him a spear and a shield.' And then, to the vulture himself: 'You called yourself a king. Die like one, then. Kill me, and these men will let you walk free into your mountains — my word on it. My word is good.'

A murmur runs through the ranks. The brigand flexes his freed hands, takes the spear, tests its weight. He looks at the mountains once — his mountains, burned — and then at the Lord of Storm's End, and he smiles like a man who has already died once and found it no great matter.

Rogar means to finish this war the way it was fought: himself, in front, at push of spear. The gods love nothing better than a lord's word wagered on a single fight.

fab_vulture.0014.desc.norogar.text:
The stormlords had thought to hang him. The marcher knights have other ideas, and after all this war has cost the marches, no one gainsays them.

The chains are struck off before the assembled host. A spear and a shield are put into the brigand's hands: he called himself a king — let him die fighting like one, then, against a champion of the men whose lands he burned. He flexes his freed hands, takes the spear, tests its weight. He looks at the mountains once — his mountains, burned — and smiles like a man who has already died once and found it no great matter.

The gods love nothing better than justice wagered on a single fight.

fab_vulture.0014.b.text: Watch from the dais. This is Rogar's fight.

fab_vulture.0014.b.tt.text: The Vulture King will not leave this camp alive — on the stormlord's spear, or, should the brigand somehow prevail and be granted his promised freedom, brought down by Lord Dondarrion's marcher knights in the western passes, who promised him nothing. The fight resolves on the morrow.

fab_vulture.0016.desc.text:
The brigand fought well — I will grant him that much, and nothing more.

He fought like the mountains fight: patient, mean, giving no inch that was not paid for. Twice his spear glanced from Rogar's shield hard enough to stagger him, and the host drew breath as one man. But Rogar Baratheon has broken bigger men than mountain kings, and there is a fury in him this war has fed to fullness. He drove the vulture back, and back again, and when the brigand's foot found loose scree at last, the stormlord's spear went through him and out the other side.

No last words. He died as namelessly as he had lived, and the men who followed him watched it happen and understood, all at once and forever, that there had never been any king in the Red Mountains at all.

Only a man. And men die.

fab_vulture.0016.a.text: It is done. The marches are quiet.

fab_vulture.0017.t.text: A Lord's Word, A Marcher's Arrow

fab_vulture.0017.desc.text:
The gods were not listening, or perhaps they were: the vulture fought like a starved animal, and when Rogar's foot turned on the scree it was the stormlord who went down, bloodied, his shield split to the boss. The brigand stood over the Lord of Storm's End with his spear raised — and then, gods know why, lowered it, spat, and turned for the mountains.

And Rogar Baratheon, bleeding on the ground, roared at his own men to stand aside. His word was given. His word is good. The host parted, and the Vulture King walked free through a thousand of his enemies, upright as any king in truth.

He walked west. It was the only way open, and it was open because Lord Simon Dondarrion held it — and the marchers, as every man in the mountains knew save one, had promised him nothing at all. They say he was smiling when the arrows found him, high in the western passes, within sight of the sands he never reached.

Rogar will mend. His word stands unbroken. And the vulture is carrion at last.

fab_vulture.0017.a.text: His word stands. And the vulture is carrion.

fab_vulture.0018.desc.text:
From the first raven to the last spear, the whole affair lasted not even half a year.

The maesters are already quarreling over what to call it. The Third Dornish War, some write, and the court at Sunspear bristles at the name — no banner of Dorne ever flew beside the vulture's, they protest, and that is true. But he was Dornish, and his mountains were Dornish, and the histories need their tidy numbers. They can have it. Those who fought there call it the Vulture Hunt, and that name is truer.

The camps are ash. The bands are broken and scattered, hunted now by Dornish lords as eagerly as by my marchers — carrion draws no borders. Ser Borys has answered for his treason, and Storm's End's honor is whole: no kinslaying stains it, and every man from the Dornish marches to the Wall knows that when the vulture rose, the old stag of Storm's End went up the goat tracks on foot, and the King of Westeros flew before him.

My realm has seen its king make war beside his lords, not above them. After the Shivers, after everything — that is worth more than the winning.

The mountains can keep their carrion. We are going home.

fab_vulture.0018.a.text: Not even half a year. Write it so in the histories.

fab_vulture_duel_modifier_desc.text: This fight was a long time coming, and it will not be a long fight.

fab_third_dornish_plot_armor_modifier_de.text: The chronicles have already written this one's ending, and it is not here.

trait_typhus_desc.text: What began as a chill now grips this character in constant shaking, bloodied coughs, and blue lips.

trait_typhus_character_desc.text: [ROOT.GetCharacter.GetFirstNameNoTooltip] shakes violently, coughing up blood while [ROOT.GetCharacter.GetHerHis] lips turn blue.
